detail.abstract: This document is a draft version of Chapter 1 from Digital Dispute System Design: Using Technology in Preventing and Resolving Conflict, authored by Amy J. Schmitz and Janet Martinez and published by Aspen in 2025. The final, updated version of this chapter appears in the published book. This chapter introduces foundational considerations for integrating technology into dispute system design. It explores the evolving duty of technological competence for legal and dispute resolution professionals, tracing its development in the United States and internationally. The discussion highlights how emerging technologies—such as generative AI, online platforms, and advanced communication tools—are reshaping legal practice and conflict resolution. By examining ethical implications, access-to-justice concerns, and the role of technology as a “fourth party,” the chapter sets the stage for understanding how digital tools can both create and resolve disputes. This draft provides an early framework for thinking about technology’s impact on dispute prevention and resolution, emphasizing flexibility and continuous learning in system design.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Emotional Framing in Political Media
affiliations: United World College South East Asia

detail.title: Sentiment Analysis of Emotional Framing in Political Media
detail.abstract: Affective polarization, a persistent challenge in today's democracy, often overshadows the subtle yet profound influence of emotional rhetoric in shaping public opinion and reinforcing partisan divides. This research delves into the critical role of emotional framing in exacerbating this polarization within the U.S. media landscape, particularly across election cycles. This research trials a novel natural language processing algorithm, to measure and classify the emotional intensity of news content. This study, encompassing a vast collection of articles sourced from MediaCloud's sorted collections, uncovers significant variations in media's emotional intensity. We observed distinct partisan strategies in how emotional language is deployed, patterns that strikingly align with established theories of political psychology. Furthermore, our findings challenge the common assumption that emotional rhetoric intensity is confined to election seasons, revealing that such framing is deeply embedded in today's information-systems.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the concept of New Integrity as an epistemic anchor in times of semantic simulation, institutional drift, and accountability vacuums. Rather than proposing ethical theories or policy corrections, it redefines responsibility as a structural force – not a moral choice.

Operating outside conventional review mechanisms, New Integrity offers an audit-based framework to identify where normative validity collapses and systemic simulation prevails. The text functions not as argument but as carrier architecture – semantically accessible, yet structurally resistant to co-optation.

It invites scholars across law, philosophy, AI governance, and institutional theory to rethink legitimacy in a world where presence is often replaced by interface. The paper is part of the Orto-9 Series (Audit-Based Epistemic Resonance Architecture) and was first deposited on Zenodo under an open license to maintain audit traceability.

title: The Science of Large Language Models
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Science of Large Language Models
detail.abstract: In the last few years there have been significant achievements and breakthroughs in large language models (LLMs). They have been integrated into various technologies and tools, such as search engines, chatbots, coding assistants, etc. These technologies are used by millions of users around the world. As a new key component of nowadays technology, it is important to study these gigantic computational models more deeply and from different aspects. In this article, we promote the idea of defining a science for large language models. We highlight key aspects of large language models that should be studied in this specific branch of science. Some important dimensions include the limitations and shortcomings of LLMs, benchmarking and evaluation of LLMs, scaling laws in LLMs, physic of language models, biology of language models, physiology of language models, mathematics of language models, societal impacts of LLM-based AI technologies, etc.

detail.abstract: Arbitration has been moving online for some time, especially with the growth of Online Dispute Resolution ("ODR"), which includes using technology to assist online negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and variations thereof. Online Arbitration ("OArb") is nonetheless a unique subset of ODR because it usually culminates in a final and binding award by a neutral third party that is enforceable under the Federal Arbitration Act ("FAA") and other arbitration laws. Indeed, I have written about OArb on prior occasions, due to its unique status. However, OArb became a norm during the COVID-19 pandemic, although some are moving back to in person since that time. Nonetheless, OArb can lower barriers and costs of arbitration for many and protocols remain important for ensuring fair and appropriate use of remote hearings.

title: How Data Shapes Competition on Digital Platforms: Consumer Welfare and Firm Risk
affiliations: University of Utah - David Eccles School of Business

detail.title: How Data Shapes Competition on Digital Platforms: Consumer Welfare and Firm Risk
detail.abstract: This paper studies how a digital platform's data shapes competition, welfare, and firm behavior. Using Amazon data, I construct a novel measure to capture the platform's informational advantage, Data Power Index (DPI). Firms in high-DPI categories see lower revenue and sales, higher cash and short-term investments, and younger innovation, consistent with tighter information-based competition. Importantly, DPI, but not traditional HHI, predicts Amazon private-brand entry. After Amazon's entry, prices fall and third-party revenues and margins decline, while exposed firms face higher risk. Consumer surplus rises while sellers' contributions to consumer surplus fall, highlighting welfare redistribution and efficiency trade-off with policy-relevant consequences.

title: Architecture of Cognitive Usurpation: Engineering and Systemic Foundations of the Crisis of Collective Reason
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Architecture of Cognitive Usurpation: Engineering and Systemic Foundations of the Crisis of Collective Reason

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was conducted independently by the author without external funding or institutional affiliation. The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animal subjects, and therefore did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Cognitive usurpation is the process by which technological, institutional, or algorithmic infrastructures capture and subordinate the mechanisms of knowledge formation, distribution, and verification. The result is a systemic reduction of collective epistemic autonomy and a concentration of semantic and trust management within a narrow center of decision-making. Unlike surveillance capitalism (Zuboff, 2019), epistemic capture (Christiano, 2022), or algorithmic authority (Shirky, 2009), cognitive usurpation operates at the meta-level: it denotes the capture not only of data or institutions, but of the very processes by which knowledge and truth are produced and validated. This paper treats cognitive usurpation as an architectural pattern of digital civilization-not as a moral deviation, but as a systemic feature of information infrastructures optimized for attention rather than truth. It develops an analytical framework for understanding the crisis of collective reason and formulates engineering principles for building resilient, human-centered epistemic ecosystems. This paper constitutes the first installment in a four-part research series on the systemic architectures of collective cognition. The forthcoming works will address the following dimensions: (2) Cognitive-Executive Operating System (CE-OS)-Epistemo-Ontological Graph (CAG v2); (3) Ethical Charter of Cognitive Singularity (v1.0); and (4) The Contour of Cognitive Civilization-A Framework for Reflexive Epistemic Systems.

title: Analysis of Biometrics in Intellectual Property in an AI Driven World
affiliations: PES University

detail.title: Analysis of Biometrics in Intellectual Property in an AI Driven World
detail.abstract: The meeting of Biometrics data and Artificial intelligence is transforming the realm of intellectual property. Biometric data is a collection which captures distinctive physical features of individuals such as fingerprints, face, voice and so on. Biometric systems use artificial intelligence to analyse this data for the processes of identification and verification. While the use of biometrics have simplified the work of Government organizations and Businesses, they also pose various challenges and threats with respect to privacy. In this era, the application of biometrics is widespread, hence it is crucial to consider how safe is it to put our personal and sensitive data in the hands of artificial intelligence. The balance between intellectual property and data privacy can fix these challenges.

title: AI in Criminal Sentencing: A Framework for Transparency and Bias Detection

detail.title: AI in Criminal Sentencing: A Framework for Transparency and Bias Detection
detail.abstract: The persistent issue of sentencing disparities based on demographic factors represents a fundamental failure of the principle of equal justice. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel framework for the use of artificial intelligence in criminal sentencing-not as an automated decision-maker, but as a powerful tool for transparency and bias detection. We introduce the AI Jury System, a multi-agent architecture designed to provide a rigorously validated, bias-mitigated, and transparently reasoned baseline recommendation for judicial review. The system is composed of a diverse panel of AI "jurors," each trained on a unique legal and philosophical framework, which must reach a consensus before presenting a recommendation. This process is protected by a "manipulation for good" protocol that ensures system integrity through continuous crossvalidation and anomaly detection, inspired by the principle of Byzantine Fault Tolerance. Furthermore, we propose a methodology for encoding deep institutional knowledge into the AI, moving beyond a purely textual analysis of law to a form of practical wisdom. This paper provides the complete architectural blueprint for the AI Jury System and argues that by systematically exposing and correcting for the biases inherent in humanled sentencing, this framework can help transform the concept of "equal justice under the law" from an ideal into a measurable, achievable standard.

title: Liquidity and the Breakdown of Risk-Neutral Pricing in a Merton Credit Model
affiliations: Texas Tech University

detail.title: Liquidity and the Breakdown of Risk-Neutral Pricing in a Merton Credit Model
detail.abstract: This study shows that liquidity-based private information can undermine risk-neutral pricing in a Merton credit-risk framework. When informed traders observe order-flow volume that predicts terminal firm value, the discounted equity price acquires a predictable drift. As signal precision increases, Novikov’s condition fails and no equivalent martingale measure exists. The result links empirical evidence on liquidity-driven credit spread mispricing to the theoretical breakdown of risk-neutral valuation, highlighting how asymmetric information embedded in trading volume endogenously generates arbitrage opportunities.

title: What Exactly is a Deepfake?
affiliations: University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business, University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business and Robert H. Smith School of Business

detail.title: What Exactly is a Deepfake?
detail.abstract: Deepfake technologies are predominantly associated with deception, misinformation, and identity fraud, raising significant societal concerns. While these concerns are warranted, they may obscure an insight: deepfakes represent sophisticated capabilities for sensory manipulation that could alter human perceptions, thereby, perhaps counterintuitively, enabling some beneficial applications across various areas, such as healthcare and education. However, realizing this potential requires first understanding how the technology is conceptualized across different fields. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of 826 peer-reviewed publications from 2017 to 2025, systematically examining how deepfakes are defined and understood in the literature. Using advanced large language models for content analysis, we extract and categorize deepfake conceptualizations along three key dimensions: Identity Source (the relationship between original and generated content), Intent (deceptive versus non-deceptive purposes), and Manipulation Granularity (holistic versus targeted modifications). Our analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity in deepfake conceptualizations that challenges simplified public narratives. In particular, we identify a subset of papers discussing the potential of deepfake approaches for non-deceptive intent, which has substantial yet underexplored potential for broader beneficial applications. Additionally, the temporal analysis reveals an evolution from predominantly threat-focused conceptualizations in early years (2017-2019) toward some recognition of beneficial applications in recent publications (2022-2025). This comprehensive analysis provides an empirical foundation for developing beneficial research and nuanced governance frameworks that can distinguish between applications that deserve prohibition and those that merit support and development. It suggests that, with appropriate safeguards, deepfake technology's realism can even serve important social purposes beyond its controversial origins.

title: AI Spillover is Different: Flat and Lean Firms as Engines of AI Diffusion and Productivity Gain
affiliations: University of Texas at Dallas, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

detail.title: AI Spillover is Different: Flat and Lean Firms as Engines of AI Diffusion and Productivity Gain
detail.abstract: Labor mobility is a critical source of technology acquisition for firms. This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) knowledge is disseminated across firms through labor mobility and identifies the organizational conditions that facilitate productive spillovers. Using a comprehensive dataset of over 460 million job records from Revelio Labs (2010-2023), we construct an inter-firm mobility network of AI workers among over 16,000 U.S. companies. Estimating a Cobb-Douglas production function, we find that firms benefit substantially from the AI investments of other firms from which they hire AI talents, with productivity spillovers two to three times larger than those associated with traditional IT after accounting for labor scale. Importantly, these spillovers are contingent on organizational context: hiring from flatter and more lean-startup-method-intensive firms generates significant productivity gains, whereas hiring from firms lacking these traits yields little benefit. Mechanism tests indicate that "flat and lean" organizations cultivate more versatile AI generalists who transfer richer knowledge across firms. These findings reveal that AI spillovers differ fundamentally from traditional IT spillovers: while IT spillovers primarily arise from scale and process standardization, AI spillovers critically depend on the experimental and integrative environments in which AI knowledge is produced. Together, these results underscore the importance of considering both labor mobility and organizational context in understanding the full impact of AI-driven productivity spillovers.

title: Africa's AI Future: Creating Half-Billion Opportunities Through Tech-Enabled Exports
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Africa's AI Future: Creating Half-Billion Opportunities Through Tech-Enabled Exports

declarations.ethicsApproval: This work was not based on patient or participant data nor on case studies.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not supported by external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper argues for a fundamental reset of AI strategy in Africa. With manufacturing's labor absorption waning, African economies must generate hundreds of millions of decent jobs. We advocate an AI strategy built for that mandate-one that extends a services-led industrial policy anchored in existing specializations and export potential-rather than diffuse, supply-side initiatives (compute buildouts, generic upskilling, blanket regulation) pursued without a clear line-of-sight to growth and employment. We document five stylized facts relevant to many African economies: services absorb most net labor; modern, digitally tradable services are expanding globally; AI deployment costs are falling even as frontier training costs rise; enabling infrastructure is spreading on the contient (if unevenly); and early evidence suggests AI technologies can raise services tradability and augment lower-skilled workers. Building on these facts, we propose a data-driven workflow that matches countries' AI activity to goods and service sectors with the highest probability of export growth over a 2-5-year horizon (a "progression network"), paired with an AI scoreboard that maps bottlenecks and assets across the AI value chain. A brief Nigeria case study illustrates how AI capabilities can reinforce current service strengths and open adjacent export opportunities. We conclude with a measurement agenda-the "African AI & Jobs Index"-to track deployment, exports, and labormarket outcomes. The approach re-frames comparative advantage for the AI era and offers a practical playbook for export-led, job-rich growth in Africa.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper Series

detail.abstract: This document contains chapters 2 and 3 of the author's dissertation. In the second chapter, I estimate the demand for cigarette and e-cigarette products using the BLP Random Coefficients demand estimator. The estimated set of elasticities reveals limited substitution both between cigarette and e-cigarette products and within product categories themselves — a finding that calls into question a longstanding notion that traditional cigarette users can be easily incentivized to switch to e-cigarettes. In the third chapter, I use the demand estimates from the second essay to simulate hypothetical counterfactuals. Among these counterfactuals, I explore the impacts of e-cigarette taxes as well as the impacts of acquisitions of e-cigarette brands by traditional cigarette companies. For the taxation counterfactuals, I estimate that a flat e-cigarette tax of $1 would generate between $52 million and $131 million ingovernment revenue per annum. In subsequent analysis, I find that if policymakers wished to maximize government revenue, a flat tax of $0.60 would push this range to $70 to $170 million per annum.

title: AI Adoption, Market Outcomes, and Coordination Risks
affiliations: Vassar College - Department of Economics, Oklahoma State University - Economics and University of Oklahoma

detail.title: AI Adoption, Market Outcomes, and Coordination Risks
detail.abstract: In this paper, we examine the impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in the U.S. airline industry, focusing on pricing, service quality, environmental externalities, and consumer welfare. We find that enterprise AI adoption improves on-time performance and local air quality while raising average fares and compressing price dispersion. For generative AI-enhanced pricing tools, the price effects of adoption are larger and span the fare distribution, but their magnitude and direction depend on how the technology is adopted. In particular, when rivals rely on the same algorithm vendor, price increases are muted or even reversed, whereas broader diffusion of AI pricing tools is associated with higher fares and reduced dispersion. Our findings point to a key trade-off in the adoption of AI technologies: while AI can enhance operational efficiency, widespread adoption in concentrated markets may raise coordination risks.

detail.title: The Local Employer Advantage: Consumer Preferences and Product Market Outcomes

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper No. 3-843
publicationDetails.journalName: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper Series

detail.abstract: We investigate how consumer preferences for goods by local employers affect retail demand and pricing. Using barcode-level scanner data, we document consumers' employment-based preferences: firms sell 2.7% more and charge up to 2.2% higher prices in counties where they employ workers. Exploiting establishment closures, takeover-induced ownership changes, and employment protection regulation changes, we identify demand effects linked to local employment provision. Moreover, exploiting exogenous shocks to supply-side incentives following the GFC and PE buyouts, we document pricing effects linked to financial and short-term performance pressures. Our findings highlight how firms exploit geographic heterogeneity in consumer preferences to extract consumer surplus.

title: Mastering the First 3 Seconds in Marketing: Lessons from The 23 Laws of Marketing: Master Them or Die

detail.title: Mastering the First 3 Seconds in Marketing: Lessons from The 23 Laws of Marketing: Master Them or Die

keywords: The 23 Laws of Marketing Master Them or Die

detail.abstract: Attention is now decided in 3 seconds. This paper operationalizes "Law 22 - Master The First Three Seconds," arguing that market survival depends on pattern disruption, instant identity resonance, and high emotional voltage. Drawing on the orienting response in neuroscience and classic judgement/decision research, we outline a practical framework for crafting openings that hijack attention before skepticism forms. A brief case analysis of the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge shows how immediate novelty and social identity cues produced outsized engagement and fundraising. We conclude with a checklist marketers can deploy across ads, landing pages, and social video to increase hook-through and conversions in the first three seconds.

title: Reassessing American Democracy: A Conceptual Analysis of Authoritarian Patterns in Donald Trump's Second Term
affiliations: Avant-Garde Research Institute

detail.title: Reassessing American Democracy: A Conceptual Analysis of Authoritarian Patterns in Donald Trump's Second Term
detail.abstract: This conceptual analysis reassesses the state of American democracy by examining the authoritarian patterns characterizing Donald Trump's second term. The study employs a three-variable conceptual model, identifying illiberalism as the independent driver and the rise of authoritarianism as the dependent outcome, with Stacey Abrams' "10 Steps to Autocracy" serving as the mediating pathway. This framework is complemented by the theoretical lens of the authoritarian personality by Adorno et al. (1950) to understand the psychological underpinnings of the political base. The study argues that Trump's presidency represents a deliberate illiberal political project that is systematically dismantling democratic guardrails through the aggressive expansion of executive power, complicity from Congress, and the active undermining of an independent judiciary. The administration is politicizing state institutions by purging the professional civil service and installing loyalists, thereby weaponizing the government against political opponents. Concurrently, strategies to control communication and undermine the free press are distorting the facts, while anti-pluralist and nativist rhetoric fosters social division. These actions, facilitated by partisan media echo chambers and widespread political capitulation, are accelerating democratic deconsolidation. The ongoing tenure serves as a critical case study in democratic resilience, testing whether core institutions can withstand sustained pressure from within.

title: Corporate political strategies in M&As: a systematic review of trajectories, impacts and managerial influence
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Shillong, Indian Institute of Management Shillong and Indian Institute of Management Shillong

detail.title: Corporate political strategies in M&As: a systematic review of trajectories, impacts and managerial influence

keywords: Systematic review Paper type Literature review

detail.abstract: Purpose-This study examines the impact of corporate political strategies (CPS) on mergers and acquisitions (M&A) outcomes, emphasizing their evolution, trends, and managerial influences. It investigates how CPS drives firm expansion, technological acquisition, and revenue growth while assessing top management's role in selecting and implementing these strategies. This understanding is vital for refining corporate strategies that balance market and nonmarket forces. Design/methodology/approach-This study employs a systematic literature review methodology using the Context-Intervention-Mechanism-Outcome (CIMO) framework. By synthesizing findings from academic sources, the review maps CPS's evolution, managerial influences, and effectiveness in shaping M&A outcomes across global markets. Findings-The review finds that CPS positively impacts M&A outcomes by easing regulatory approvals and improving post-acquisition performance. However, its effectiveness depends on factors like legal frameworks and ownership structures. Risks include prolonged deal reviews and over-reliance on political connections, leading to suboptimal decisions and reputational damage. Managerial behaviors significantly influence CPS success, and strategies have become more adaptive. Future trends point to increasing use of predictive technologies to manage risks in M&A. Originality/value-This study systematically reviews the evolving role of CPS in M&A transactions, incorporating managerial behavior and institutional context. Integrating the CIMO framework and examining the interplay between CPS and managerial traits, it offers a novel perspective on how firms strategize within political environments during M&A.

title: The Power of Choice in Random Sampling

detail.title: The Power of Choice in Random Sampling

declarations.funderStatement: Supported in part by a Simons Investigator Award, a Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship, the Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR grant FA9550-19-1-0183), a Simons Collaboration grant, and a grant from the John. D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Choice Random Walk (CRW), a generalization of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) in which the sampler receives a set of k candidate moves and selects among them according to an optimizable policy. This formulation casts sampling as a convex optimization problem over transition policies, enabling systematic improvement of key metrics such as the average acceptance rate, the mixing time, and a differentiable relaxation of maximum congestion. CRW provides a scalable computational tool for stochastic programming and simulation-based optimization, enhancing efficiency in generating representative or rare-event scenarios. Experiments on real-world networks demonstrate gains in sampling performance.

As such, ethical approval and informed consent were not required. The research has adhered to all standard ethical guidelines for secondary data analysis, including proper citation, data integrity, and compliance with relevant copyright and data usage policies.
declarations.funderStatement: self

detail.abstract: This study looked at the combined impact of governmental administration, economic services, and social service spending on GDP growth in Nigeria from 1981 and 2023, taking exchange and inflation into consideration. The study used annual time-series data and autoregressive econometric techniques. The model's overall statistical significance (p < 0.01) indicates that the independent variables have a combined impact on GDP growth. Individual sector spending on public administration (p = 0.91), social services (p = 0.95), and economic services (p = 0.69) did not. The limited effectiveness of fiscal spending in the face of macroeconomic uncertainty is shown by the negative but statistically insignificant effects of inflation and exchange rate volatility (p = 0.17 and p = 0.92). Diagnostic tests were used to verify the model's resilience. The Breusch-Pagan-Godfrey test revealed no heteroskedasticity (p = 0.11), however the Breusch-Godfrey LM test revealed a small autocorrelation (p = 0.05). The results were more credible because the variance inflation components did not exhibit multicollinearity. Complementary SWOT and PESTEL analyses uncovered internal weaknesses including fiscal inefficiencies and inconsistent policies, in addition to external risks like oil price shocks and market volatility. The analysis concludes that the country has been unable to produce sustainable growth due to inefficiency and a weak institutional structure. It recommends that expenditures be tightly matched with sectors that boost productivity, executed by ethical companies, and publicly tracked.

title: Data collection on housing conditions in ageing cohort studies: a meta-research study
affiliations: The University of Sydney - Concord Clinical School, The University of Sydney, The University of Sydney - School of Public Health, The University of Newcastle - School of Medicine and Public Health, The University of Sydney, University of New South Wales (UNSW), The University of Sydney and The University of Sydney - Concord Clinical School

detail.title: Data collection on housing conditions in ageing cohort studies: a meta-research study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Objectives: To identify the availability and describe measurement methods of housing conditions in ageing cohort studies across Oceania, and to highlight data and measurement gaps.

Methods: For this meta-research study, ageing cohort studies in Oceania were identified using an online cohort repository, which includes ageing cohort studies across the globe (search finalized January 2022), along with an updated PubMed search (to October 2024). Availability and measurement methods for sixteen subdomains of housing conditions were considered across four main domains of internal housing conditions, neighbourhood/outdoor environment, perceived housing conditions, and other (tenure, affordability, stability, location).

Results: Of 25 ageing cohort studies identified, 21 were from Australia and four from New Zealand; none were from other Oceanic countries. All included studies captured at least one housing-related measure—most commonly in the subdomains of housing/dwelling type, housing profile, or housing tenure. Other housing conditions subdomains were often overlooked, with only 4% to 24% of included studies assessing housing design, facilities, problems, transportation, satisfaction, safety perception, location, and affordability, while no studies measured housing quality or perceived control and autonomy.

Conclusions: This study highlights the lack of comprehensive housing measures in ageing cohort studies in Australia and New Zealand, limiting our understanding of how housing conditions impact health and well-being of older adults. It is therefore crucial to integrate standardized and comprehensive housing measures into cohort studies, particularly in the context of population ageing and climate change. The absence of cohort studies from other countries in Oceania also highlights a significant data equity issue.

title: Juggling Red Tape: The Effects of Regulatory Fragmentation on Takeover Targets
affiliations: Fordham University  , Xiamen University - School of Economics and Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE)

detail.title: Juggling Red Tape: The Effects of Regulatory Fragmentation on Takeover Targets
detail.abstract: This paper explores the dual role of regulatory fragmentation in the high-stakes domain of mergers and acquisitions (M&A). We find that regulatory fragmentation acts as a deterrent, significantly reducing a firm's likelihood of being acquired by introducing information uncertainty that impedes valuation and imposing coordination costs that erode profitability. Paradoxically, this regulatory gauntlet also functions as an effective screening mechanism. For deals that successfully navigate these hurdles, target firm announcement returns increase, especially in acquisitions with high synergy potential, suggesting that only strategically superior transactions prevail. Ultimately, our findings highlight that the structure of regulation, rather than its sheer volume, plays a crucial role in both dampening M&A activity and enhancing deal quality, offering a new perspective on the corporate control market.

title: Colonial Logics in the Mobilization Mechanics of Climate Disinformation

detail.title: Colonial Logics in the Mobilization Mechanics of Climate Disinformation
detail.abstract: Climate disinformation is not an incidental byproduct of the digital age but the latest expression of colonial logics of mediated authority. This study argues that the mechanics through which climate denial and distortion circulate across the Global South cannot be understood apart from the infrastructures of British indirect rule, which historically governed ‘through’ intermediaries rather than ‘over’ subjects. Drawing on the Model of Indirect Epistemic Domination, the research demonstrates how recruitment, localization, deflection, normalization, and exploitation, once deployed to entrench imperial power, are today reactivated in digital and spiritual ecosystems, where religious, cultural, and viral social influencers legitimize climate falsehoods as indigenous truths. The study analyzes 200 purposively sampled disinformation posts from Facebook, X, and YouTube across eleven African states (January–June 2025) alongside structural indices of religiosity, trust in science, education, and media access. Multi-scalar analysis reveals that religiosity strongly amplifies susceptibility (r ≈ 0.83), while media access functions as a double-edged vector, broadening reach but intensifying exposure. Regression modeling confirms that susceptibility is not merely informational but structurally conditioned, with colonial residues shaping epistemic ecologies. By revealing the genealogical continuity between colonial governance and climate disinformation, the study reframes the crisis as both epistemological and environmental, calling for climate communication strategies that confront inherited structures of authority, epistemic power, and belief.

detail.title: Managing decarbonization in global value chains: Decision-making and operational resilience in Finnish manufacturing MNEs

declarations.funderStatement: Rudolf Sinkovics gratefully acknowledges financial support from the BA/Leverhulme Small Research Grants, UK [grant number SRG2223\231623].

detail.abstract: Decarbonization is a pressing issue that must be embedded in business strategies, as excessive carbon emissions accelerate extreme weather events, deplete ecosystems, and exacerbate the biodiversity crisis. The rapidly evolving regulatory landscape, including stringent European mandates, underscores the need for adaptable strategies to mitigate environmental impacts while enhancing resilience in global value chains. Despite the significant emissions they generate, the decision-making processes that enable managers to achieve decarbonization in global value chains are poorly understood. This gap is significant, as businesses face mounting pressures to align with new regulations and foster resilience. To address this, we conducted an exploratory study with two Finnish machinery manufacturing firms, leveraging in-depth interviews and sustainability reports. By employing the Awareness-Motivation-Capability framework, the study reveals that decision-making is shaped by awareness linked to planning, motivation tied to path dependency, and capability influenced by time, offering insights into decarbonization strategies and operational resilience.

detail.title: Enclosed solar steam generation industrial applications: Overview of world's first commercial-scale hybrid system

publicationDetails.detailsText: Osama A. Marzouk (2025). Enclosed solar steam generation industrial applications: Overview of world’s first commercial-scale hybrid system. Results in Engineering. Volume 28. Article number 108186.

detail.abstract: Enhanced oil recovery (EOR) or tertiary oil recovery (TOR) is a process used in the oil industry to extract remaining crude oil from partially-exploited reservoirs by changing the characteristics of this underground crude oil (particularly for heavy viscous oil grades with an API gravity degree below about 20 •) to improve its mobility. In the current study, we present a case study comprising innovative solar thermal projects in Oman at the Amal West offshore oil field in Concession Block 6 (in the southern Omani governorate of Dhofar, about 640 km south of Muscat). This oil field is fully owned and operated by Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), a leading oil and gas exploration and production company in Oman. In these three projects, glasshouse-enclosed parabolic troughs are used to generate steam for thermal enhanced oil recovery (steam flooding), using solar heat for industrial processes (SHIP). These three enclosed solar enhanced oil recovery (ESEOR) projects are: Amal I pilot project (8 MWth peak capacity), Amal II pilot project (8 MWth), and Miraah flagship project (330 MWth). If combined, these three ESEOR projects can supply annually about 1.992 trillion Btu of heat (1.992 million MMBtu or 19.92 million therms), which is about 2.05 PJ (petajoules) or 570.0 GWh. This is approximately equivalent to 1.992 billion standard cubic feet (Bcf) of natural gas or 56.92 million normal cubic meters (MNm 3) of natural gas. If combined, these three ESEOR projects can produce daily up to 2100 tonnes of steam. The conventional heating method of burning natural gas may release annually more than 100 kilotonnes of carbon dioxide (CO 2). We discuss these EOR projects as examples of successful sustainable practices.

title: Trade Policy and Productivity Growth: Why Do Sudanese Manufacturing Firms Export Less

detail.title: Trade Policy and Productivity Growth: Why Do Sudanese Manufacturing Firms Export Less
detail.abstract: This paper aims to study the role of trade policy on industrial development and productivity growth. We analyze the relationship between trade policy and productivity growth of manufacturing firms in Sudan. For this work, we evaluate the previous trade policy instruments that implemented between 2000 and 2022. The study finds that Sudan's trade policy has significant positive effects on manufacturing firms' productivity. The study reveals that manufacturing firms offer the largest scope for productivity gains through trade policies aiming at enhancing economic growth. The study also found there was a weak support for investment promotion and tariff protection. This study recommends that building a proper trade policy to support manufacturing firms and adopt new technologies and focusing on labor intensive industries are the key success to sustain productivity growth and enable manufacturing firms' export.

title: How Does Patent Protection Affect Venture Capital Investment?
affiliations: , University of Warwick and Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance

detail.title: How Does Patent Protection Affect Venture Capital Investment?
detail.abstract: We study how patent protection affects venture capital (VC) investment in startups by exploiting the Bilski v. Kappos Supreme Court decision, which unexpectedly narrowed patent eligibility. Using variation in industry exposure to the ruling, we find that more exposed industries experienced larger increases in initial VC investment after the decision. The effect reflects a divergence in investment responses: exposure to Bilski is associated with more investment in startups without patents but less investment in startups with pre-Bilski patents. Our findings suggest that weaker patent protection lowers barriers to VC-backed entry and reallocates capital toward startups previously constrained by incumbent patents.

title: The Role of Entrepreneurial Culture in Enabling Transformation and Innovation in Organizations
affiliations: Institute for Change Leadership and Business Transformation

detail.title: The Role of Entrepreneurial Culture in Enabling Transformation and Innovation in Organizations
detail.abstract: This paper examines entrepreneurial culture as a strategic foundation for business transformation. Drawing from management literature and illustrative cases, it argues that culture is not a peripheral support but a structural capability that enables continuous adaptation. Entrepreneurial culture integrates innovation, autonomy, and risk tolerance, fostering both incremental improvements and disruptive opportunities. A conceptual framework is proposed around four interdependent dimensions: entrepreneurial leadership and vision, empowerment of people, adaptive organizational processes, and a sustainability mindset. Together, these dimensions create a cultural system that embeds innovation, strengthens resilience, and aligns transformation with longterm competitiveness and social legitimacy. The discussion highlights practical implications for leaders, including the need to incorporate cultural metrics and experimentation in transformation programs, as well as academic implications for further research on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, resilience, and sustainability.

title: The Paradox of Institutional Reform: Why Scientific Gatekeeping Persists Where Racial Segregation Collapsed
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Paradox of Institutional Reform: Why Scientific Gatekeeping Persists Where Racial Segregation Collapsed
detail.abstract: The parallel between racial segregation in mid-20th century America and contemporary academic gatekeeping is striking—yet the outcomes have diverged dramatically. While the civil rights movement produced transformative institutional reform, the academic publishing crisis has produced no comparable movement despite systematic suppression of innovation, error correction, and theoretical progress. This essay analyzes the structural reasons for this asymmetry. We argue that contemporary academic gatekeeping persists and intensifies precisely because it operates under conditions fundamentally different from racial segregation: (1) the beneficiaries of gatekeeping constitute a massive, organized interest group controlling institutions and resource allocation; (2) entry into this interest group is nominally open, masking the gatekeeping beneath appearance of meritocracy; (3) resistance is atomized and powerless, composed of scattered individuals rather than organized constituencies; (4) the economic incentives sustaining gatekeeping far exceed the potential gains from reform; and (5) alternative platforms lack sufficient institutional legitimacy to compete with entrenched peer review systems. We document how scientific gatekeeping functions as a protected form of institutional corruption—more durable and effective than overt discrimination because it operates through legitimated institutional mechanisms rather than explicit exclusion. The essay concludes that meaningful reform in academic publishing requires not just ethical commitment but the emergence of counter-institutional structures with sufficient resource and credibility to constitute genuine alternatives to peer review gatekeeping.

title: Access to Data for Access to Justice: Unpacking Judicial Congestion Using an Event Log
affiliations: Tel Aviv University - Coller School of Management, , University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Access to Data for Access to Justice: Unpacking Judicial Congestion Using an Event Log
detail.abstract: Courts globally suffer from congestion, which undermines social welfare, economic growth, and access to justice. Despite the criticality of judicial operations, empirical research is scarce due to (a) complexity of court systems, characterized by constrained resources, increasing demand, prolonged waiting times, and cases lasting years, and (b) limited access to comprehensive data. This paper addresses these gaps by mapping the underlying judicial system and its operational dynamics as captured in court records. Methodology: Using advanced natural language processing and machine learning techniques, we standardized 18 years of U.S. Federal District Court case dockets into an event log comprising millions of timestamped entries. The dataset presented in this paper lowers the barrier of access to data by capturing the temporal structure and multi-phase nature of judicial processes, as we demonstrate through preliminary descriptive analyses. The dataset thus facilitates investigations into judicial process modeling and workload patterns, helping to identify systemic bottlenecks and operational dynamics within the courts. Managerial Implications: Our work establishes a robust, data-driven framework that provides descriptive insights into judicial operations. Moreover, it paves the way for further predictive, comparative, and prescriptive research. The dataset offers a foundation for exploring judicial process modeling, optimizing resource allocation, and assessing operational interventions, thereby opening new avenues for evidence-based strategies to alleviate court congestion and enhance access to justice.

title: Cost and Demand Effects of Legal Adult Prostitution on Child Sex Trafficking
affiliations: Otaru University of Commerce, University of Tokyo - Graduate School of Economics, Toyo University and East West University

detail.title: Cost and Demand Effects of Legal Adult Prostitution on Child Sex Trafficking
detail.abstract: We examine the impact of legal adult prostitution on the prevalence of trafficked child sex workers and children engaging in prostitution out of economic necessity. Using a nationwide survey of child sex workers, historically determined locations of legal brothels, and counterfactual simulations, we find that the presence of legal brothels increases the prevalence of trafficked children by 18.8 percent nationwide, primarily because they are camouflaged as legal prostitutes. Rigorous screening procedure within brothels mitigates this increase. However, the inability to exclude non-trafficked children who misreport their age as adults raises their prevalence beyond that of actual brothels, revealing policy tradeoffs.

title: Performing in "Autonomy Theater": Balancing t he Needs of Social Media Researchers with Perspectives of High Profile Figures
affiliations: and George Washington University

detail.title: Performing in "Autonomy Theater": Balancing t he Needs of Social Media Researchers with Perspectives of High Profile Figures

declarations.ethicsApproval: The authors met with the high profile figures over Zoom and recorded each session with express permission from the participants in line with GWU IRB (#NCR234951).
declarations.funderStatement: The Institute for Data, Democracy & Politics (IDDP) launched in 2019 with the support of the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. IDDP's mission is to help the public, journalists and policymakers understand digital media's influence on public dialogue and opinion, and to develop sound solutions to disinformation and other ills that arise in these spaces.

detail.abstract: Publicly available social media data has become increasingly important for understanding issues of public interest. As voluntary researcher access to such data becomes more restricted, policymakers have proposed mandates requiring large platforms to share high reach public data with researchers through mechanisms we call public content libraries. Although this data is often described as less sensitive, the collection and use still raises meaningful privacy and ethical questions. This study explores how individuals most represented in these datasets—high profile figures—perceive their own privacy, the privacy of others, and researchers’ use of public social media content. Drawing on 18 in-depth interviews, we find that high profile figures actively manage physical, emotional, and financial boundaries online, adjusting their posting practices based on their experiences. Participants understood their content was public and circulating through a suite of third party marketing tools. Despite this increased awareness of third parties, high profile figures still prefer "autonomy theater,” an understanding that data ethics practices may seem performative in a world of near ubiquitous surveillance but nonetheless acknowledge individual’s autonomy—which researchers and journalists working in the public interest to disseminate information that is trusted should not ignore. To perform in autonomy theater, researchers and policymakers may understand that a high profile figure’s expectations of privacy are low, even for deleted posts and bystanders in their content, but still take steps to protect individuals when possible and reasonable—aiming to balance the needs of social media researchers with the perspectives of high profile figures. We conclude with a series of recommendations for researchers working with social media data and policymakers who mandate that platforms offer some type of public content library.

title: Can a Skill be Measured or Assessed? 6-Level Skills Development Approach to Skill Assessment
affiliations: Hochschule Fresenius - University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Can a Skill be Measured or Assessed? 6-Level Skills Development Approach to Skill Assessment
detail.abstract: This paper reviews historic and current definitions of skill as a concept, as well as frameworks that have been applied to analyse levels of skills development across the academic and professional spectrum. The author proposes a 6-level chart of skill development based on the "can-do descriptors" approach by CEFR, also known as the ability assessment approach, for further discussion, development, and application. The proposed chart is based on six levels. These are organized into two Entry levels, two Operational Use levels and two Strategic Vision levels. Further debate on the typology of skills by Deloitte, LinkedIn Research and World Economic Forum is presented as of 2020 documentation. Its dynamic manner of paradigms changing the importance of a wide array of skills (alternatively denominated as employability skills, soft skills and/or 21st Century skills) are analysed, both for educators and employers.

title: How Aesthetics influences Aversion of Routing Operations Algorithms
affiliations: Leiden University - Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Rotterdam School of Management (RSM) and Erasmus Research Institute of Management (ERIM)

detail.title: How Aesthetics influences Aversion of Routing Operations Algorithms
detail.abstract: Calculating optimal routes is useless when route planners decide not to use them. This is not a hypothetical problem many people display algorithm aversion, resisting to follow algorithmic advice even when this advice is good. Indeed, accurately predicting the decisions of route planners enables more efficient traffic management, empowering route planning systems to provide effective executive route plans. In existing research on vehicle route problems, visual appeal is assumed as a factor that influences route planners' decisions, and its effectiveness is assumed to follow certain rules. However, these assumptions lack any support from empirical research and may not accurately capture route planners' behavior patterns at all. We develop empirical studies to explore the role of a route plan's visual appeal in planners' route choices. This contributes to bridging the gap between vehicle routing problems, which focus on optimizing routes in ideal situations, and route planners' behavior in real-world scenarios, since even mathematically optimal routes may not be the best routes in practice.

title: Assessing the Relative Importance of the Drivers of CO2 Emissions in the Selected Emerging Economies Using Machine Learning Approach
affiliations: VIPS

detail.title: Assessing the Relative Importance of the Drivers of CO2 Emissions in the Selected Emerging Economies Using Machine Learning Approach
detail.abstract: The main objective of the present research is to answer a key research question: what is the relative importance of the drivers of CO2 emissions? Another important question the present study addresses is how the countries are related to each other regarding CO2 emissions. Taking a sample of 42 emerging economies from Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and using hierarchical clustering and the neural network method the study tries to answer the key question. Firstly, the explanatory variables were identified through a review of the literature. Subsequently, the gathered data was classified into two clusters having similar characteristic variables utilizing the dendrogram by performing an exploratory clustering method known as hierarchical clustering. Later using the machine learning K-Means clustering technique, the clusters were verified. The use of another machine learning method of feed-forward multilayer perceptron commonly known as neural network helped us to identify the relative importance of explanatory variables viz. economic growth (EG), renewable energy consumption (REC), urbanization (URB), democracy index (DI) and foreign direct investment (FDI) for their relation to the response variable viz. CO2 emissions. The neural network results reveal that EG, REC, and URB are the most important variables (with Rank 1,2, and 3 respectively) followed by DI (Rank 4) and FDI (Rank 5). FDI seemingly is the least important among these identified variables.

title: When AI Meets Entrepreneurship: Evidence from the Commercialization of ChatGPT
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When AI Meets Entrepreneurship: Evidence from the Commercialization of ChatGPT
detail.abstract: This paper examines how the commercialization of generative artificial intelligence influences new firm creation, leveraging the release of ChatGPT as an exogenous shock to AI accessibility. We develop a novel industry-level measure of AI compatibility that captures the extent to which AI tools can support early-stage entrepreneurial tasks. Using a difference-indifferences design, we find that industries more compatible with AI experienced an increase of over 10% in firm formation following ChatGPT's release. To investigate why, we examine three mechanisms: reduced experimentation costs, capital reallocation, and human capital complementation. While we find no evidence supporting the latter two, we show that the increase in firm formation is concentrated in industries where AI can effectively assist and experimentation is critical—evidence consistent with a reduction in the cost of experimentation as the key driver. Moreover, new firms created after ChatGPT's release in AI-compatible industries are more likely to survive, grow faster, and attract more educated workers. Taken together, the mechanism and quality results suggest that AI lowers the cost of experimentation in a way that disproportionately benefits high-ability entrepreneurs, leading to both greater and higher-quality firm formation.

title: Impact of Inventory on Production Smoothening in FMCG Supply Chain
affiliations: VIPS

detail.title: Impact of Inventory on Production Smoothening in FMCG Supply Chain
detail.abstract: The FMCG sector is the cornerstone of any economy with significant contribution to GDP, employment and economic growth. The study aims to explore the relationship among production, demand, inventories and profit before interest and tax for FMCG sector in context of India. For analysis a panel data is employed with 64 firms of Indian FMGC sector, over 10-year time span from 2013-2023. To analyze cost structures and production, ordinary least square (OLS), fixed effect model and random effect model is utilized. It is found that demand, inventories and profit before interest and tax significantly impact Production. Furthermore, higher profitability helps firms to minimize their cost of production and operational costs. The study also highlights the unobserved heterogeneity across firms after employing Breusch-Pagan and Hausman test, illustrating variations in production techniques due to firm specific policies and strategies. Moreover, the inventories plays a significant role in production smoothening.

title: The Paradox of Delivery Failure: How Human vs. Machine Failure Shapes Customer Adoption of Autonomous Delivery Vehicles
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School, Southern University of Science and Technology - School of Business, University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School and University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School

detail.title: The Paradox of Delivery Failure: How Human vs. Machine Failure Shapes Customer Adoption of Autonomous Delivery Vehicles
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of online retail has elevated last-mile delivery into one of the most costly and customer-critical segments of the supply chain. In response, autonomous delivery vehicles have emerged as a promising solution for efficient, on-demand service at scale. Yet autonomy fundamentally reshapes the service process: rather than a traditional courier-led interaction, delivery completion now operates through joint customer–machine co-production, requiring active customer participation. Moreover, this shared responsibility creates significant attributional ambiguity, complicating how blame and trust are assigned when things go wrong. In this study, we investigate how the attribution of responsibility, whether the customer or the autonomous delivery vehicle is at fault, impacts subsequent customer engagement. Leveraging a unique dataset of over 200,000 autonomous delivery orders from a leading global e-commerce platform, we uncover a paradox: overall, experiencing a delivery failure increases customers' future engagement with autonomous delivery. We reconcile this paradox by disaggregating failures based on their source, which reveals two opposing mechanisms: (1) internal (human-fault) failures trigger a powerful make-up effect potentially driven by regret, increasing re-engagement; (2) external (machine-fault) failures elicit a punitive effect potentially driven by eroded trust, decreasing re-engagement. The counterintuitive aggregate result arises because the make-up effect from human-fault failures outweighs the punitive effect from machine-fault failures. We validate these distinct pathways using a two-stage least squares (2SLS) approach. Finally, as the perceived costs of the failure impact the intensity of these opposing reactions, we examine the moderating effects of order- and customer-specific factors. For human-fault failures, the make-up effect is amplified by high collection costs (e.g., large packages) and failures during non-working hours, but attenuated by coupon usage and habituation to self-pickup. Conversely, for machine-fault failures, the punitive effect is mitigated by high collection costs and coupon usage, but amplified by failures during non-working hours and habituation to self-pickup. Our study contributes to the literature on operational failures and human-AI collaboration by demonstrating how the cause of failure in a co-production context shapes technology adoption.

title: Measuring the Impact of Inventory and Marketing on Production Smoothening in a Utility Sector: A Panel Data Approach
affiliations: VIPS

detail.title: Measuring the Impact of Inventory and Marketing on Production Smoothening in a Utility Sector: A Panel Data Approach
detail.abstract: Utility sector is the foundation of economic growth that ensures energy security and industrial productivity along with influencing the living standards especially for the developing countries. The present study critically examines the progressing landscape of India's utility sector, focusing on demand side drifts, executive challenges, financial performances and technological improvements. The study uses extensive panel data of 26 major firms of the utility sector listed in Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sectoral indices over the period of 10 years (2013-2023). The panel data analysis includes multiple linear regression modelling, random effect analysis and fixed effect regression models capture the heterogeneity in the data. The regression model indicates that change in cost of goods sold (proxy variable of demand), marketing expenses, profit before interest and tax (PBIT) and inventories are significantly impacting the change in cost of production (proxy variable for production). Between ordinary least square (OLS) and random effect, Breusch pagan test concluded that random effect is better approach which shows time invariability. After that Hausman test confirms that there is temporal dynamism present in data and hence the fixed effect prevails. The study provides valuable insights for optimizing production smoothening and hence the operational efficiency based on financial performance.

detail.abstract: Case Objectives and Usage This case is developed for financial management degree, especially courses on company merger and acquisition (M&A), post-merger integration (PMI), and multifamily business management. The target student groups are undergraduate students in management, accounting, finance, and business administration major. Through this case, students can understand complexity in multifamily business, merger and integration, and corporate governance. It serves as an excellent introductory case for business education. It helps students understand conflicting interests in multifamily business, and how to develop appropriate check-and-balance controls in finance, human resources, and business operations post merger.

title: Arbitration in England and Wales outside London
affiliations: University of Leicester Law School

detail.title: Arbitration in England and Wales outside London
detail.abstract: This article discusses the foundations of arbitration in England and Wales outside London, including topics such as the arbitration market, the arbitration community, arbitration practice, and arbitration institutions.  The interviews on which the article is based were performed as part of a research project funded by the United Kingdom’s Economic and Social Research Council.  Interviews were performed in 47 countries, including 127 cities and 1,086 interviewees.  Further information on the project is available on the project website (https://commercialarbitrationineurope.wordpress.com).  Seventeen interviews were performed in England and Wales outside London, involving 39 participants, with four interviews performed in Birmingham on 10 March 2019; one interview performed in Bristol on 16 November 2022; one interview performed in Cambridge on 24 October 2022; one interview performed in Cardiff on 14 November 2022; one interview performed in Cheltenham on 11 November 2022; one interview performed in Hull on 14 October 2022; three interviews performed in Ipswich on 20 October 2022; two interviews performed in Leeds on 12 October 2022; one interview performed in Liverpool on 5 September 2022; two interviews performed in Manchester on 7 September 2022; one interview performed in Newcastle on 10 October 2022; one interview performed in Northampton on 6 March 2019; two interviews performed in Nottingham on 9 March 2019; one interview performed in Oxford on 28 October 2022; one interview performed in Sheffield on 17 October 2022; and one interview performed in Southampton on 7 November 2022.  All interviews were performed by the author.  Interviews were recorded and then professionally transcribed.

detail.abstract: In early 2025, I publicly announced my withdrawal from any direct debate with Mr. Frank R. Zindler-a decision made out of respect for his health, his age, and his lifelong contributions to free thought and rational discourse. However, after this announcement, Mr. Zindler continued to publish additional replies and rejoinders concerning my previous research (Faith, Not Trance, 2025) and broader questions of religion and science. As he remained intellectually active and continued to address the same subjects publicly, I found it necessary-out of scholarly responsibility and fairness-to present a further response. Thus, The End of an Excuse was written not as a revival of personal debate, but as a continuation of academic inquiry. It aims to clarify scientific, methodological, and philosophical issues raised in his later works, including In Defense of Science (2025), and to preserve the integrity of the discussion for future readers and researchers. This paper stands as a record of intellectual dialogue, not confrontation-written in the same spirit of critical respect that guided my earlier decision to withdraw.-This note is included for transparency regarding the historical context of publication and debate.

title: Do Better Local Governments Make Cleaner Environment? Evidence from Fiscal Monitoring Policies
affiliations: , University of Alberta - School of Business, City University of Hong Kong and

detail.title: Do Better Local Governments Make Cleaner Environment? Evidence from Fiscal Monitoring Policies
detail.abstract: This study examines whether municipal governance shapes local industrial firms’ pollution levels. We argue that well-governed municipalities have strong environmental oversight and enforcement and, in turn, effective controls on corporate pollution. Using the staggered adoption of fiscal monitoring policies across U.S. states as a plausibly exogenous improvement in municipal governance, we find that toxic emissions from industrial facilities decline significantly following the implementation of such policies. This effect is more likely driven by investment in abatement measures than shrinkage in production activity. Our cross-sectional analyses show that the effect of fiscal monitoring policies on reducing toxic emissions is more pronounced for facilities located in areas with lower levels of ex-ante local government stewardship and those subject to weaker regulatory oversight from the Environmental Protection Agency. Overall, our findings underscore municipal governance and, more generally, local government quality as a significant factor disciplining local industrial firms’ environmental practices.

title: Rewriting the Future: How Metamodern Education Can Redefine Society and Leadership
affiliations: Hochschule Fresenius - University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Rewriting the Future: How Metamodern Education Can Redefine Society and Leadership
detail.abstract: This food-for-thought paper challenges traditional paradigms and proposes a metamodern framework for redefining the optics on the role of education in society, advocating for a new social contract rooted in shared values, inclusivity, and interdisciplinary collaboration. How can we democratize higher education and empower individuals to navigate the uncertainties of the 21st century? Is moving beyond fragmented knowledge and fostering skills-based education truly beneficial? Moving beyond postmodern fragmentation, metamodernism emphasizes cooperation and holistic development, presenting a blueprint for transforming society by bridging individual agency and collective progress. The Inner Development Goals (IDG) promotes skills-based and humanity-focused leadership that addresses the inner and outer dimensions of sustainable development. This transformative skills-based approach to leadership encourages educators and institutions to embrace complexity and ambiguity, preparing future leaders to leverage inherited chaos for meaningful change. This approach challenges traditional paradigms and calls for a dynamic interplay that aligns with the metamodern ethos.

title: Enhancing Examination Integrity Through Vision-Based Smart Proctoring Powered by YOLOv8 and Dlib Frontal Face Detector
affiliations: and

detail.title: Enhancing Examination Integrity Through Vision-Based Smart Proctoring Powered by YOLOv8 and Dlib Frontal Face Detector

publicationDetails.detailsText: Chinese Space Science and Technology Journal,  Volume 21 Issue 11, November 2025. Available Online at: https://www.xbna-pku-edu-cn.ddns-ip.net

detail.abstract: The ubiquity of online exam systems, driven by the swift surge in digitization and globalization, especially in times of global health crises like pandemics, necessitates a robust cheating detection mechanism. While current platforms employ conventional machine learning techniques based on vision, their efficacy is limited by the reliance on manually crafted features and the inability to extract hierarchical representations from raw data. This paper aims to address challenges related to complex system integration and low-resolution video by introducing a practical and efficient deep learning-based method for real-time cheating detection in online exam systems. Leveraging recorded videos from a custom real-world video dataset, YOLOv8 is used for object detection, while Dlib serves as a frontal face detector using a Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG)-based approach. The proposed method fuses the outputs of YOLOv8 and HOG to accurately detect faces, enhancing detection reliability and performance. The proposed method, which combines YOLOv8 and Dlib's HOG-based detector, achieved exceptionally high performance in the fused system, reaching 99.9% accuracy, 99.8% precision, 99.7% recall, and a 99.6% F1-score, surpassing existing methods. This fused approach accurately detected faces in online exam hall scenarios, demonstrating its reliability and suitability for maintaining exam integrity.
