detail.abstract: This white paper presents a systems-informed approach to qualitative inquiry that integrates reflexive interviewing, qualitative coding, and memo-based modelling within a unified epistemological framework. Drawing from second-order cybernetics and systems theory, the paper emphasises the researcher’s role as an observer within the observed system, advancing qualitative research as a process of co-constructing meaning through dialogue. It positions qualitative inquiry not merely as data collection but as systemic observation, interpretation, and theory building. The proposed methodology introduces a reflexive conversation framework inspired by von Foerster’s second-order observation, Luhmann’s social systems theory, and Pask’s conversation theory, articulating a novel mode of qualitative practice suited to organisational and social systems research.

title: Monotheism and the Limits of Multiculturalism: A Civic Rethink for NDMCs A Position Paper by
affiliations: Centre for the Study of Minority Cultures & Law

detail.title: Monotheism and the Limits of Multiculturalism: A Civic Rethink for NDMCs A Position Paper by

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Monotheism, by its nature, promotes theological singularity and civic discomfort in plural societies. NDMCs must avoid adopting monotheistic frameworks as state philosophy or civil religion, and instead cultivate pluralistic models like Anekantavad that affirm multiplicity, coexistence, and epistemic humility. 

This essay critically examines the civic implications of monotheism in the context of Newly Developing Multicultural Countries (NDMCs). Drawing on theological, philosophical, and sociopolitical sources, it argues that monotheism—while historically influential—carries metaphysical and civic risks when adopted as a framework for public life in plural societies. The essay challenges the adequacy of conventional multiculturalism, which often fails to interrogate the theological singularity embedded in civil religion. Through analysis of historical patterns, insider movements, contextual theology, and grassroots syncretism, the essay demonstrates that monotheism’s exclusivist tendencies can produce discomfort, symbolic dominance, and epistemic closure in NDMCs. It proposes a shift toward metaphysical pluralism, grounded in traditions like Anekantavad, which affirm manifold truths and relational coexistence. The essay concludes by advocating for a pluralistic civil theology—one that decouples civic unity from theological singularity and embraces diversity not merely as demographic fact but as metaphysical principle. This framework offers NDMCs a path toward inclusive civic identity, legal equilibrium, and interfaith harmony without replicating the exclusionary legacies of monotheistic statecraft.

title: The Impact of Political Leadership on Organizational Culture in the Civil Service in Ukraine
affiliations: University of Lagos and

detail.title: The Impact of Political Leadership on Organizational Culture in the Civil Service in Ukraine

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The Authours have No Interest to Declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: No Approval Required
declarations.funderStatement: The Authours Received No Funding For This Paper

detail.abstract: This study examined the impact of political leadership on organizational culture and civil service in Ukraine. The study employed a qualitative review to evaluate this impact. Using a purposive sampling technique, the researchers analyzed relevant documents obtained from academic sources, and from international institutions in order to get a more holistic picture of the impact of various aspects of political leadership on Ukraine's public and civil service. The findings from this research showed that although the effects of political responsibility were felt in the local levels of government, the enshrinement of ethical standards was not uniformly applied. There appeared to be some disparity between the enforcement of ethical standards among the lower cadres of staff and what obtained at the higher rung of the ladder. Furthermore, because of the crisis presented by the 2022 Russian invasion, the leadership structure in Ukraine's public service evolved from its previously rule based system, to a more adaptive form of leadership that was agile, innovative and able to take up multiple responsibility in a time of crisis. The study concludes that the decentralization efforts of the government were yet to be completed because many aspects of its implementation require urgent attention. The paper further recommends that for this process to be effective and efficient, the government would have to institutionalize adaptive leadership principles in order to ensure that the local authorities are better equipped to carry out their functions and to avoid political interference from the government hierarchy.

title: The Necessity of Error: Why Mistakes Are the Essential Nutrients for Scientific Progress
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Necessity of Error: Why Mistakes Are the Essential Nutrients for Scientific Progress
detail.abstract: Modern academic publishing operates under the illusion that the elimination of error guarantees scientific excellence. The peer review system, designed to prevent the publication of incorrect papers, has paradoxically become the primary obstacle to genuine innovation. This paper argues that error is not a threat but a prerequisite for progress. Through historical and modern examples, including systematic errors in microwave absorption theory and the entrenched resistance of peer-reviewed journals to correction, this study reveals that attempts to create a "perfect" error-free publishing ecosystem sterilize intellectual evolution. Just as life could not arise in pure water, science cannot thrive in an environment purged of mistakes. The suppression of "incorrect" ideas not only prevents their correction but also delays the birth of new paradigms. The paper concludes that the most dangerous aspect of the current publishing system is not the presence of error-but the institutional denial of its necessity.

title: The Johari Window Revisited: An Analysis of 48,000 LeaderView360 Reviews
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Johari Window Revisited: An Analysis of 48,000 LeaderView360 Reviews
detail.abstract: Analyzing 47,891 multisource leadership assessments from 2005–2025, this study revisits the Johari Window framework to quantify self-awareness and “blind spots” in 35 leadership competencies. Results reveal that leaders consistently overestimate interpersonal and adaptive behaviors—such as understanding others, recognizing trends, and building teams—while showing stronger alignment on task-based competencies. Cluster analysis identifies fourteen “blind-spot” competencies centered on emotional intelligence, adaptability, and people development. Although overestimation rates have declined modestly over time, relational misalignments persist. The findings highlight that sustainable leadership growth depends less on technical skill than on feedback-driven self-awareness and emotionally attuned interaction with others.

title: Is the only Purpose of Companies making Profits: Analysis of the CSR Role of Companies in Promoting Social Welfare?
affiliations: University of East Anglia

detail.title: Is the only Purpose of Companies making Profits: Analysis of the CSR Role of Companies in Promoting Social Welfare?
detail.abstract: The earliest forms of Modern Companies were instinctively and inherently social entities that were first invented to support societal welfare. In the past many years, however, dictated by the principles of capitalism and the Agency Theory of the Firm, companies are recognized by law as institutions primarily organized for the sake of operating economic activities targeted to maximize profit, and they have no legal duty to engage in activities of corporate social responsibility ('CSR'). Recently, however, as per the Stakeholders Theory of the Firm, the societal purpose of companies is regaining ground. Due to the proliferation of globalization, the lack of strong global governance mechanisms, and the presence of weakened national governments, the impact and business's place in society is, once again, being transformed, which has augmented the companies' ability to play essential roles in public policy and social welfare and thereby tackle global problems of welfare in a coordinated way. It has become an international norm for companies to engage in CSR activities aimed at advancing societal welfare. Having considered the amount of capital mobilized or profit earned, many countries also require companies, by law, to allocate a certain percentage of their yearly profits to engage in CSR activities that give back to the society in which they operate their business. Accordingly, this article analyzes the CSR duties of companies (including transnational companies) and argues that companies can and should engage in activities that promote social welfare.

title: Anchoring Debt Management on National Financial Net Worth -A Nigerian Perspective
affiliations: Nigerian Economic Summit Group

detail.title: Anchoring Debt Management on National Financial Net Worth -A Nigerian Perspective
detail.abstract: Nigeria stands at a critical fiscal crossroads, grappling with a complex debt structure, structurally weak revenue mobilisation, and rising development financing needs. This article advances a novel policy perspective centred on Nigeria's sovereign net worth as an anchor for sustainable public finance management and development-oriented borrowing. Drawing on global best practices, fiscal transparency frameworks, and balance sheet-based approaches, the article critiques Nigeria's evolving debt portfolio, particularly the shift from concessional to commercial financing, and assesses the macro-fiscal vulnerabilities it creates. It proposes a paradigm shift toward the National Financial Net Worth (NFNW) framework, which prioritises asset-backed borrowing, comprehensive balance sheet accounting, and capital budget ringfencing. Through this lens, innovative instruments such as GDP-linked bonds, climate-contingent debt, and infrastructure special purpose vehicles (SPVs) are explored as mechanisms to align fiscal expansion with long-term value creation. The article concludes by advocating for institutional reforms, particularly in fiscal transparency and asset valuation, and introduces a prototype Fiscal Sustainability Dashboard to track Nigeria's public sector net worth. Overall, the article provides a forward-looking, diagnostics-based approach to public finance in Nigeria, aimed at restoring fiscal credibility while unlocking transformational development outcomes.

title: Internet Ozone Layer: A Vision for Reclaiming Human Freedom in Information Civilization

detail.title: Internet Ozone Layer: A Vision for Reclaiming Human Freedom in Information Civilization
detail.abstract: In the 1990s, the United States and the European Union created the "ozone hole" in the global information environment by allowing the governance of the World Wide Web (Web)-the global public information infrastructure-to fall under corporate control. In pursuit of profit, these corporations adopted surveillance as their business model, transforming the Web into a system of mass behavioural extraction and modification. This led to an "Information Armageddon"-a state of eroding trust in the shared reality that threatens democracy, markets, and the global rule of law. As the US backs its technology corporations against regulations worldwide, the EU stands as the last line of defence capable of restoring balance. Europe faces an existential dilemma: calls for "competitiveness" and "simplification" risk weakening the digital rulebook, even as the movement for enforcement and technological sovereignty-known as EuroStack-is gaining momentum. This paper advances a vision for Europe's path forward: the creation of an Internet Ozone Layer-a public information infrastructure built upon user agents (browsers and operating systems) regulated as public utilities. These agents would serve as the backbone of a fair and sustainable online advertising ecosystem that monetises the Web. Achieving this requires urgent coordinated action tied into a coherent industrial policy: (1) enforcing the EU digital rulebook, (2) regulating user agents and online advertising, (3) establishing robust governance (4) funding the development of a European user agent infrastructure, such as browser engines. Addressed to policymakers, civil society, academia, and industry, this discussion paper calls for Europe to reclaim its information infrastructure and rebuild the online environment on democratic foundations.

title: Centralize or Decentralize? Co-Location with Accounting Precision and Incentive Power
affiliations: Keio University - Graduate School of Business Administration

detail.title: Centralize or Decentralize? Co-Location with Accounting Precision and Incentive Power
detail.abstract: We analyze a principal-agent environment with two levers: a measurement designer chooses accounting precision and a decision maker sets incentive intensity. In a CARA-normal setting with heterogeneous priors, we prove strict complementarity between precision and incentives and establish a Co-Location Theorem: when a single residual claimant controls both levers, expected residual value weakly exceeds any split allocation, and strictly exceeds it under disagreement. Robustness analyses (interval-mean ambiguity and multiplier preferences) preserve these results, while institutional frictions (limited liability and pay caps) leave the comparative statics intact. When "hard" measurement and "soft" discretion are technological substitutes, we characterize a switching frontier: separation can be locally optimal under small disagreement but gives way to co-location beyond a threshold. The model yields testable predictions for KPI redesign, pay-performance sensitivity, and the centralization of governance.

title: Advance Selling under Dynamic Uncertainty and Time-Dependent Penalty
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business, Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School and UCL School of Management, University College London

detail.title: Advance Selling under Dynamic Uncertainty and Time-Dependent Penalty
detail.abstract: We study a setting where a firm offers products or services, such as hotel rooms or rental units, under time-dependent cancellation policies. Customers choose between two types of options: a pay-in-advance (PA) policy with limited refund flexibility and higher penalties for cancellation, and a pay-later (PL) policy offering greater cancellation flexibility at a higher price. Customers are forward-looking, their utilities from PA and PL options are correlated, have heterogeneous willingness-to-pay and dynamic cancellation risks modeled using a Mixed Nested MNL choice model. We characterize the firm's optimal assortment of PA/PL options and prices. We uncover previously ignored interactions between service usage valuation and cancellation penalties and how they drive optimal pricing and assortment decisions.

title: Property Rights and Financial Access
affiliations: London Business School

detail.title: Property Rights and Financial Access
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effect of property rights on financial inclusion and subsequent changes in labor market participation and human capital investment. Using hand-collected savings bank data linked to the English census, I exploit the 1870 Married Women's Property Act, which granted married women ownership of their financial assets. A 10% increase in the population of married women is associated with a 1% rise in accounts and a 1.2% rise in deposit receipts after the reform, indicating greater financial inclusion. In districts with a savings bank, following the reform, female employment increases by ∼3 pp for married women and ∼6 pp for single women, with no change for men. The occupational structure shifts, with married women moving toward low-entry-cost work and single women moving into higher-skill roles that require greater human capital. Girls' school attendance rises by 9-12%, with no change for boys. These patterns align with an appropriability and agency channel in which greater control over earnings raises the private return to work and skill investment, with savings banks making property rights operative by providing secure, interest-bearing deposits. I develop a theoretical framework emphasizing this complementarity between reduced expropriation risk and enforceable, remunerated savings. These results demonstrate an important role of property rights in encouraging financial participation, and the complementarity of property rights and financial access in employment and education outcomes.

title: Alcohol Prohibition and Attitudes towards Spousal Violence against Women
affiliations: Le Moyne College and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Alcohol Prohibition and Attitudes towards Spousal Violence against Women

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: We study the effects of a comprehensive, statewide alcohol ban on attitudes towards spousal violence in the Indian state of Bihar. Using a triple-difference framework, we document significant improvements in attitudes towards spousal violence involving scenarios reflecting an increase in women's personal freedom, such as going out without telling the husband and arguing with the husband. We observe no change in attitudes involving a wife's supposedly traditional responsibilities, such as looking after kids, cooking, and having sex with the husband. We argue and provide evidence that alcohol consumption exerts a significant income effect, souring spousal relations that causes men's attitudes towards wife-beating to worsen. Our findings suggest that the alcohol ban benefited women of weaker sections (SC/ST communities) of society the most. We conclude that while such policies can empower women in certain walks of life, they are insufficient to alter long-rooted patriarchal beliefs.

title: Policy instruments for circular economy: Evidence-Based assessment of sustainable waste management in the UK and Finland
affiliations: Environment Europe Foundation

detail.title: Policy instruments for circular economy: Evidence-Based assessment of sustainable waste management in the UK and Finland
detail.abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) management has become a critical issue globally, driven by its growing environmental and societal impacts. This study addresses these concerns by identifying key factors across policy, economic, social, and technological dimensions through a systematic review of relevant literature. To assess the effectiveness of these factors, linear regression analysis is applied to examine the role of landfill taxes (policy), oil prices and Gross Domestic Product (economic indicators), education (social factor), and patents (technological innovation) in MSW management. The model is tested using data from the United Kingdom and Finland. The results show that landfill taxes are an effective policy tool in both countries, reducing waste sent to landfills. Based on econometric modeling, we recommend that nations introduce a complementary incineration tax to shift focus from incineration to recycling, invest in research and development of recycling technologies, enhance education and public awareness, monitor the impact of fluctuating oil prices on energy markets and waste management, encourage extended producer responsibility, and design integrated policy frameworks to foster circularity. These findings offer valuable insights for improving waste management practices and advancing circular economy initiatives globally.

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Educational Strategy Challenges and Opportunities for International Schools in Egypt A Case Study of Repton School Cairo
affiliations: Ain Shams University, Misr American College, Elsewedy Electric, Zadna KSA and ALMehwar hospital

detail.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Educational Strategy Challenges and Opportunities for International Schools in Egypt A Case Study of Repton School Cairo
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is poised to become a cornerstone of educational transformation, offering pathways to personalized learning and operational efficiency. This study investigates the integration of AI into the strategic management of international K-12 schools in Egypt, a highly competitive market. It focuses on how strategic AI adoption can enhance pedagogical outcomes, administrative efficiency, and the overall quality of education. Despite Egypt’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025–2030), adoption at the school level is often fragmented. This paper uses a qualitative case study of Repton School Cairo to analyze a mature, first-mover strategy. Through a document analysis of the school's official AI policies, governance frameworks, and public case materials, this study finds that Repton has moved beyond fragmented tools. The school has developed a holistic, "human-centred" (UNESCO, 2019) strategy centered on (1) proactive data governance that mitigates key ethical risks, (2) the development of a secure, in-house AI assistant named "Nour," and (3) a school-wide AI literacy program. This paper proposes the Strategic AI Integration Framework for Education (SAI-F-Edu), validated by the Repton case, to offer other international schools in Egypt a phased roadmap toward AI-driven educational excellence.

title: Do Banks Build Societies? Evidence from Brazilian and U.S. Mutual Intermediaries
affiliations: Texas Tech University,  and Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School

detail.title: Do Banks Build Societies? Evidence from Brazilian and U.S. Mutual Intermediaries
detail.abstract: This paper develops a structural framework to quantify how banks shape real lending capacity and financial resilience across advanced and emerging economies. We model equilibrium loan demand and supply under balance-sheet constraints, identifying two channels through which banks affect mutual and cooperative intermediaries: a cost-offunds channel and a constraint-relaxation channel. Using a new crosscountry dataset covering all major U.S. banks and credit unions alongside Brazilian commercial banks and cooperatives from 2002-2025, we structurally recover the time-varying loan-capacity multiplier that governs intermediation under stress. The results reveal that in the United States, banks stabilize mutual lending by absorbing liquidity shocks, whereas in Brazil, funding constraints bind and amplify credit contractions. The findings demonstrate that banks "build societies'' when they act as stabilizers, transmitting liquidity rather than retrenching it, and highlight how financial development hinges on institutional capacity to sustain intermediation when liquidity vanishes.

title: Slaying the Dragon: The Quest for Democracy in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, and Complexity Science Hub Vienna

detail.title: Slaying the Dragon: The Quest for Democracy in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
detail.abstract: This chapter explores how Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs), a novel institutional form based on blockchain technology, challenge traditional centralized governance structures. DAOs govern projects ranging from finance to science and digital communities. They aim to redistribute decision-making power through programmable, transparent, and participatory mechanisms. This chapter outlines both the opportunities DAOs present, such as incentive alignment, rapid coordination, and censorship resistance, and the challenges they face, including token concentration, low participation, and the risk of de facto centralization. It further discusses the emerging intersection of DAOs and artificial intelligence, highlighting the potential for increased automation alongside the dangers of diminished human oversight and algorithmic opacity. Ultimately, we discuss under what circumstances DAOs can fulfill their democratic promise or risk replicating the very power asymmetries they seek to overcome.

title: Global Sourcing under Political and Technological Expropriation Risk: The Role of Financing Frictions
affiliations: King’s College London - King's Business School

detail.title: Global Sourcing under Political and Technological Expropriation Risk: The Role of Financing Frictions
detail.abstract: Growing concerns over intellectual property protection have renewed interest in how multinationals organize production. We examine how state political risk and technologytargeted expropriation threats shape the choice between outsourcing (lower capital commitment but weaker control) and internalization (higher capital but stronger control over technology), and whether financing frictions condition these decisions. Using data on 3,000 U.S. multinationals across 95 countries (2002-2017), we find that higher political risk is associated with a shift toward outsourcing, consistent with firms avoiding capital exposure in hazardous institutional environments. Yet this effect reverses when firms face technology-targeted expropriation threats and possess high-quality patents, suggesting internalization is used strategically to protect proprietary technologies. However, high leverage strengthens outsourcing even under high technology expropriation threats, indicating that financial risk limits firms' ability to commit capital to secure stronger control. Our findings show how political, technological, and financing frictions jointly shape the boundaries of the multinational firm.

title: From suspected to prosecuted: Investigating insider trading
affiliations: Stockholm University

detail.title: From suspected to prosecuted: Investigating insider trading

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study analyzes identifiable Suspicious Transaction and Order Reports (STORs) provided by the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen, FI) under a data-use agreement. The material contains personal data and information relating to suspected offenses within the meaning of GDPR Article 10 and, therefore, requires ethical review under the Swedish Ethical Review Act (SFS 2003:460). The project sought and obtained approval from the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (Etikprövningsmyndigheten), Linköping division: Decision Dnr 2024-03527-01, approved 6 Aug 2024 (decision notice 14 Aug 2024). Data were processed only for research purposes, on secure systems, with confidentiality undertakings, and without any contact with the data subjects. Individual consent was not required because this data is a secondary use of administrative records.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the progression from suspicion to prosecution of illegal insider trading, using proprietary data of broker and exchange reports. Only 2% of the suspicion reports result in prosecution. Thus, public datasets limited to prosecutions capture only a narrow slice of enforcement. Reports are more likely when there are signs of information leakage, when the information is more valuable, and around scheduled announcements, but less likely at times of higher illiquidity and for firms listed on regulated markets. Regulators focus on trading profits, the suspect’s ties to the firm, the information value, budget constraints, and the volume of reports. Consistent with informed trading, suspected insider trading increases abnormal returns and correlates positively with asymmetric information.

title: Values-Driven Investment Choices by Gen Z for Spirituality and Security
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, and NDIM - New Delhi Institute of Management

detail.title: Values-Driven Investment Choices by Gen Z for Spirituality and Security
detail.abstract: This research delves into the convergence of Gen Z's spiritual values and financial security in investment behavior. Being the first generation to be born digitally native, Gen Z is reshaping conventional norms not just in lifestyle and work but also the way they merge personal values and financial behavior. Ever more, spirituality, mindfulness, and seeking purpose are impacting this group's investment decisions, with an increased interest in ethical, sustainable, and impactoriented financial products. Meanwhile, fears of economic volatility, global warming, and job insecurity inform Gen Z's need for economic security and risk-averse management. This article examines how these twin priorities spiritual alignment and financial security exist together, sometimes intersect, and finally influence Gen Z's investment choices. Shows there is significant association, having prayed to God and making a purchase in different age group. Also significant difference is found in chose the investment which feels secure for money purchase in different age groups.

title: A Computational Method for Solving the Stochastic Joint Replenishment Problem in High Dimensions
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Computational Method for Solving the Stochastic Joint Replenishment Problem in High Dimensions
detail.abstract: We consider a discrete-time formulation for a class of high-dimensional stochastic joint replenishment problems. First, we approximate the problem by a continuous-time impulse control problem. Exploiting connections among the impulse control problem, backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with jumps, and the stochastic target problem, we develop a novel, simulation-based computational method that relies on deep neural networks to solve the impulse control problem. Based on that solution, we propose an implementable inventory control policy for the original (discrete-time) stochastic joint replenishment problem, and test it against the best available benchmarks in a series of test problems. For the problems studied thus far, our method matches or beats the best benchmark we could find, and it is computationally feasible up to at least 50 dimensions-that is, 50 stock-keeping units (SKUs).

title: Report of the Pittsburgh Task Force on Public Algorithms
affiliations: University of Pittsburgh

detail.title: Report of the Pittsburgh Task Force on Public Algorithms
detail.abstract:
This report summarizes the findings of the Pittsburgh Task Force on Public Algorithms, a group created to examine how the city of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County use automated systems to make major decisions. The Task Force found that local governments are already using algorithms in critical areas like child welfare, policing, and court risk assessments.

A key trend is a mixed track record: some agencies are transparent, but overall, there is low public awareness and a significant risk that these tools could reinforce existing racial and social biases. The report emphasizes that without strong oversight, transparency, and mandatory public participation, these algorithms may worsen inequity. The recommendations focus on giving the public a voice, ensuring clear accountability, and requiring outside review before high-risk systems are adopted.

title: Beyond military sales: the market premium on dual-use R&D in the defence sector
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond military sales: the market premium on dual-use R&D in the defence sector
detail.abstract: We examine how financial markets value defence firms’ R&D investments in the context of rising European military spending. Using data for listed European and US contractors, we relate equity valuation and expected earnings to R&D intensity and dual-use (civilian and military) activities. We find that higher R&D intensity is linked to stronger equity valuations, especially for firms with substantial dual-use exposure.

title: Flexible Data Aggregation for Prediction and Decision Making with Contextual Information: Applications in Retailing
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Meituan, Meituan and Meituan

detail.title: Flexible Data Aggregation for Prediction and Decision Making with Contextual Information: Applications in Retailing
detail.abstract: Problem definition: How should online retailers make demand predictions or operational decisions with limited relevant data? Motivated by conventional data aggregation approaches, we develop a flexible data aggregation (FlexDA) framework to adapt to different degrees of heterogeneity across products, thereby striking a better balance between the bias and variance of data-driven predictions and decisions. Methodology/results: Under the FlexDA framework, we propose aggregating the individual datasets at different levels, potentially based on contextual information, and training submodels with each aggregated dataset. A meta-model is trained to integrate the outputs of these submodels with a set of weights. For demand prediction tasks with linear models, we propose a consistent estimate of the optimal weight, and theoretically demonstrate the advantage of the FlexDA approach over existing approaches under the small-data, large-scale regime. For decision making with nonlinear feature-demand relationships, with a fixed sample size, we show that the optimality gap of the FlexDA approach decays near-linearly in the number of products with high probability. We further validate the FlexDA approach with synthetic data and real data from the Rossmann store. Building on the theoretical development and empirical validation, we conducted an internal study with Meituan Youxuan, focusing on ordering problems in their community group buying business. Our proposed approach achieves an average reduction of more than 10% in both lost sale ratio (LSR) and inventory ratio (IR) for newly launched fresh products as well as standard products compared with the algorithm implemented by Meituan Youxuan. Managerial implications: Simply aggregating data from all products and training a shared model reduces the high variance caused by data scarcity but compromises the ability to capture heterogeneity across products. Our study highlights the value of flexible data aggregation for data-driven prediction and decision-making, especially for large-scale applications with limited data, with both theoretical and empirical support.

title: Integrated Planning of Drone-Based Disaster Relief: Facility Location, Inventory Prepositioning, and Fleet Operations under Uncertainty
affiliations: ,  and Texas Tech University

detail.title: Integrated Planning of Drone-Based Disaster Relief: Facility Location, Inventory Prepositioning, and Fleet Operations under Uncertainty
detail.abstract: We introduce a two-stage robust optimization (RO) framework for the integrated planning of a drone-based disaster relief operations problem (DDROP). Given sets of demand points, candidate locations for establishing drone-supported relief facilities, facility types, drone types, and relief items types, our first-stage problem solves the following problems simultaneously: (i) a location problem that determines the number of facilities to establish and where to establish them, (ii) an inventory prepositioning problem that decides the quantity of relief items to store at each established facility, (iii) a fleet sizing problem that decides the number of drones to deploy, and (iv) an assignment problem that assigns drones to established facility and demand points. In the second stage, the model determines a relief distribution plan and enables the reassignment of drones to demand nodes. We equip the RO model with an uncertainty set that captures the relationship between facility disruptions, demand for relief items, drone operational status, and the remaining usable fraction of pre-positioned supplies after the disaster. Additionally, we explicitly model the dependency of postdisaster drone functionality on the pre-disaster assignment decisions. To address the challenges of integer recourse, we derive a K-adaptability approximation of the RO model and develop a column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm to solve it. Moreover, we introduce several strategies to enhance the computational performance of C&CG, including an efficient warm-starting mechanism, symmetry-breaking constraints, and valid inequalities. We present extensive numerical experiments that demonstrate the computational efficiency of our framework and provide valuable insights.

title:
From Busyness Management to Business Management:

Reclaiming Business Management from the Cult of Busyness
affiliations: University of Portsmouth

detail.title:
From Busyness Management to Business Management:

Reclaiming Business Management from the Cult of Busyness
detail.abstract: This paper distinguishes between business management and busyness management as competing logics of organizing and knowing in contemporary organizations. Through conceptual analysis and theoretical synthesis, we argue that modern managerial practice has become dominated by a culture of busyness-the continuous performance of productivity through activity rather than achievement-a phenomenon we term and theorize as "Headless Chicken Syndrome." Drawing on classical management thought, theories of bounded rationality and sensemaking, critical management studies, and the sociology of time, this paper develops a conceptual framework contrasting the reflective, purposive logic of business management with the reactive, performative logic of busyness management. The paper advances the notion of managerial resonance as an alternative paradigm for reclaiming time, attention, and meaning in organizational life, while providing normative implications for leadership practice. In doing so, it contributes to the emerging discourse on post-productivist management and the ethics of attention by providing both a diagnostic lens and a restorative framework for organizational transformation.

title: A structured reflection for improving third party interventions and mediation practice: Reconsidering debrief
affiliations: Rutgers University

detail.title: A structured reflection for improving third party interventions and mediation practice: Reconsidering debrief
detail.abstract: We make a case for structured reflective practice for improving third-party interventions and mediation decision-making and outcomes. We propose that a lack of awareness of the automatic, intuitive nature of judgments that dominate the fast-paced and uncertain mediation circumstances risk a proper treatment of implicit social-psychological matters driving conflict and suitably addressing substantive issues. Implicit matters include parties' feelings about themselves and relational and process-related issues. The quality of intuitive unconscious decisions could improve by conscious structured reflective practice. This reflection presents a learning opportunity to gain an awareness of unconscious judgments and advance a beneficial interplay between conscious and unconscious processing. To support the significance of conscious, reflective practice for improving automated decisions in third-party interventions and mediation, we present the context of mediation and findings on cognitive processing, intuitive decision-making, expertise, and reflective practice. Empirical findings in negotiation, management, and medicine confirm the effectiveness of structured reflective practice. A research-based, four-dimensional Structured Reflective Instrument (SRI) developed by Tzofnat Peleg-Baker is offered. It was designed to systematically help mediators improve judgments, particularly the response to implicit mediation goals and outcomes. We provide an example of one dimension of the SRI in the Appendix.

title: AI-ENHANCED MULTI-OBJECTIVE OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR LEAN MANUFACTURING EFFICIENCY AND ENERGY-CONSCIOUS PRODUCTION SYSTEMS
affiliations: Lamar University

detail.title: AI-ENHANCED MULTI-OBJECTIVE OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR LEAN MANUFACTURING EFFICIENCY AND ENERGY-CONSCIOUS PRODUCTION SYSTEMS

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There were no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals and therefore did not require ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Manufacturing enterprises increasingly operate under the dual imperative of enhancing operational efficiency while simultaneously reducing energy consumption. However, conventional improvement approaches often remain siloed-addressing either productivity or sustainability-thereby constraining opportunities for reproducible and system-wide optimization. This study aims to develop and empirically evaluate an AI-enhanced, multi-objective optimization framework that aligns lean manufacturing principles with energy-conscious operations. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional, case-based design, enterprise cloud data pipelines were established to integrate Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) historians with submetered energy logs across multiple discrete-part production lines in three industrial plants. The primary variables included Lean Practice Intensity (measured through a five-point Likert instrument), Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and its components, and Energy Intensity (kWh per good unit). Additional operational moderators such as peak kW, demand variability, product mix, machine age, and shift patterns were also captured to account for contextual heterogeneity. The analysis pipeline consisted of scale reliability testing, descriptive and inferential statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression incorporating plant-and shift-level controls. Furthermore, mediation analysis tested the role of efficiency as an intervening variable, while moderation analysis assessed the conditional effects of demand variability. To complement empirical inference, a surrogate-assisted evolutionary optimization algorithm was employed to generate Pareto-optimal fronts and knee solutions, benchmarked against baseline production schedules. Key results demonstrate that Lean Practice Intensity exhibits a positive association with OEE and a negative association with energy intensity, confirming efficiency as a significant mediator with a residual direct effect of lean practices on energy outcomes. The influence of lean practices was found to diminish under high demand variability, indicating a boundary condition for implementation. The optimization results further revealed that knee-point policies typically improved OEE by approximately 2-5 percentage points, reduced energy intensity by 6-15%, and curtailed peak demand by around 6%, all without compromising delivery performance or schedule adherence. From a managerial and systems integration perspective, the findings highlight the importance of viewing lean routines as actionable energy levers rather than ancillary practices. The study recommends institutionalizing variability-aware and tariff-aware production planning, and adopting a governed digital stack that links key performance indicators (KPIs), digital-twin telemetry, and AI-driven optimization engines.

title: No-good Pattern-based Solutions for the Operational Final Pit Problem
affiliations: University of Chile,  and University of Chile

detail.title: No-good Pattern-based Solutions for the Operational Final Pit Problem
detail.abstract: The operational final pit problem (OFPP) is the problem of determining the set of blocks that maximizes the undiscounted economic value of an open-pit mine while satisfying both slope-precedence and operational horizontal geometric constraints. Unlike the classical final pit problem, which considers only slope-precedence constraints, the OFPP explicitly enforces additional operational constraints on minimum widths that account for extraction, non-extraction, connectivity, and reclassification requirements. To overcome these challenging geometric constraints, we propose a simple yet effective heuristic based on an integer linear programming model that incorporates no-good patterns to eliminate infeasible block configurations. This pattern-based formulation ensures geometric consistency by maintaining a strictly positive Hamming distance between infeasible and feasible pit layouts. The methodology is evaluated on seven large-scale instances, showing that practical pit limits can be achieved with less than 1.1% loss in undiscounted value for most cases, while deviations above 5% in others highlight the model's ability to reveal potential value losses that conventional approaches may overlook until later planning stages.

title: Random Tariff Wars and Business Uncertainty
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta

detail.title: Random Tariff Wars and Business Uncertainty

keywords: business uncertainty JEL Classification Numbers: F13

detail.abstract: The paper investigates the effects of frequent random tariff wars on business profit. One country randomly imposes an import tariff while the other country always retaliates tit-for-tat with the same import tariff rate. I characterize equilibria in which firms earn higher profits under a permanent reciprocal tariff war than under random reciprocal tariff wars. The profit loss due to uncertainty does not depend on risk aversion. The loss of profit occurs because firms are unable to plan and deliver their optimal production and sales levels when reciprocal import tariff rates fluctuate randomly.

title: Suing the Bretton Woods Institutions: A Legal and Moral Imperative for the People of Developing Countries

detail.title: Suing the Bretton Woods Institutions: A Legal and Moral Imperative for the People of Developing Countries
detail.abstract: Developing countries frequently endure the adverse impacts of corruption, poor governance, and maladministration within public institutions, outcomes often enabled or aggravated by the conditionalities, lending practices, and oversight weaknesses of the Bretton Woods Institutions (BWIs), notably the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). This paper argues that citizens of developing countries should pursue legal action in U.S. courts against these institutions to compel institutional reform and accountability. Building on the legal precedent set by Jam v. International Finance Corporation (2019), which curtailed the doctrine of absolute immunity historically enjoyed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs), this analysis demonstrates that victims of development-related harm now possess viable grounds to litigate under U.S. jurisdiction. Drawing on comparative reasoning from international law, sovereign immunity principles, and recent U.S. court decisions, the essay argues that citizens of developing countries can and should strategically utilize litigation to demand transparency, enforce restitution, and reform governance frameworks. The rationale emphasizes that legal challenges would not only promote justice for affected communities but also catalyze global accountability mechanisms, strengthening equitable and sustainable development governance.

title: The Price of Liquidity: Implied Volatility of Automated Market Maker Fees
affiliations: State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo and Stevens Institute of Technology - School of Business

detail.title: The Price of Liquidity: Implied Volatility of Automated Market Maker Fees
detail.abstract: An automated market maker (AMM) provides a method for creating a decentralized exchange on the blockchain. For this purpose, individual investors lend liquidity to the AMM pool in exchange for a stream of fees earned from its operations as a market maker. Within this work, we reinterpret the loss-versus-rebalancing as the implied fee stream generated by an AMM so that a risk-neutral investor is indifferent in the decision of providing liquidity. With this implied fee structure, we propose a novel fixed-for-floating swap on the fees generated by an AMM in order to quote the implied volatilities and implied correlations of digital assets. We apply this theory to realized fees in different markets to empirically validate the relevance of the deduced fee-based volatility.

title: Killer Acquisitions: How Big Tech's Startup Buyouts Threaten Innovation and Market Competition
affiliations: National Law University Odisha and National Law University Odisha

detail.title: Killer Acquisitions: How Big Tech's Startup Buyouts Threaten Innovation and Market Competition
detail.abstract: This article examines the phenomenon of the "killer acquisitions" wherein the dominant technology firms acquire the nascent competitors to neutralize threats and consolidate market power. It highlights how such acquisitions can disrupt dynamic competition by eliminating innovative challengers before they mature; which ultimately shapes the market structure and consumer choice. This paper explores the global regulatory responses including the US Federal Trade Commission's reinvigorated merger guidelines, the EU's Ex-Ante Digital Markets Act and UK's proactive Competitions and Market Authority. Against this backdrop, this article addresses India's emerging legal framework, noting the introduction of Deal Value Threshold and the proposed Digital Competition Bill designating Systematically Significant Digital Enterprises (SSDEs). It argues for a balanced approach that combines the qualitative and quantitative tests which strengthens institutional capacity and ensures proportionality to avoid overregulation that could stifle innovation. This paper concludes by emphasizing the need for international cooperation and a tailored, adaptive framework to preserve innovation, consumer welfare and market contestability in the digital economy.

title: Supply Chain Management and Operational Performance: A Critical Evaluation of Available Literatures
affiliations: Canadian University of Bangladesh and Bangladesh University of Professionals (BUP)

detail.title: Supply Chain Management and Operational Performance: A Critical Evaluation of Available Literatures
detail.abstract: The Supply Chain Management (SCM) is a strategic tool that companies across the world are using for promoting performances. Operational performance is one of the performance measures for both manufacturing and service companies. Proper implementation of SCM is instrumental for achieving targeted performance and growth for companies. It contributes in improving competitiveness for the companies in the global market place. There is hardly any option left for companies in Bangladesh for not implementing extended SCM in order to survive in the industry. In this era of intense competition, implementation of SCM is the likely solutions for grabbing more market share. This study makes a critical evaluation of available literatures on influence of SCM on operational performance in the Bangladesh Readymade Garments Industry.

title: Judicial Corruption and Creative Destruction in Colombia
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: Judicial Corruption and Creative Destruction in Colombia
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the Colombian “Cartel de la Toga” scandal (2017–2020) from the theoretical perspective of Joel Mokyr , Philippe Aghion, and Peter Howitt , Nobel laureates in Economics 2025. Their central postulate — that sustained development depends on investment in knowledge , innovation culture, and regulatory competition — is contrasted with the institutional deterioration caused through judicial corruption . paper explores how the scandal undermined social trust, reduced innovation incentives, and deepened territorial inequality by weakening the mechanisms that sustain creative destruction . The analysis adopts a multidisciplinary approach combining economic , financial , and cultural perspectives to evaluate the long-term impact of institutional failure on development and competitiveness in Colombia.

title: Conscious Distraction Learning Theory

detail.title: Conscious Distraction Learning Theory

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: ODEFTO LABS (ODEFTO TECH Pvt Ltd.- ODEFTO.COM)

keywords: Conscious Distraction Learning Theory Conscious Distraction Learning Theory Conscious Distraction Learning Theory conscious distraction

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Conscious Distraction Learning Theory (CDLT), a novel educational framework that harnesses intrinsic curiosity through strategic conscious distractions to promote continuous learning across diverse environments. Unlike traditional structured learning approaches, CDLT transforms everyday experiences into rich learning opportunities, cultivating meta-cognitive skills and enhanced decision making capabilities. The proposed learning equation, L = (C × E) + (O × R), where Learning equals Curiosity multiplied by Environment and Observation multiplied by Reflection, provides practitioners with a simple framework to implement this methodology. This research explores how CDLT offers advantages over conventional approaches by aligning learning with intrinsic motivation, facilitating domain specific value creation, and promoting perpetual growth mindsets. Through case studies across multiple domains, we demonstrate how conscious distraction learning develops pattern recognition, predictive capabilities, and innovative problem finding & solving skills essential for success in the rapidly evolving 21st-century landscape.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption through the Lens of Strategy, Governance & Risk Management
affiliations: , Consultant and  Truist Financial Corporation

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption through the Lens of Strategy, Governance & Risk Management
detail.abstract:
The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping industries and redefining how organizations achieve their strategic objectives. When effectively harnessed, AI enables smarter, faster decision-making, fuels product and service innovation, enhances customer personalization, and drives significant productivity and cost efficiencies. It is, without a doubt, a critical lever for sustaining a competitive advantage.

However, these same technologies, if implemented without appropriate governance, oversight, and ethical safeguards, can introduce material risks that undermine strategic intent. Poorly designed or misaligned AI initiatives can expose organizations to operational, ethical, and reputational vulnerabilities, ultimately eroding stakeholder trust and long-term value.

As AI becomes embedded in core business processes and decision-making frameworks, the imperative for a clear, coherent, and well-governed AI strategy has never been greater. Organizations that fail to establish such a strategy risk falling behind competitors, misallocating resources, or even incurring unintended financial and reputational debt due to ineffective implementation.

This paper is intended to:

  • Provide strategic guidance on how AI initiatives and use cases should be pursued with deliberate intent.

  • Offer direction to boards and executive leadership on developing and executing AI initiatives that deliver short and long-term value creation.

  • Stimulate discussion and reflection among directors and senior management as they review, approve, and oversee AI-related investments and governance structures.

title: Supplier Performance and CEO Compensation Contracts: Theory and Evidence
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin - McCombs School of Business,  and Fordham University - Gabelli School of Business

detail.title: Supplier Performance and CEO Compensation Contracts: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: This study examines how a firm's strategic interactions with its suppliers influence its executive compensation contracts. We develop a parsimonious model that demonstrates how a firm's board of directors can positively link CEO pay to supplier performance as a commitment mechanism to encourage supplier investment in production capacity. Our empirical analysis provides evidence consistent with this prediction, indicating that managerial incentives, on average, reflect not only the interests of the firm but also those of its supply base. Cross-sectional results reveal that positive incentive weights on supplier performance are larger for firms whose suppliers operate closer to full capacity, for firms with more financially constrained suppliers, and for firms with major suppliers or strategic alliances with their suppliers. Additionally, we find that suppliers increase their capital expenditures after their customers' CEO compensation is positively linked to supplier performance.

title: The Toga Cartel and Social Morality. Judicial Corruption and Social Morality
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: The Toga Cartel and Social Morality. Judicial Corruption and Social Morality
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the phenomenon of judicial corruption in Colombia known as the "Cartel of the Robe ," drawing on the theoretical postulates of Émile Durkheim's sociology and the positivist philosophy of law. It examines how the collective moral structure was weakened by institutional deviations that transformed justice-conceived as a guarantor of social cohesion-into a mechanism of privilege and impunity. Through a qualitative and hermeneutical approach, the case is interpreted as a manifestation of anomie and a loss of moral legitimacy in the State. The analysis relies on Durkheimian concepts of solidarity, the moral division of labor, and the sanctity of the legal norm to explain how the ethical decay of the judicial elite erodes the sense of community. It concludes that the reconstruction of justice requires a moral renewal of the State based on civic education, public ethics, and social responsibility.

title: The Challenge of Embracing Our Relational Nature in a Divided World
affiliations: Rutgers University

detail.title: The Challenge of Embracing Our Relational Nature in a Divided World
detail.abstract: This chapter examines the challenges of overcoming binary, divisive responses to crises-such as the 2023 Hamas-Israel war-through a relational lens. While polarized reactions often reduce complex realities to simplistic categories of oppressor and oppressed, such habits are rooted in Western individualist traditions that prioritize autonomous selves, monologic interaction, and hierarchical structures. These cultural patterns reinforce defensive reactions, diminish the value of the "other," and obscure the relational dynamics of power, thereby hindering genuine collaboration and dialogue. Drawing on social constructionist, dialogic, and relational theories, the chapter critiques the limits of individualist assumptions and highlights facilitative leadership as a transformative practice. Facilitative leadership can offer inclusive, reflective, and dialogic spaces that can surface hidden cultural and psychological dynamics, rebalance power, and foster co-created meaning. Through practices such as reflective inquiry, relational awareness, and dialogic engagement, it can support a shift from adversarial, top-down models toward collaborative, equality-based systems that can sustain constructive conflict engagement and collective problem solving. Ultimately, the chapter argues for embracing a relational paradigm that recognizes interdependence and fluid identities as central to human existence. By doing so, we can move beyond reactive binaries toward transformative collaboration grounded in dignity, mutual respect, and shared responsibility-conditions necessary for thriving in a divided and complex world.

title: The Sterile Ground: How an Environment of "Failure to Pass Review" Stifles the Birth of Thinkers
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Sterile Ground: How an Environment of "Failure to Pass Review" Stifles the Birth of Thinkers
detail.abstract: The genesis of transformative thought and profound intellectualism is not a spontaneous occurrence but the product of a conducive environment. This essay argues that a socio-intellectual climate dominated by the mechanism of "failure to pass review"-where ideas are preemptively filtered, censored, and judged against rigid, orthodox standards-is inherently antithetical to the cultivation of true thinkers. By examining the psychological, philosophical, and practical dimensions of such an environment, this paper will demonstrate how it systematically extinguishes the essential conditions for intellectual birth: cognitive liberty, the tolerance for failure, and the freedom to challenge the fundamental premises of established systems. Finally, it will posit a connection between the rise of bureaucratic academic review and the perceived stagnation in fundamental scientific progress since the 1970s Keywords

title: The Garbage Majority: Why Most Academic Papers Are Useless-and Why This Harms Scientific Progress
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Garbage Majority: Why Most Academic Papers Are Useless-and Why This Harms Scientific Progress
detail.abstract: It is increasingly asserted that the overwhelming majority of academic publications-often estimated at 90-95%-provide little or no intellectual value. While the claim is controversial, bibliometric evidence and historical patterns strongly suggest that only a very small minority of scholarly work produces meaningful scientific or theoretical advancement. This article examines the intellectual, structural, and epistemic reasons for the proliferation of low-value research, critiques the argument that "useless" papers are harmless or necessary, and evaluates historian Li Bozhong's assertion that academic garbage constitutes a public hazard, not a neutral by-product. We argue that low-quality research is not merely unhelpful-it actively distorts knowledge, consumes resources, reinforces false paradigms, and suppresses innovation. The crisis is not individual but systemic: publication incentives reward quantity rather than originality, leading to an explosion of incremental, derivative, and conceptually hollow work. The conclusion emphasizes that scientific progress requires a reorientation toward problem-driven inquiry, theoretical advancement, and critical scrutiny rather than publication volume.

title: Inclusive Economic Growth and Poverty Reduction Strategies in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Bibliometric Study
affiliations: 8 Mai 1945 – Guelma University

detail.title: Inclusive Economic Growth and Poverty Reduction Strategies in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Bibliometric Study
detail.abstract: This study offers a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of scholarly research on inclusive economic growth and poverty reduction in sub-Saharan Africa from 2015 to 2025, utilising data from the Scopus database and advanced network visualization tools like VOS viewer. The research maps patterns of author collaboration, thematic clustering, and research productivity in the field. The findings reveal the dominance of a small group of influential scholars such as Handa and Davis who serve as central nodes within dense collaborative clusters. Temporal and density visualisations highlight both long-established research communities and emerging themes, particularly in financial inclusion and governance reforms. Despite robust co-authorship networks, the analysis uncovers ongoing gaps, including limited interdisciplinary integration and underexplored policy mechanisms for poverty alleviation at micro and sectoral levels. The results emphasize the importance of high-quality, inclusive growth strategies and effective knowledge dissemination for sustainable development. Policy implications highlight the need for targeted capacity building, increased cross-sector collaboration, and the adoption of innovative development paradigms to accelerate poverty reduction in the region. This bibliometric approach provides an evidence-based model for ongoing assessment and strategic planning in African development research.

title: Strategic Management (SM)

detail.title: Strategic Management (SM)
detail.abstract: This paper, submitted by Nambili Samuel for the Master's in Global MBA at Abertay University, provides an in-depth strategic management evaluation of International Business Machines Corporation (IBM). The author draws upon professional experience as a data scientist within the organization to support the analysis. Using established strategic tools such as SWOT, PESTLE, and Porter's Five Forces, the study examines IBM's competitive position in the rapidly changing global technology landscape. The findings indicate that IBM possesses notable strengths, including a reputable global brand, extensive international presence, and leadership in hybrid cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI). However, the company faces persistent challenges related to bureaucratic structures, reliance on traditional business models, and strong competition from major cloud service providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. Strategic initiatives, including the acquisition of Red Hat and progress in quantum computing, have strengthened IBM's market differentiation. The report concludes that IBM's long-term success will rely on its capacity to increase organizational flexibility, promote customer-focused innovation, and embed sustainability and ethical governance into its overall corporate strategy.

reference: Osama A. Marzouk (2025). Verification of the reactingFoam Solver Through Simulating Hydrogen–Methane Turbulent Diffusion Flame, and an Overview of Flame Types and Flame Stabilization Techniques. Processes. 13(11):3610. https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9717/13/11/3610
title: Verification of the reactingFoam Solver Through Simulating Hydrogen-Methane Turbulent Diffusion Flame, and an Overview of Flame Types and Flame Stabilization Techniques
affiliations: University of Buraimi

detail.title: Verification of the reactingFoam Solver Through Simulating Hydrogen-Methane Turbulent Diffusion Flame, and an Overview of Flame Types and Flame Stabilization Techniques

publicationDetails.detailsText: Osama A. Marzouk (2025). Verification of the reactingFoam Solver Through Simulating Hydrogen–Methane Turbulent Diffusion Flame, and an Overview of Flame Types and Flame Stabilization Techniques. Processes. 13(11):3610. https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9717/13/11/3610

detail.abstract: This study aims to qualitatively and quantitatively assess the ability of the flow solver "reactingFoam" of the open-source OpenFOAM software v.2506 for a control-volumebased computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver in treating the reacting flow problem of a popular benchmarking bluff-body-stabilized turbulent diffusion (non-premixed) flame, that is, the HM1 flame. The HM1 flame has a fuel stream composed of 50% hydrogen (H2) and 50% methane (CH4) by mole. Thus, the acronym "HM1" stands for "hydrogen-methane, with level 1 of jet speed". This fuel stream is surrounded by a coflow of oxidizing air jet. This flame was studied experimentally at the University of Sydney. A measurement dataset of flow and chemical fields was compiled and made available freely for validating relevant computational models. We simulate the HM1 flame using the reactingFoam solver and report here various comparisons between the simulation results and the experimental results to aid in judging the feasibility of this open-source CFD solver. The computational modeling was conducted using the specialized wedge geometry, suitable for axisymmetric problems. The turbulence-chemistry interaction (TCI) was based on the Chalmers' partially stirred reactor (CPaSR) model. The two-equation k-epsilon framework is used in modeling the small eddy scales. The four-step Jones-Lindstedt (JL) reaction mechanism is used to describe the chemical kinetics. Two meshes (coarse and fine) were attempted, and a converged (mesh-independent) solution was nearly attained. Overall, we notice good agreement with the experimental data in terms of resolved profiles of the axial velocity, mass fractions, and temperature. For either mesh resolution, the overall deviation between the computational results and the experimental results is approximately 8% (mean absolute deviation) and 10% (root mean square deviation). These are favorably low. The current study, and the presented details about the reactingFoam solver and its implementation, can be viewed as a good case study in CFD modeling of reacting flows. In addition, the information we provide about the measurement dataset, the emphasized recirculation zone, the entrainment phenomena, and the irregularity in the radial velocity can help other researchers who may use the same HM1 data.

title: The Quantum Organizational Framework (QOF): The Grammar of Transformation

detail.title: The Quantum Organizational Framework (QOF): The Grammar of Transformation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal conflicts of interest related to the subject matter of this paper or the frameworks described. All concepts and models referenced (Quantum Organizational Framework, Structural Maturity Continuum, Pragmatic Transformation Diagnostic, Quantum Contribution Model, and Atomic Organizational Evolution) are the author’s original intellectual property.

detail.abstract:
Transformation failure is most often diagnosed as behavioural, yet its root cause is structural - organisations cannot deliver what their architecture cannot sustain. This paper introduces the Quantum Organizational Framework (QOF) as a diagnostic grammar that makes structure visible and measurable. QOF integrates the Pragmatic Transformation Diagnostic (PTD), Quantum Contribution Model (QCM), Atomic Organizational Evolution (AOE), and Structural Maturity Continuum to map how friction, flow, and feedback determine adaptive capacity. Drawing on organisational-design theory (Galbraith, Lawrence & Lorsch, Burns & Stalker, Mintzberg), systems and learning theory (Senge, Argyris & Schön, Beer, Wiener, Meadows), and information ethics (Floridi), it defines a five-level Leverage Hierarchy that links energy, visibility, and coherence across design layers. The paper positions constructive autonomy and dual-loop governance as design disciplines that turn ethics into engineered visibility. It serves as the theoretical and diagnostic foundation for the QOF ecosystem and related research on structural maturity and AI governance.

Transformation has become the most overused and least understood word in management.

title: The MiCA Paradox: Regulatory Enablement and Network Effect Constraints in Euro-Denominated Stablecoin Development
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: The MiCA Paradox: Regulatory Enablement and Network Effect Constraints in Euro-Denominated Stablecoin Development
detail.abstract: The European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation represents a landmark effort to create a harmonized framework for digital assets, with a key objective of fostering a eurodenominated stablecoin market. This paper identifies and empirically tests the "MiCA Paradox": the regulation successfully enabled market entry, yet its enactment is associated with a significant relative decline in the market share of euro stablecoins. Using a difference-indifferences eventstudy design with wild cluster bootstrap inference and data spanning 2020-2025, we find robust evidence that the post-enactment period led to a 33.5% relative decline in the euro stablecoin market share compared to USD stablecoins. We attribute this paradox to the interplay between regulatory enablement and the insurmountable network effects enjoyed by incumbent USD stablecoins. The findings highlight the limits of territorial regulation in global digital platform markets and offer critical lessons for the design of the digital euro and other jurisdictional policies.

title: Sequential Decision Making in Dynamic Environment Bandits with Stochastic Structure

detail.title: Sequential Decision Making in Dynamic Environment Bandits with Stochastic Structure
detail.abstract: Motivated by the dynamic/non-stationary nature of many real-world market settings, we study sequential decision making problem under dynamic environment that satisfies two conditions: (i) the amount of changes is linear in time horizon T ; (ii) the expected reward of each possible decision (an arm) follows an ergodic stochastic process. Existing algorithms fail to perform well in the dynamic settings, where the expected reward of decision evolves over time. In this formulation, the expected reward of each arm follows a Reflected Brownian Motion (RBM that governs the temporal structure of the reward distributions. Our goal is to characterize the cost of adopting to the changing environment. Due to the dynamic nature of rewards, in this setting, decision maker has to continuously keep exploring in order to adapt to the changing environment. It implies that the confidence bounds do not shrink over time. Our formulation is a special case of the restless multi-armed bandit problem that is ”stateless reinforcement learning (RL)” problem.

title: Behavioral Insights in Public Administration: Leveraging Nudges to Improve Public Policy Implementation

detail.title: Behavioral Insights in Public Administration: Leveraging Nudges to Improve Public Policy Implementation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve the participation of real human subjects. Therefore, no formal ethics approval was required, and the study complies with institutional ethical guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors for the research work or publication of this article.

detail.abstract: Governments worldwide are increasingly applying behavioral insights, particularly "nudges," to enhance policy implementation and public service outcomes. This paper reviews the theory and practice of nudges in public administration, drawing on cases from developed and developing contexts (UK, USA, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia). This study examines the evidence for nudge effectiveness, compares meta-analyses and government trials, and discusses design and implementation factors. Behavioral economics and choice-architecture concepts build our theoretical framework, while policy implementation models (e.g., top-down vs. bottom-up) guide our analysis of administration. A mixed-methods approach is used: systematic literature review and comparative case-study synthesis. This investigation finds that nudges can yield modest but meaningful behavior changes (often a few percentage points). Success depends on context: well-targeted nudges (e.g., timely text reminders, default options) have improved tax compliance, health uptake, and environmental behaviors in multiple countries, but effects often diminish at scale. Ethical and capacity considerations are critical: high-level political support, institutional infrastructure, and safeguards against manipulation are needed for sustained impact. Based on this analysis, this research proposes a framework to integrate behavioral science into public policy cycles, emphasizing data-driven experimentation, cross-agency collaboration, and evaluation. Finally, this study discusses implications for administrative capacity and longterm governance.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence Framework in Accountancy (Validated & Revised)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nil
