detail.abstract: This short essay provides an overview of ICE's conduct and detention practices. It offers with concrete suggestions on how state and local officials can respond now by enforcing existing laws and creating new ones. In addition, there are action items for every single member of Congress to undertake, even if they are in the minority party. This essay is a first draft in a needed larger conversation and call to action. This essay came from an October 2, 2025 talk, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TqxZgpqiEE4 and will be part of a larger article on this matter. This essay ends with an action list with concrete policies that state and state government officials can undertake.

title: QED Appointments
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, Israel Institute of Technology and Texas A&M University - Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering

detail.title: QED Appointments

declarations.funderStatement: AM was supported by ISF (Israeli Science Foundation) 491/22.

detail.abstract: There is a vast world of service-systems that are driven by appointments (reservations). Many of these systems are large, time-varying, and stochastic, which motivates the present study. Specifically, we optimize appointments to such a service system with soft capacity (e.g., an amusement or a nature park), with penalties for over- and under-capacity utilization ("newsvendor" tradeoffs). As capacity grows, we offer an asymptotically-optimal two-stage solution, first of a macro fluid model and then its diffusion refinement. This solution alternates among three operational regimes, which are temporally determined by the fluid model: under-loaded when the fluid level is below capacity, over-loaded when above capacity, and critically-loaded when fluid equals capacity. In the latter regime, the over- vs. under- tradeoff is ameliorated by exploiting economies-of-scale via square-root safety-appointments. Borrowing the terminology of many-server queueing theory, the operation is then Quality- and Efficiency-Driven (QED).

title: The War that Never Ends: A Psychological Discourse
affiliations: INSEAD - Entrepreneurship and Family Enterprise

detail.title: The War that Never Ends: A Psychological Discourse

publicationDetails.journalName: INSEAD Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This essay examines the enduring psychological dimensions of human aggression and war, tracing their evolution from instinctual impulses to cultural rituals and institutionalized ideologies. Drawing on psychoanalytic theory, ethology, and trauma studies, the essay argues that while aggression may have biological origins, it is profoundly shaped and sustained by imagination, narrative, and social learning. Human violence, unlike animal aggression, is moralized and mythologized-transformed from reflex into ritual, from necessity into ideology. The essay explores how organized aggression becomes "the machinery of madness," a collective enactment of the psyche's shadow in which empathy is selectively reassigned and cruelty legitimized. Civilization rests on fragile psychic structures-easily dismantled when repression gives way to collective regression. Through this lens, war is not only a political or physical event but a profound disturbance of meaning, conscience, and identity. The text proceeds through a psychological anatomy of trauma: the body's memory of fear, the mind's fragmentation, and the soul's struggle with moral injury. War's casualties extend beyond the battlefield into the inner life-manifesting as post-traumatic stress, survivor's guilt, emotional numbing, and the collapse of symbolic order. Furthermore, trauma can become both personal and transgenerational, silently transmitted through families as "grief with an echo." Yet within this darkness lies the paradox of resilience: the human capacity to transform pain into meaning, guilt into empathy, and suffering into witness. Ultimately, the essay frames the aftermath of war as an unfinished psychological process-the "long return to humanity." Healing requires not the denial of horror but its integration through mourning, narrative, and compassion. In its final reflection, the work suggests that the only true victory over war's persistence lies not in conquest or deterrence, but in the psyche's enduring capacity to care, to rebuild, and to love again.

title: Do Set-Aside Auctions Pay Off? Evidence from Brazil
affiliations: Ghent University, National University of Singapore (NUS) - Department of Finance, University of São Paulo and Utrecht University - School of Economics

detail.title: Do Set-Aside Auctions Pay Off? Evidence from Brazil
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of Set Aside (SA) auctions for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Brazilian public procurement. Exploiting a legal reform that made SA auctions mandatory for contracts below BRL 80,000, we show that restricting competition to SMEs significantly increases their chances of winning contracts by 17.9%, but also raises procurement costs by 12.1%. This implies an annual fiscal cost of approximately BRL 73 million, given the total procurement spending affected by the policy. This result likely reflects the exclusion of larger, potentially more efficient firms. A trade-off emerges when analyzing the effects of mandatory SA auctions. Using a difference-indifferences approach, we find significant positive effects on employment and earnings for SMEs, with an average increase of 0.93 jobs per firm. Our cost-benefit analysis suggests that, despite the additional procurement expenses, the economic gains for SMEs indicate that SA auctions can be a viable policy tool in certain contexts. An estimated cost per job created of approximately USD 2,800.

title: Magnitude Effects and Decreasing Impatience in Temporal Discounting: Models, Evidence, and Applications
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business and LIUC Cattaneo University

detail.title: Magnitude Effects and Decreasing Impatience in Temporal Discounting: Models, Evidence, and Applications
detail.abstract: Many factors influence how individuals discount future payouts. A robust factor is the magnitude effect, whereby a small payout is discounted more than a larger one. But when individuals are confronted with more than one future payout, what drives the magnitude effect? Using a ceteris paribus design, we find that the discount rate decreases with the sum of cash flows and the highest cash flow. We also consider a separable model with cash-flow specific discount rates, but find mixed support for it. We also observe decreasing impatience, and propose various parametric models to predict present equivalents. To test these models out-of-sample, we design a retention bonus whose goal is to keep employees as highly motivated as possible during an extended period of time. All models that account for magnitude effect do a good out-of-sample job, whereas the models that merely account for decreasing impatience do not. Thus, our research can aid individuals, managers, and regulatory agencies better predict how individuals perceive financial offerings.

title: Identity Reconstruction and Psychological Resilience of Expat Partners During Career Transition
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Identity Reconstruction and Psychological Resilience of Expat Partners During Career Transition
detail.abstract: Global mobility continues to redefine family structures and individual professional trajectories. While corporate relocation policies typically center on the employee, the expat partner's experience of identity loss and reconstruction remains largely invisible. This paper explores how expat partners navigate the psychological and professional transformation that follows career disruption abroad. Based on qualitative reflection and theoretical analysis, the study investigates the processes of identity reconstruction and resilience building during career transition, focusing on expatriate families living in Luxembourg-one of Europe's most multicultural microstates. The paper integrates perspectives from identity theory, resilience studies, and adult development, revealing how self-concept evolves through disruption, adaptation, and redefinition. It argues that resilience is not merely a personal trait but a relational and systemic process shaped by environment, support structures, and meaning-making practices. The findings suggest that coaching, mentoring, and community-based ecosystems can accelerate identity recovery and support sustainable adaptation in global mobility.

title: Career Development of Female Managers Toward Senior Positions in Israel
affiliations: Alexandru Ioan Cuza University

detail.title: Career Development of Female Managers Toward Senior Positions in Israel
detail.abstract: Background and Aims: This literature review will examine the internal and external factors inhibiting female managers' advancement to senior positions in Israel's labor market. Some of the inhibiting factors stem from the nature of the State of Israel since it became independent. The cultural framework consists of a few main elements that direct gender roles, including the military structure as translated to the business arena and the expectation that women will focus on caring for the family. Others stem from the status of women internationally and related discrimination in the workplace. In terms of employment, women absorbed more of the difficulties associated with COVID-19 constraints than men; women's work was more often stopped or decreased to part-time, and their promotion ceased. Methods: The review is divided into internal and external factors in four main areas: sociology, economics, human capital emphasizing female management, and legislation that includes retention of positions saved for women in top management in the public sector. Results and Discussion: The external reasons for the lack of promotion of women to senior positions are the ones that also form the part of the internal reasons. From an early age, children see the different roles of their parents. Boys and girls experience different treatment according to gender. The distinction between genders becomes established according to women's social expectations and, therefore, their perception of themselves. Thus, the distortion of differences between sexes is duplicated from generation to generation, and social gaps, economic dependence, and discrimination of women are created. Conclusions: Changing the perception of different gender roles, not only in educational institutions but also in art, advertisements, and all areas of life, could lead to change by legislation whose principles should be first applied in government institutions. Further research will explore how legislation and enforcement can advance women to senior positions.

title: The Presumption of Accountability: A New Legal Doctrine in Public Governance
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Presumption of Accountability: A New Legal Doctrine in Public Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with any individuals, organizations, or institutions that may have or could be perceived to have influenced the content of this proposal.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This proposal did not involve human participants, interviews, or personal data collection. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This proposal was conducted independently and received no external funding from any government agency, private institution, political organization, or advocacy group.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This paper is a legal and governance study that does not involve human subjects, clinical interventions, or empirical testing requiring trial registration.

detail.abstract: The Presumption of Accountability is introduced as a complementary doctrine to the long-established Presumption of Innocence. While the latter protects citizens from unjust prosecution, the former ensures that public officials remain continuously answerable for the lawful, transparent, and ethical exercise of their duties. It reframes accountability from a reactive process into a standing legal and ethical obligation. By shifting the evidentiary burden toward those who hold public trust, the doctrine establishes a structural safeguard against corruption and administrative abuse (Fair Trials, n.d.; Rule of Law Education Centre, n.d.; U.S. Attorney-General’s Department, n.d.).

title: The Third Eye of AI: Project Trinetra
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Third Eye of AI: Project Trinetra
detail.abstract: Modern AI systems heavily mirror the heuristics of human System 1 thinking which is fast, pattern-driven, and prone to error while lacking the reflective depth of System 2 reasoning. In this white paper, we argue that both systems are insufficient for navigating the complexity, ethics, and long-term implications of AI at scale. We introduce the concept of System 3: a Saturnian model of intelligence grounded in deliberation, foresight, and context-sensitive evaluation. Through philosophical framing, cognitive analogies, and technical architecture suggestions, this paper explores how AI must evolve beyond mimicry toward a new paradigm of reflective intelligence. We critiquw the voice of AI and the illusion of transparency in current "glass box" systems and outline the risks of scaling reactive models without embedded ethical cognition.

title: The Black Nightmare Bombardier UAV MAR12
affiliations: Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School

detail.title: The Black Nightmare Bombardier UAV MAR12

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This research presents the development of a next-generation unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) designed for highaltitude, long-endurance missions with advanced stealth capabilities. The UAV features a highly aerodynamic delta-wing configuration optimized to minimize drag and maximize lift, enabling efficient flight at high suborbital altitudes. Its smooth, streamlined structure is further enhanced by a pixelated blue digital camouflage pattern that reduces visual and radar cross-section signatures, making it ideal for reconnaissance, strategic surveillance, and precision operations in contested airspace. Advanced composite materials and integrated surface technologies contribute to its lightweight construction and superior thermal resistance. The design prioritizes aerodynamic efficiency, stealth performance, and autonomous navigation, representing a significant step forward in UAV innovation. This platform exemplifies the future of unmanned flight, merging cutting-edge aerodynamics, stealth engineering, and adaptive design for multi-mission versatility across military and scientific applications.

title: Predictable Progress: Constructive Autonomy and the Design of Dual-Loop Governance for AI Systems

detail.title: Predictable Progress: Constructive Autonomy and the Design of Dual-Loop Governance for AI Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None Declared
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable (conceptual and theoretical work)
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has advanced faster than the governance frameworks designed to guide it. Traditional containment metaphors-regulatory, defensive, and retrospectiveslow progress without increasing safety. This paper introduces the concept of constructive autonomy: the capacity of an intelligent system to evolve safely, visibly, and predictably within defined structural boundaries. Drawing on Floridi's conjecture and information ethics, Heisenberg's uncertainty, Beer's viable-systems model, Wiener's cybernetics, and Meadows's systems leverage, it defines visibility as the new foundation of trustworthy autonomy. The dual-loop governance model proposed here distinguishes between a performance loop that drives efficiency and an integrity loop that ensures fairness, explainability, and reversibility. Together, they enable organizations to achieve predictable progress-a state where AI learns within ethical and structural limits.

title: The Development Trap: Prosperity Today at the Expense of Tomorrow's Generations

detail.title: The Development Trap: Prosperity Today at the Expense of Tomorrow's Generations
detail.abstract: The discourse on the Middle-Income Trap (MIT) has long dominated development studies, portraying economic stagnation as the main threat to developing countries. This perspective assumes that rising per capita income will automatically improve people's welfare. However, this paper argues that such growth-oriented approaches often overlook ecological sustainability and intergenerational justice. Through a reflective-philosophical analysis, this study introduces the concept of the Developing-Country Survival Trap (DCST), namely a condition in which countries pursue higher income status at the expense of future generations and political-economic sovereignty. By critically reviewing literature and cases in Indonesia and other developing nations, this paper highlights the paradox that economic progress in statistical terms can coexist with ecological fragility and social inequality. The findings emphasize the need to reconsider the direction of development: shifting from a narrow focus on economic growth toward frameworks that uphold ecological resilience, sovereignty, and intergenerational well-being.

title: In Shenzhen's Shadow: Xiamen, Zhuhai, and Shantou

detail.title: In Shenzhen's Shadow: Xiamen, Zhuhai, and Shantou
detail.abstract: The success of modern China, and by extension the Communist Party’s economic policies, is often symbolized by the metropolis of Shenzhen. Previously an underpopulated fishing village, Shenzhen is now one of the leading financial and technological capitals of the world. This is an astounding transformation and achievement for any government, let alone a nominally “socialist” one. Moreover, since Shenzhen’s ascendance is directly attributed to the government designating the city as a “Special Economic Zone” in 1980, many governments from around the world have tried to emulate Shenzhen’s success by establishing their own SEZs. But what is easy to forget is that Shenzhen was not in fact the only SEZ, though it was certainly the most prominent and by far the most productive. In fact, in 1980, the Chinese government had selected three other cities to become SEZs, namely Xiamen in Fujian Province and Zhuhai and Shantou in Guangdong. But for various reasons, which this article will delve into, these cities have not achieved nearly the same success as Shenzhen. This divergence in development helps to explain why merely adopting SEZ policies will not lead to Shenzhen-like economic growth.

title: The Interplay between National Truth-Seeking and Criminal Justice Mechanisms in Transitional Justice Processes: A Comparative Case Study of the Liberian (2005) and the Kenyan (2008) Transitional Truth-Seeking and Justice Processes
affiliations: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg

detail.title: The Interplay between National Truth-Seeking and Criminal Justice Mechanisms in Transitional Justice Processes: A Comparative Case Study of the Liberian (2005) and the Kenyan (2008) Transitional Truth-Seeking and Justice Processes

declarations.ethicsApproval: none

detail.abstract:
The truth-seeking mechanisms in both Kenya and Liberia worked under a lot of pressure from almost all sides with limited resources and in a very limited period of time for an investigation spanning close to a century.
The TRC and TJRC have enabled victims and their families as well as witnesses to tell the truth. They have gone back to colonial and pre-colonial times to identify the underlying causes of conflicts and socio-economic challenges and proposed immediate and long time, structural solutions to resolve the challenges the nations face. But on ensuring the right to justice of the victims, their families and the society, the Liberian and Kenyan governments could either take measures without waiting for the outcomes of the truth-seeking process or should implement the recommendations of TRC and TJRC. Under the existing circumstances, it is difficult to discuss about the inclusive, integrated approach or an “interplay” between justice and truth where the only player in the field of transitional justice, albeit with all its limitations, is the truth-telling component. Equal attention needs to be accorded to the equally important component of the right to justice in both cases of Kenyan and Liberian transitional justice processes.

title: The Business Chessboard Strategy (BCS): A Conceptual Framework for AI-Driven Marketing

detail.title: The Business Chessboard Strategy (BCS): A Conceptual Framework for AI-Driven Marketing
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping marketing strategy, offering unparalleled opportunities for personalization, automation, and strategic foresight. However, existing research often treats AI as a set of tools rather than as an integrated managerial paradigm, leaving a conceptual gap between technological capabilities and strategic frameworks. To address this gap, this paper develops the Business Chessboard Strategy (BCS)-a conceptual model that interprets organizational strategy through the metaphor and logic of chess. Drawing upon secondary insights from recent studies and professional observations in AI-driven marketing, the BCS framework maps key organizational dimensions to chess pieces: King (vision and mission), Queen (core strategy), Rooks (processes and systems), Bishops(culture and ethics), Knights (innovation), and Pawns (operational actions). Through this metaphorical structure, the BCS integrates strategic foresight, decision-making agility, and ethical responsibility into a unified framework for navigating the complexities of AI-enhanced marketing environments. The paper contributes conceptually by bridging metaphor theory, AI strategy, and management practice, providing a flexible framework that can guide both academic inquiry and managerial decision-making in the era of intelligent technologies.

title: The Yaoharee Proposal -A Transdisciplinary Framework for Contextual Coherence Across Physical, Cognitive, and Ethical Systems

detail.title: The Yaoharee Proposal -A Transdisciplinary Framework for Contextual Coherence Across Physical, Cognitive, and Ethical Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. This study was conducted as part of the Yaoharee Coherence Framework Project under Araya Nikah Social Enterprise’s open-science initiative, without commercial or political influence.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or identifiable personal data. Ethical approval was therefore not required. All analyses were conducted within publicly available datasets and theoretical modeling frameworks.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work was self-supported by Araya Nikah Social Enterprise Co., Ltd., as part of its social innovation and knowledge development mission.

detail.abstract: This study proposes a unified informational-coherence framework that bridges physics, cognition, and ethics through a general continuity principle. The Coherence Field Equation, expressed as with , extends conservation dynamics into informational and moral domains. Within Regulatory Stability Theory (RST), the boundary term represents reflective regulation that sustains equilibrium. Three core case studies-AI ethics, social polarization, and ecological resilience-demonstrate coherence retention across adaptive contexts. Additional discussions outline cosmological and quantum applications as higher-order validations. Findings suggest that coherence preservation functions as a universal condition for systemic stability across physical and ethical domains.

title: Causal vs Retrocausal Attention Boundaries
affiliations: Universidad de la Republica

detail.title: Causal vs Retrocausal Attention Boundaries
detail.abstract: This study quantifies the minimal right context that changes model decisions about authority bearing constructions under strict causal masking versus non causal access. We formalize flip probability P_flip(b to b+Δ), the instance level threshold τ(x), and the construction level threshold τ_C, and we measure breakpoint sharpness over a right context ladder b in {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}. The dataset contains minimal pair ladders per construction family, deontic stacks, nominalizations, enumerations, defaults, agent deletion, scope setting adverbs, role addressatives, across six languages, en, es, pt BR, fr, de, hi, with balanced length, domain, and register, and human gold labels. We evaluate frozen causal decoder models, non causal encoders and encoder decoders, and causal streaming variants with sliding windows. Masking primitives include hard truncation, stochastic truncation, and delayed reveal streaming with cache isolation and sentinel based leakage tests. Primary endpoints are τ_C by construction and language, P_flip curves, AUC_flip, and a latency accuracy frontier. Results map τ_C to observed compliance deltas on instructed tasks while holding administrative workflow constant. The contributions are a public dataset with right context ladders, an evaluation harness with tested masks, per construction τ atlases and P_flip plots, and a preregistered analysis that links regla compilada constraints, Type 0 production equivalence, to measurable authority judgments.

title: Managed Money
affiliations: Cato Institute

detail.title: Managed Money
detail.abstract:
"The United States has no predictable monetary policy from week to week, much less over decades. Since the bulk of international transactions and reserves are in dollars, the world too has no monetary anchor. Nobody can know what the Federal Reserve is going to do in the years ahead, or how, or why. The Fed uses inadequate tools to manipulate inappropriate targets to attain impossible objectives. . . 

Gold cannot be safely ignored, which is why its price in on the radio every few minutes. As a prime inflation hedge, the gold price is an outstanding leading indicator or incipient inflation or deflation. People never leave the gold standard --only governments do."

title: The Mutations of Digital Speech

detail.title: The Mutations of Digital Speech
detail.abstract:
Algorithmic outputs now populate the digital environments through which contemporary life is organized. The role of law in facilitating and constituting (rather than merely responding to) these processes is gaining increasing traction in scholarly accounts. This inquiry traces the evolution of algorithmic outputs beyond their technical operations, attending to what it calls their mutations. The first mutation redefined speech as data to be queried: search engines transformed the web from a space of information retrieval into an economic regime of ordered knowledge. The second mutation reframed speech as engagement: social media platforms fused moderation with amplification, turning expression into a metric of attention, governed by corporate architectures. The third mutation emerges in conversational systems and interfaces, where generative text displaces information retrieval, bringing with it dense technolegal entanglements and profound epistemic consequences. 
Scholars of freedom of expression, informational privacy, and communication studies have long grappled with these dynamics, yet their implications for broader legal thought have also become urgent. This piece seeks to organize and clarify the evolving debate around algorithmic speech, making this critical but often fragmented discourse more accessible to wider legal and interdisciplinary audiences. In doing so, it bridges the gap between observing technological transformation and critically assessing the constitutive role of law within it, offering a conceptual resource for researchers, students, policymakers, and practitioners navigating and contesting this evolving landscape.

title:
Handbook on the Global Governance of Artificial
Intelligence
affiliations: Stockholm University - Department of Political Science and University of Gothenburg - Department of Political Science

detail.title:
Handbook on the Global Governance of Artificial
Intelligence
detail.abstract: Global governance is conceptualized, in this handbook, as the formal and informal arrangements – institutions, norms, networks, and practices – through which collective action is organized beyond the nation-state. AI, in turn is defined broadly as computational systems capable of tasks that typically require human intelligence. The object of study for the authors in this handbook is the evolving constellation of efforts to shape the development, deployment, and consequences of AI through cross-border cooperation and regulation. The book collects contributions aiming to better understand and explain the global governance of AI (GGAI), and brings together empirical chapters that focus on the task of uncovering, analyzing, and explaining existing governance structures related to AI, and normative chapters that rely on ethical and philosophical theories and methods to assess them. In this introductory chapter, the editors situate the handbook in relation to existing scholarship on GGAI, and summarize each of the remaining 23 chapters.

title: The Primacy of Problem Formulation in Scientific Inquiry: Why Asking the Right Question Matters more than Experimental Validation
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Primacy of Problem Formulation in Scientific Inquiry: Why Asking the Right Question Matters more than Experimental Validation
detail.abstract: Contemporary scientific practice has become dominated by an epistemological framework that privileges experimental validation as the fundamental arbiter of scientific truth, often expressed through the maxim "experiment is the sole criterion for testing theory." This paper challenges this empiricist orthodoxy and argues that the capacity to formulate correct scientific problems represents the most critical determinant of genuine scientific progress. We demonstrate through historical analysis (Newton's gravitational problem, Galileo's inquiry into falling bodies, Schrödinger's waveparticle investigation) that transformative scientific breakthroughs emerge not from experimental execution but from the correct formulation of foundational problems. Experimental validation, while important, plays a secondary role-validating insights already generated through theoretical reasoning. Furthermore, we argue that contemporary gatekeeping mechanisms in scientific publishing have systematically suppressed theoretically novel problem formulations by demanding evidence prior to exploration, thereby reversing the actual logic of scientific discovery. We contend that correct problem formulation-often expressed through educated speculation (speculation)should precede and guide empirical investigation rather than follow from accumulated data. The paper examines how this inversion has produced an explosion of experimentally-saturated but theoretically shallow publications, while suppressing the genuine theoretical innovations necessary for scientific progress. We conclude that restoring the primacy of problem formulation requires institutional recognition that theoretical novelty should be evaluated on the basis of conceptual depth rather than evidentiary completeness at the moment of initial formulation.

title: Can Open Audit Committee Chairs Cure the Chilling Effect of Management's Presence on Auditors' Information Sharing During Audit Committee Meetings?
affiliations: , University of Alberta - Department of Accounting, Operations & Information Systems, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University and MacEwan University, School of Business

detail.title: Can Open Audit Committee Chairs Cure the Chilling Effect of Management's Presence on Auditors' Information Sharing During Audit Committee Meetings?

declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was approved by the Internal Review Board (IRB) of the institution where the experiment was conducted.

detail.abstract: This study experimentally examines how the leadership style of the audit committee (AC) chair (controlling or open) influences the amount of discretionary information that auditors intend to share with the AC, in the context of common meeting formats (i.e., AC meetings with versus without management present, or private meetings between the auditor and AC chair). Participants are highly experienced auditors, including partners and (senior) managers, from Big 4 accounting firms. We predict and find that an open AC chair mitigates the chilling effect of management's presence on the number of discretionary issues shared with the AC. Compared to those who attend AC meetings only, auditors who engage in private meetings with the AC chair before AC meetings plan to disclose fewer discretionary issues to the AC in subsequent AC meetings, but disclose more discretionary issues in total across meetings. AC chair leadership style has no impact on their discretionary information sharing in these private meetings. These results suggest that open AC chairs can mitigate the adverse effect of management's presence on auditors' discretionary information disclosure and have implications for regulators aiming to enhance corporate governance.

title: WAGE DELAYS AND MARKET FAILURES IN COLOMBIA
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: WAGE DELAYS AND MARKET FAILURES IN COLOMBIA
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the economic impact of payroll delays as generators of market failures in developing economies. It argues that the time lag between work performed and actual compensation produces liquidity constraints that reduce aggregate consumption, distort production cycles, and limit business efficiency. From a development and economic growth perspective, wage delays are considered negative externalities that spread throughout the market, triggering a chain of defaults, shortages of final goods, and late payment inflation. The article emphasizes how workers' financial uncertainty is transmitted to the production system, disrupting planning, resource flows, and territorial stability, especially in contexts with weak institutions and high structural inequality.

title: The European Best Bid and Offer (EBBO): From Fragmented Feeds to a Consolidated Tape
affiliations: LMU Munich School of Management, LMU Munich School of Management and Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich, Faculty of Business Administration (Munich School of Management)

detail.title: The European Best Bid and Offer (EBBO): From Fragmented Feeds to a Consolidated Tape
detail.abstract: We construct the first nanosecond-level European Best Bid and Offer (EBBO) by consolidating direct-feed quotes from ten major venues for Eurostoxx50 constituents between 2020 and 2024. The EBBO reveals that consolidation halves quoted spreads and nearly triples displayed depth, yet only 79–86% of marketable orders execute at the best available price. Geographic latency, routing frictions, and incomplete connectivity generate welfare losses of more than €50 million per year. These results quantify some of the costs of fragmentation and demonstrate how a consolidated European benchmark could enhance execution quality, transparency, and competition—directly informing the design of the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive III’s (MiFID III) Consolidated Tape.

title: Human Capital Disclosure and Equity Value in Japanese Stock Market
affiliations: Tokyo Metropolitan University and Kyoto University

detail.title: Human Capital Disclosure and Equity Value in Japanese Stock Market
detail.abstract: Disclosure regarding human capital has been mandatory for financial reports since the fiscal year ending in March 2023 in Japan. This movement can be viewed as a type of Investor Relations (IR) activity, as it widely discloses a company's human capital to a broader range of stakeholders. If one of the goals of IR activities is to enhance corporate value by reducing the cost of capital, then human capital disclosure is expected to increase corporate value through a lower cost of capital. Therefore, this study analyzes how much the cost of capital differs between companies that are proactive in disclosing human capital and those that are not. The results indicate that companies with more proactive information disclosure have a higher cost of capital, and that human capital disclosure does not necessarily lower the cost of capital. However, companies that showed a more proactive year-on-year change in human capital disclosure were found to have a lower cost of capital than those that were less proactive, a trend that was particularly pronounced among large companies.

title: May I Nudge You a Bit?
affiliations: Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University

detail.title: May I Nudge You a Bit?
detail.abstract: This study examines the Behavioral Economics approach, which analyzes human decisionmaking processes through emotional and cognitive factors, and explores the Nudge Theory developed within this framework. While classical economics assumes that individuals are rational actors, Behavioral Economics argues that decisions are often made intuitively, based on limited information and emotional influences. In this context, the Nudge Theory, introduced by Thaler and Sunstein, emphasizes the importance of subtle interventions that guide individuals toward beneficial choices without restricting their freedom of choice. The article illustrates applications of Nudge Theory across various domains such as public policy, environment, health, education, business, marketing, and artificial intelligence. Experiments conducted in Minnesota (USA) and the United Kingdom demonstrate the measurable impact of nudges on individual behavior, particularly in increasing tax compliance. Additionally, a field experiment conducted in Çanakkale, Turkey achieved a 75% reduction in cigarette littering through a competition-based nudge. The findings suggest that Nudge Theory not only enhances individual decision quality but also contributes to measurable improvements in public policy, environmental sustainability, and social well-being. Furthermore, the study argues that the integration of behavioral insights with artificial intelligence could make future nudge applications more effective, personalized, and ethically grounded.

title: Cultural Heterogeneity, Intergenerational Transmission, and Local Development: Evidence from Quilombos in Brazil

detail.title: Cultural Heterogeneity, Intergenerational Transmission, and Local Development: Evidence from Quilombos in Brazil
detail.abstract: I investigate the effects of cultural heterogeneity on local development using quilombos-communities of descendants of fugitive and liberated slaves-in Brazil. Using geo-coded data on all quilombos, I construct a "Quilombo Access" measure and exploit variation in paved road construction to build a formulabased instrument. Increased access systematically raises productivity in ancestrybased skills, education, and political participation for the black population, closing the black-non-black gap in these outcomes and reversing it to a black premium for blacksmiths and metalworkers. Quilombos function as organizations with vertical and oblique cultural transmission of traits through homogamous families, apprenticeship, and cultural-religious initiatives, groups, and policies, while providing amenities to increase black population density. I provide the first quantitative evidence that quilombo cultural traits, sustained through a cultural-heterogeneity equilibrium with organizational infrastructure, generate economic advantages for the black population, which also suggests the local coevolution of culture and institutions.

title: Leadership for age-diverse teams: mechanisms for integration, collaboration, and well-being
affiliations: Accra Institute of Technology

detail.title: Leadership for age-diverse teams: mechanisms for integration, collaboration, and well-being
detail.abstract: Multigenerational workplaces offer opportunities for innovation but also challenges of conflict, exclusion, and miscommunication. This integrative, theory-driven review examines how leadership behaviors shape integration, collaboration, and well-being in age-diverse teams. Drawing on inclusive leadership, social exchange, and socioemotional selectivity theories, it identifies key mediators-emotional intelligence, psychological safety, organizational support, intergenerational trust, and high-quality contact-and moderators including age stereotypes and generational attributions. Findings show that inclusive leadership, strengthened by emotional intelligence and bias awareness, fosters dialogue, trust, and psychological safety across cohorts. Motivational differences among generations further necessitate adaptive leadership approaches. A conceptual framework is advanced, positioning leadership as a strategic mechanism for leveraging age diversity. The study contributes to leadership and diversity scholarship by clarifying mechanisms that determine whether age diversity becomes an asset or liability, and calls for inclusive practices, leadership development, and sustained cross-generational engagement.

title: AlphaFlows GFlowNet based Framework for Formulaic-Alpha Discovery and Diversification
affiliations: and WorldQuant University

detail.title: AlphaFlows GFlowNet based Framework for Formulaic-Alpha Discovery and Diversification
detail.abstract: The generation of robust, uncorrelated alphas presents a significant challenge in quantitative financial modeling. Traditional methods, such as Genetic Programming, have historically been employed but are often limited by their tendency to converge on local optima, resulting in highly correlated alphas. Similarly, standard Reinforcement Learning approaches can suffer from mode collapse, leading to undiversified portfolios and suboptimal reward structures. GFlowNets is a novel framework that significantly overcomes the limitations of traditional methods. In this framework, the alpha discovery process is modeled as a sequential selection of alphas proportional to their reward. Furthermore, the integration of the Sub-Trajectory Balance (SubTB) objective enables the framework to discover a diverse set of high-performing alphas. We tested this framework on a dataset consisting of 10 years of 100 US Stocks. The resulting analysis showed that GFlowNets successfully produced a portfolio of unique and diversified alphas, resulting in an out-of-sample net Sharpe ratio of 1.70 after accounting for the transaction costs.

title: Evaluation Of Flexibility of the Exchange Rate Regime's Effect on Pass-Through Phenomenon: An Application of the Multiple-Doses Matching Approach
affiliations: Monetary and Banking Research Institute: Tehran, Tehran, IR, University of Isfahan and University of Isfahan

detail.title: Evaluation Of Flexibility of the Exchange Rate Regime's Effect on Pass-Through Phenomenon: An Application of the Multiple-Doses Matching Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no personal or financial relationships with other individuals or organizations that may have influenced their study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: There is no conflict of interest in this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not funded by any person or organization.

detail.abstract: Exploring effects of the main determinants on exchange rate pass through is crucial for the adoption of various economic policies, including exchange rate stability as well as trade expansion. An exchange rate regime can be a source of exchange rate and price changes, which is substantial in the implementation of foreign exchange policies. Among the various factors affecting exchange rate pass through, the flexibility of exchange rate regime has received less attention in empirical studies. Accordingly, the present paper seeks to find out how different exchange rate regimes affect the exchange rate pass through, which is proxied by the import price. To answer this question, we have used the multiple-doses matching approach by estimating the dose-response functions, to evaluate the effect of an exchange rate regime on the pass through. To this purpose, we have used data of 118 developing countries employing four types of exchange rate regimes in 2021. The results obtained from the use of dose-response analysis show that there is a negative and significant relationship between the degree of exchange rate pass-through and the degree of flexibility of the exchange rate regime at the significance level of 5%, so that an increase in the flexibility of the exchange rate regime has resulted a decrease in the degree of exchange rate pass-through. As a result, the degree of exchange rate pass-through in the hard-pegged exchange rate regime has been higher than those of other regimes, while, it has been the lowest in the floating exchange rate regime.

title: AI, Privacy, and Online Shopping Behavior: Decoding Consumer Actions Among Chinese University Students
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tianjin University, Guangzhou University and Jiangsu University

detail.title: AI, Privacy, and Online Shopping Behavior: Decoding Consumer Actions Among Chinese University Students
detail.abstract: This study advances the theoretical understanding of AI-mediated consumer behavior by introducing two novel frameworks that challenge conventional models. Examining Chinese university students' online shopping, we propose Contextual Privacy Recalibration Theory (CPRT), explaining why traditional privacy calculus fails in collectivist digital environments where institutional trust supersedes individual concerns, and Reflective Technology Engagement Theory (RTET), clarifying the counterintuitive negative relationship between perceived usefulness and shopping behavior through a usefulness-reflection pathway. Using PLS-SEM (n = 696), our integrated model achieves exceptional explanatory power (R² = 0.852). Results demonstrate that digital literacy functions as both a direct predictor and a critical moderator of AI engagement. While AI functions, social influence, and ease of use significantly predict behavior, privacy concerns showed no significant impact, fundamentally challenging Western-centric theoretical assumptions. These findings extend theoretical boundaries by contextualizing technology adoption within specific cultural and institutional environments.

detail.abstract: This study presents the development of a mobile-based intelligent system for the detection and classification of soursop (Annona muricata Linn) leaf diseases using deep learning. Recognizing the limitations of traditional visual inspection methods used by smallholder farmers, the project integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) model with a mobile application capable of operating fully offline. The CNN, based on MobileNetV2 architecture, was trained using the publicly available SoursopBD dataset containing 3,838 annotated images across six categories: Cutting Caterpillar, Cutting Weevil, Die Back, White Fly, Yellowing, and Healthy. Data augmentation techniques were applied to enhance robustness against real-world imaging conditions. The optimized model, quantized to TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) float16 format, achieved test accuracy of 97.74% with macro averaged precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.98. When deployed on Android devices, the app-maintained inference times averaging 0.68 seconds per image and remained stable during extended testing, confirming suitability for low to mid-range mobile hardware. Usability evaluation involving 21 participants utilized the UTAUT2 framework, yielding high mean scores for Original Research Article

title: Major Scientific Breakthroughs Are Not Born From Journals: A Direct Examination of AI, Microchips, and the Myth of "Gradual Academic Progress"
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: Major Scientific Breakthroughs Are Not Born From Journals: A Direct Examination of AI, Microchips, and the Myth of "Gradual Academic Progress"
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence and semiconductor technology are celebrated as the greatest technological achievements of the modern era. Yet neither emerged through academic journal debates, incremental peer-review exchanges, or the slow, organized evolution of ideas within the publishing system. Instead, they appeared suddenly, driven by breakthroughs outside the traditional academic pipeline-rooted in industry, engineering laboratories, and individual insight. This paper examines whether any major modern technology was born inside the journal ecosystem. If the answer is no, then a serious conclusion follows: the modern publishing system, dominated by garbage output and suppression of innovation, represents the darkest era in scientific history.

title: Individual vs. bundle HRM practices: effects on SMEs’ performance
affiliations: University of Prishtina - Faculty of Economy, Saints Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje,  and University of Gjilan (UGJ) - Faculty of Economy, Managment and Informatic

detail.title: Individual vs. bundle HRM practices: effects on SMEs’ performance
detail.abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of HRM practices, such as recruitment and selection, training and development, communication and information sharing, compensation and reward, job design, and performance appraisal, on the performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). We analyze these practices by examining their individual effects, as well as by strategically combining them to improve SMEs' financial, nonfinancial, and organizational performance. We employed a quantitative approach to conduct this study, using self-administered questionnaires. The study analyzes data collected from 153 manufacturing SMEs to explore the relationships between HRM practices and SMEs' financial, non-financial, and organizational performance. First, we find that using HRM practices individually has a limited impact on the financial and non-financial performance of SMEs. Next, we find that HRM practices, as a set of bundles, have a direct positive relationship with SMEs' organizational performance. The research findings suggest that SMEs that implement HRM practices as a bundle achieve greater performance and competitive advantage than those that apply them individually. This study makes a valuable contribution to understating the complex relationship between HRM practices and the performance of SMEs in the manufacturing industry.

title: Seats of Change? Female Board Directors and Firm Performance in Pakistan: An Event Study Approach

detail.title: Seats of Change? Female Board Directors and Firm Performance in Pakistan: An Event Study Approach

declarations.funderStatement: 1. International Growth Centre 2. Department of Economics, Lahore University of Management Sciences

detail.abstract: This paper explores the impact of female corporate board directors on firm performance and culture in Pakistan. Using data from 2012-23 on listed and unlisted firms in the country, we use an event study approach to assess the causal impact of the first entry of a female director on firm performance, exploring heterogenous effects on family and non-family firms. We extend this firm-level analysis using a director-level dataset that allows us to chart the specific characteristics and contributions of directors on different types of boards. We supplement this quantitative evidence with detailed interviews of 20 board directors as well as a larger survey of board directors. Our results show that the first introduction of a female director on a board has a positive and significant effect on firm assets, particularly in the case of family firms. Meanwhile non-family firms experience significant, positive effects on firm profitability, as well as on returns on assets and equity, effects that persist and accentuate in the years following the inclusion of a female director. Family firms, however, do not experience any significant effect on profitability. We argue that the inclusion of female board members in family firms often entails the appointment of 'token' directors that help consolidate firm ownership and control, manifested in growth in assets, but do not otherwise improve firm governance. In non-family firms, female directors are usually appointed based on their competence and expertise, leading to improvements in firm-level decision-making, leading to better performance outcomes across a range of measures.

title: The Role of Financial Capital in The Relationship Between Latin America and Industrialized Countries
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Colombia

detail.title: The Role of Financial Capital in The Relationship Between Latin America and Industrialized Countries
detail.abstract: This paper determines the existence of subordination dynamics between the center-periphery through the import of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) from industrialized countries during the models of Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI) and financial globalization throughout the 20th century in Latin America. For this, its general characteristics, origin, objectives and use in both models are contrasted through an imperialist theoretical framework, approximating FDI to the concept of financial capital and its respective classification between industrial and banking capital. Thus, similarities were found related to the positive shock that was expected on the domestic market and the foreign sources that provided its financing while there were differences such as the restrictive role of the government that was later more flexible and the use for industrial activities that, subsequently, was extended to commercial and financial activities. Therefore, it can be affirmed that the dynamics of subordination between the center-periphery worsened in the second half of the twentieth century because, during the ISI, there were restrictive government filters in defense of the fulfillment of the objectives, in contrast to the financial globalization that increased bank indebtedness and instability in the economic, social, and political context.

title: This Candidate is [MASK]. Prompt-based Sentiment Extraction and Reference Letters
affiliations: National Research University Higher School of Economics (Moscow)

detail.title: This Candidate is [MASK]. Prompt-based Sentiment Extraction and Reference Letters
detail.abstract: I propose a relatively simple way to deploy pre-trained large language models (LLMs) in order to extract sentiment and other useful features from text data. The method, which I refer to as prompt-based sentiment extraction, offers multiple advantages over other methods used in economics and finance. In particular, it accepts the text input as is (without preprocessing) and produces a sentiment score that has a probability interpretation. Unlike other LLM-based approaches, it does not require any fine-tuning or labeled data. I apply my prompt-based strategy to a hand-collected corpus of confidential reference letters (RLs). I show that the sentiment contents of RLs are clearly reflected in job market outcomes. Candidates with higher average sentiment in their RLs perform markedly better regardless of the measure of success chosen. Moreover, I show that sentiment dispersion among letter writers negatively affects the job market candidate's performance. I compare my sentiment extraction approach to other commonly used methods for sentiment analysis: 'bag-of-words' approaches, fine-tuned language models, and querying advanced chatbots. No other method can fully reproduce the results obtained by prompt-based sentiment extraction. Finally, I slightly modify the method to obtain 'gendered' sentiment scores (as in Eberhardt et al., 2023). I show that RLs written for female candidates emphasize 'grindstone' personality traits, whereas male candidates' letters emphasize 'standout' traits. These gender differences negatively affect women's job market outcomes.

title: Marginal Productivity Theory versus the Labor Theory of Property: An analysis using vectorial marginal products
affiliations: University of Ljubljana - Faculty of Social Sciences

detail.title: Marginal Productivity Theory versus the Labor Theory of Property: An analysis using vectorial marginal products

keywords: vectorial marginal products JEL Classification: D2

detail.abstract: Neoclassical economic theory presents marginal productivity (MP) theory using the scalar notion of marginal products, and takes pains, implicitly or explicitly, to show that competitive equilibrium satisfies the supposedly ethical principle: "To each what he and the instruments he owns produces." This paper shows that MP theory can also be formulated in a mathematically equivalent way using vectorial marginal products-which however conflicts with the above-mentioned "distributive shares" picture. Vectorial MP theory also facilitates the presentation of modern treatment of the labor theory of property which on the descriptive side is based on the fact that, contrary to the distributive shares picture, one legal party gets the production vector consisting of 100 percent of the liabilities for the used-up inputs and 100 percent of the produced outputs in a productive opportunity. On the normative side, the labor theory of property is just the application of the usual juridical norm of imputation to the question of property appropriation.

title: Phased Residential Project Management: A Reproducible Methodology for Design and Renovations
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Phased Residential Project Management: A Reproducible Methodology for Design and Renovations
detail.abstract:
In the field of residential renovations, the problem of systematic project management remains one of the key obstacles to achieving the expected results. A significant number of studios and contractors work without clear phase models and control mechanisms, which leads to delays and missed deadlines, cost overruns, and inconsistent quality of work. This article presents an analytical study of a reproducible project management methodology at the intersection of interior design and construction, developed and tested in a number of residential cases. The main elements of the methodology are phase planning, the formation of small cross-functional teams, and the implementation of regular QC/QA loops integrated into budget and logistics control.

The factual material consists of seven completed residential projects with budgets ranging from $80,000 to $150,000 and teams of three to four specialists. The analysis criteria cover the structure of phases, the dynamics of changes during implementation, the effectiveness of quality control, and the level of compliance with the budget and deadlines. The comparative analysis revealed consistent patterns: projects with clear phase logic and regular quality checks show minimal deviations from the plan, while chaotic change management sharply increases the risk of delays.

As a result, a reproducible “Phased Residential PM” structure is proposed, combining systematic planning, a matrix of team roles, and a change management process focused on maintaining a balance between budget and quality. The methodology is scalable for different types of residential renovations and can be integrated into the practice of design studios and contracting companies.

title: **ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: DOES IT KILL JOBS OR CREATE JOBS?
affiliations: GHANA RESEARCH

detail.title: **ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: DOES IT KILL JOBS OR CREATE JOBS?
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is not a threat to employment; it is a catalyst for transformation. AI will eliminate outdated, low-productivity jobs, but it will simultaneously create new, more sophisticated jobs in agriculture, manufacturing, services, logistics, and public administration. These new jobs require digital competence, problem-solving ability, technical adaptability, and human-machine collaboration skills. However, these jobs cannot emerge without a fundamental transformation of the educational system. Ghana does not currently have enough trained teachers to deliver AI-ready, digital-ready education. The solution is not simply to recruit more teachersit is to restructure the teaching profession itself, expand teacher capabilities through AI-supported training, embed digitalisation and problem-solving into all curricula, and build a national digital ecosystem similar to Estonia's ID-card model. This article explains how to implement this transformation in practice: how universities must redesign teacher-training, how current teachers can be upskilled at scale, how AI can support teacher shortages, and how Ghana can build an integrated digital-education backbone that prepares the entire population for the future economy.

title: Article 5(2) DMA: The prohibition on processing, combining, and cross-using personal data across core platform services
affiliations: University Villanueva

detail.title: Article 5(2) DMA: The prohibition on processing, combining, and cross-using personal data across core platform services
detail.abstract: This paper analyses Article 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act, which restricts gatekeepers from processing, combining, and cross-using personal data across core platform services without specific choice and valid GDPR consent. It explains the provision’s competition-driven rationale, its interaction with EU data protection principles, and the distinct obligations imposed on designated gatekeepers. The paper examines each prohibited conduct, the strict interpretation of the consent-based exemption, and the DMA’s role as lex specialis limiting available GDPR legal bases. It also discusses practical implications, including effects on advertising, AI development, consent design, anti-circumvention rules, and links with profiling-audit duties.

title: The Crisis In Economic Inflation Theory -Restoring the Emperior's Clothes
affiliations: RVA LLC

detail.title: The Crisis In Economic Inflation Theory -Restoring the Emperior's Clothes
detail.abstract: This paper offers a critical examination of prevailing economic theories of inflation, supported by both logical reasoning and empirical evidence. It identifies fundamental weaknesses in commonly accepted Keynesian and aggregate-demand models, showing that they lack empirical validity, perform poorly in practice, and disproportionately harm lower-income groups. The analysis then proposes a set of theoretical corrections to the traditional quantity-of-money framework to address its limitations and restore its practical relevance. Finally, the paper advances a structural shift in inflation policy - from a reactive stance focused on restraining demand to a preventive framework that aligns money supply growth with the economy’s productive potential. This approach promises greater price stability, stronger real growth, and fewer negative side effects.

title: Cheaper (and more effective) by the dozen: Evidence from 12 randomized A/B tests optimizing tutoring for scale
affiliations: University of Oxford, University of Oxford and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cheaper (and more effective) by the dozen: Evidence from 12 randomized A/B tests optimizing tutoring for scale
detail.abstract: Over the course of 12 rapid randomized experiments, we optimize an educational tutoring program. Tutoring is one of the most effective educational approaches yet has remained difficult to scale due to high costs. We adaptively test and improve a technology-enabled tutoring program to enhance cost-effectiveness and scalability. Results show that seven of twelve tests led to efficiency improvements, a "rate of discovery" of 58%. This compares favorably to the tech sector where 10-40 percent of tests generate improvements, demonstrating the potential for A/B testing to yield large efficiency gains in the education sector. The largest efficiency gains were driven by cost-reducing modifications that streamlined labor-intensive implementation processes and effectiveness-enhancing innovations that actively involved caregivers in their child's education, more than doubling impact at minimal additional cost. We explicitly measure practitioner prior and posterior beliefs, and find that rigorous testing facilitates more accurate identification of 'what works.' Our findings both reveal the returns to iterative testing in social programs and contribute new evidence on simple, cost-effective strategies to improve learning outcomes.

title: Nigeria Fiscal-Monetary-Structural Simulator: Complete Technical Documentation

The model integrates fiscal policy, monetary policy, structural reforms, distributional impacts, and external sector dynamics in a unified framework for policy analysis and simulation.

title: Beyond Stationarity: A Statistical Theory of Regime-Implicit Risk Premia in Self-Exciting Financial Markets

detail.abstract: Traditional asset-pricing models typically impose smooth dynamics or explicit regimeswitching structures on financial time series. However, modern markets exhibit endogenous bursts, volatility clustering, and abrupt transitions that rarely align with pre-specified regimes. This paper develops a theory of Regime-Implicit Risk Premia (RIRP), in which market states emerge endogenously from a self-exciting structure and are revealed through a statistical decomposition of return dynamics.
