Under scalar heterogeneity and single-crossing preferences, the coe¢ cient functions in the PDEs are nonparametrically identi…ed. Under symmetry, these lead to path-independent, money-metric welfare. We illustrate our methods with a simple empirical exercise using British microdata on home-rents and neighborhood school quality.

title: Quantitative Easing and Government Debt Sustainability
affiliations: University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business and University of Exeter

detail.title: Quantitative Easing and Government Debt Sustainability
detail.abstract: We show that quantitative easing (QE) worsens government debt sustainability. In our model, the government runs a primary deficit with elastic debt demand that makes interest rates endogenous. The central bank has long-term capital and remits profits to the fiscal authority. QE depletes this capital stock, reducing future remittances and crisis-fighting reserves. Contrary to Sargent and Wallace (1981), where greater monetary accommodation lowers the steadystate debt level, we show that QE increases the steady-state level of debt and shifts the default boundary inward, thus heightening fragility and reducing debt sustainability. Moreover, while QE can keep interest rates low for extended periods, continued debt accumulation eventually triggers a sharp rise in financing costs. Under certain parameters, large-scale QE makes previously sustainable debt levels unsustainable, leading ultimately to sovereign default.

title: Ways to improve Ukraine’s carbon tax
affiliations: University of Luxembourg - Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT)

detail.title: Ways to improve Ukraine’s carbon tax

keywords: excise duty tax on energy resources
price instruments for reducing greenhouse gas emissions

detail.abstract: This research paper is an overview of theoretical aspects of carbon taxing. This publication aims to review and summarize the practice of combining the environmental taxation system with the CO2 Emissions Trading System commonly used in European countries. In the course of the study, practical recommendations have been developed focusing on the future of the environmental taxation of greenhouse gas emissions. The results of this study can be used by government authorities and a wide range of stakeholders involved in the elaboration of solutions to create and implement the environmental taxation policy

title: Weather Anomalies, Climate Risk, and Inflation Expectations of Households and Firms
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey and TED University

detail.title: Weather Anomalies, Climate Risk, and Inflation Expectations of Households and Firms
detail.abstract: We show that locally unusual weather leaves a distinct imprint on prices, expectations, real activity, and credit. Linking the Business Tendency Survey (BTS) and the Consumer Tendency Survey (CTS) to province-day records from the Turkish State Meteorological Service, we build province-month anomaly measures and trace their effects in Türkiye, 2015-2024. A one-standard-deviation positive temperature anomaly raises near-term food CPI inflation for several months (peaking around months 4-6) before meanreverting. This salient price signal maps into beliefs: households' 12-month CPI expectations rise by about 1.5%, with larger revisions for rural, female, and financially constrained respondents. Households also report weaker income prospects, a darker macro outlook, lower willingness to buy durables, and higher unemployment concerns; effects are larger for rural, female, and lower-income respondents. On the food sector firm side, 12-month CPI beliefs increase by about 0.6%, unit-cost expectations rise, and sales expectations and overall business conditions deteriorate, with stronger responses among SMEs and highly leveraged firms. Beyond prices and beliefs, real outcomes soften at monthly horizons: domestic sales fall by about 0.8%, exports by 1.2%, total purchases by 0.6%, and employment by 0.4%, with larger contractions for SMEs and high-leverage firms. Credit-registry evidence shows an access-amplified working-capital response: total outstanding credit increases by about 1.7%, driven by short-term balances (+3.6%) alongside a decline in long-term balances (1.0%), implying pronounced maturity shortening (strongest for borrowers with better bank access, though constrained firms also tilt short). Taken together, transient but salient weather shocks raise expected inflation while depressing perceived and realized conditions and shortening debt maturity, temporarily steepening the monetary-policy trade-off and highlighting the value of climateaware communication and adaptation policies that dampen pass-through to costs, activity, credit, and beliefs.

title: INVESTMENT REGULATION IN THE ASEAN COUNTRIES: MAIN TRENDS
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations

detail.title: INVESTMENT REGULATION IN THE ASEAN COUNTRIES: MAIN TRENDS
detail.abstract: The proposed article aims to identify the main trends of investment regulation in the ASEAN countries. The assessment of the regulation of the admission of FDI into the economy of ASEAN countries at the regional and national levels has been carried out. The main conclusion reached by the author is that ASEAN membership and deepening integration interaction have effectively affected the growth of the investment attractiveness of the member countries, the liberalization of investment regimes and the strengthening of measures to support foreign investors. Over the past decade, ASEAN has become an investment hub in the Global South. Despite the problems (insufficient investment liberalization, low international competitiveness, lack of highly qualified labor, gap in economic development levels between countries, etc.), there are still prospects for strengthening the positions of member countries in global FDI due to deepening integration, dynamic economic growth, investment attractiveness, increased participation in global and regional value chains, strategic geographical location, rich natural resources.

title: On the Problems of the Student

detail.title: On the Problems of the Student
detail.abstract: In this paper, I model several aspects of student decision making and classroom competition, within a game-theoretic framework. Specifically, in Part 1, I develop a Two-Period Learning Model (TPLM) to show how uncertainty over course difficulty prior to registration can lead to problems of overconfidence or underconfidence in equilibrium (the former case, providing a partial explanation for the problem of dropping-out). In Part 2, I consider the ways in which a classroom resembles a first-price-all-pay Auction and develop a Winner-Take-All Model (WTAM) to show how competition for the 'top mark' affects effort in equilibrium. Within this competitive framework I show that increasing class size has an encouraging-effect on the outcome attainment of high ability students, and a discouraging effect on the outcome attainment of low-medium ability students. On average, the second effect dominates, such that if we are concerned with maximizing the average educational outcome of the classroom then class-sizes should be kept small to reduce competitive discouragement; whereas, if we are only interested in maximizing the educational outcomes of the most elite, then we ought to increase class sizes to induce greater competition. Furthermore, I show that equilibrium effort is, at first, decreasing in ability (extra productivity is simply traded for leisure) but ultimately it increases in ability as students become more in contention for the 'top mark'. I call these two effects the leisure substitution effect and the competitive effect, respectively. Finally, I introduce several other settings that possess the essential features of classroom competition and discuss how my results may be carried over. As usual, I conclude with a brief discussion of some of the possible areas in which future research could be directed.

title: Insurance for Agricultural Labourers in Asia: Evolution, Structure, and Trends from a Scientometric Research
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Pondicherry University, Pondicherry University - Department of Economics, PJN College of Agriculture and Research Institute and Pondicherry University (A Central University)

detail.title: Insurance for Agricultural Labourers in Asia: Evolution, Structure, and Trends from a Scientometric Research
detail.abstract: Agricultural labourers, one of the most vulnerable groups in the Asian agricultural ecosystem, constitute a significant share of the workforce across economies but remain ignorant. They are exposed to various risks such as wage volatility, seasonal unemployment, occupational hazards, migration, and climate-induced uncertainties, and are often excluded from traditional crop and insurance schemes. In this study, an attempt has been made to explore the evolution, structure, and trends in agricultural labourers' insurance in Asia using a scientometric approach. Bibliometric data from Scopus (1963-2025) covering 350 documents across 125 sources were analyzed using citation, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and co-citation techniques. Findings indicated a steady growth in research (3.41% per annum), with India and China leading contributions and forming strong collaborations with the USA, Australia, and European countries. Analysis on the thematic area exhibits a significant shift from the studies on localized labour and rural development spanning between 1963 and 1996 to methodological and regional focus between 1998 and 2010, and finally to contemporary research areas like climate extremes, food security, and inclusivism spanning from 2011 to 2025. In-depth review of the literature on insurance identifies four major models, such as the public sector insurance model, public-private partnership (PPP), index-based insurance model, and community-based insurance models, focusing on labour protectionism. Findings also alarm that despite product innovations, the adoption level is low owing to affordability and coverage gaps. However, insurance has been viewed as a social protection measure, a risk management tool for stabilizing the livelihoods of the agricultural labourers as well as improving the resilience of rural economies of Asia.

title: Developmental Maturity as the Driver of Loyalty Reordering from Family of Origin to Nuclear Family
affiliations: Arizen Corporation

detail.title: Developmental Maturity as the Driver of Loyalty Reordering from Family of Origin to Nuclear Family
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the commonly observed transition in adulthood-shifting primary loyalty from the family of origin (FoO) to the nuclear family (NF)-is not driven by chronological age but by developmental maturity. Drawing on family systems theory, attachment research, intergenerational boundary studies, emerging adulthood research, and developmental neuroscience, the paper proposes a multi-stage model in which differentiation of self, attachment hierarchy transfer, boundary clarity, and stewardship formation serve as the true mechanisms of loyalty reordering. Chronological age merely approximates the developmental timeline along which these changes typically consolidate. The model further explains why younger adults often misinterpret internal developmental incompleteness as partner distrust and use this misread insecurity to justify continued FoO loyalty. A mixed-methods empirical design is proposed to test these claims, including psychometric measures, vignette-based behavioral tasks, and longitudinal follow-up. The findings have implications for couples, clinicians, and cultural norms regarding adulthood, loyalty, and the protection of emergent households.

title: Securitized Receivables: How Brazil's Market Reform Lowered SME Financing Costs
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Securitized Receivables: How Brazil's Market Reform Lowered SME Financing Costs
detail.abstract: Credit card receivables in Brazil settle in T+30, creating a market for short-term advances that was historically costly and fragmented. Before 2018, each receivable was recorded only by the originating card acquirer, limiting access to other financing providers. The central bank required these receivables to be securitized via registration entities, creating standardized, centralized records. A difference-indifferences analysis shows that relative to the control, treated financing rates fell by around 25 basis points, maturities shortened slightly, and new advances as a share of outstanding loans rose following the reform. This case study shows how market design interventions-information standardization, broader access and greater transparencyenhanced competition and lowered the cost of financing for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

title: Endogenous Incentive Decay in Finite-Reward Proof-of-Work Systems
affiliations: Society of Actuaries

detail.title: Endogenous Incentive Decay in Finite-Reward Proof-of-Work Systems
detail.abstract: Bitcoin's proof-of-work (PoW) protocol enforces a halving schedule that asymptotically drives its block reward to zero. We formulate a dynamic game-theoretic model showing that, under standard competitive-mining and trust-price feedback assumptions, the equilibrium hash rate decays geometrically and security collapses. We identify counterconditions-fee endogeneity, cost collapse, or price hyperelasticity-that can sustain equilibrium. The result formalizes the claim that a PoW network can fail from within.

title: Fair Taxation of Inheritance?
affiliations: Masaryk University - Faculty of Law and Masaryk University

detail.title: Fair Taxation of Inheritance?
detail.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this article is to clarify the meaning and character of inheritance tax from a legal perspective. It is necessary to identify its role within the tax system and explore its connections to other taxes. Such an approach is the only way to substantiate arguments in favour of retaining inheritance tax. For the purposes of this paper, we assume that most countries in the European Union continue to levy inheritance tax, which must therefore be justified. A small number of states, on the other hand, have abolished this tax. The hypothesis we aim to confirm or disprove is that inheritance tax is a traditional levy firmly embedded within the tax systems of individual countries. Design/Methodology/Approach: To achieve the aims of the paper, we follow the IMRaD methodology. Within the research section, it is necessary to characterise inheritance tax, identify its place within the tax system, and analyse the reasons behind its abolition in some jurisdictions. The research also includes an analytical-comparative component devoted to examining the individual structural elements of inheritance tax. This detailed analysis enables us to formulate a set of questions concerning the optimal and fair legal construction of the basic structural components of inheritance tax, which are addressed in the discussion section of the article. In the concluding section, we primarily determine whether the arguments for retaining or abolishing inheritance tax are more persuasive. Findings: The hypothesis that inheritance tax is a traditional levy firmly embedded within the tax systems of individual countries is confirmed. Nevertheless, the decision to impose inheritance tax remains a purely political one. As is evident from the design of its structural components, the law and legal regulation can ensure that inheritance tax is implemented in a fair manner. Contribution to the Field: The research, which focuses on the fairness of inheritance tax from a legal perspective, is novel. Given that the decision to levy inheritance tax lies with political authorities, this paper offers options for designing the individual structural components of inheritance tax in consideration of other forms of taxation. Research Implications/Limitations: This paper does not examine the fairness of taxation from political, sociological, or psychological perspectives. It does not consider the possibility that populism may serve as a strategic approach for introducing or abolishing inheritance tax. Furthermore, the research does not address the economic efficiency of inherit-ance taxation. Originality/Value: The topic is highly original, as it addresses the legal regulation of inheritance taxation and the design of its individual structural components. The approach is applicable in all countries worldwide, regardless of whether they currently levy inheritance tax. It contributes to the discourse on inheritance taxation from a legal standpoint.

title: The Iberian Blackout and Frequency Stability in Power Systems with High Renewable Energy Source Penetration: Dynamics, Comparisons, and Implications for ENTSO-E Policy
affiliations: Cracow University of Economics and Centre for Security Studies

detail.title: The Iberian Blackout and Frequency Stability in Power Systems with High Renewable Energy Source Penetration: Dynamics, Comparisons, and Implications for ENTSO-E Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported under the Potencjał Program (project No. 027/EEE/2025/POT) by the Krakow University of Economics.

detail.abstract: The Iberian power system disturbance of 28 April 2025 exposed the vulnerability of converter-dominated systems with high renewable energy source (RES) penetration to rapid frequency decline and voltage-reactive instability. This paper reconstructs the second-by-second event sequence using publicly available waveform data, estimates system inertia using ROCOF-based and aggregate-unit methods, and examines the interaction between voltage-reactive stress and frequency response. System inertia (H) denotes the equivalent inertia constant of the synchronous area; ΔP is the net active-power loss; ROCOF is the rate of change of frequency; IAI is the Inertia Adequacy Index; and IAI-V its voltage-coupled extension. Results show that the disturbance originated in the voltage/reactive domain through overvoltage-triggered disconnections, which amplified ΔP and accelerated frequency decay to a nadir of approximately 48.5 Hz. Estimated inertia was in the range of 3.2-4.0 s. The constrained operational time window, driven by voltage-reactive events, limited the effectiveness of UFLS and FCR services. The findings indicate that inverter-dominated regions require harmonized grid-forming capabilities, locational VAR/FFR procurement, and enforceable inertia floors.

title: Patent Semiotics (and Forward: Remembering Professor Dan L. Burk)
affiliations: University of California, Irvine School of Law

detail.title: Patent Semiotics (and Forward: Remembering Professor Dan L. Burk)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: Patent law is structured around the use and characteristics of a particular type of document, drafted by an aspiring inventor and issued by the federal government.1 The patent is generally expected to convey particular types of legal and technical meaning to its audience.2 This suggests that patents and associated patent doctrines should be prime contenders for examination as a matter of semiotics, the study of signs, including text or graphics, and how they convey meaning. Yet, surprisingly little has been previously said about patent semiotics,3 especially considering that the text and drawings of every patent are quintessentially an exercise in signification. I will argue here that the semiotic nature of the patent document in fact makes it amenable to understanding via the insights and methods developed to study signification more generally. This analysis may be particularly apt in the circumstance of interpreting patent claims, which is a notoriously fraught exercise in determining meaning.

title: Jumping without parachutes. Revolving doors and political incentives
affiliations: University of Barcelona - Institut d'Economia de Barcelona (IEB) and DISEIS, Faculty of Political and Social Sciences, Universita' Cattolica del Sacro Cuore

detail.title: Jumping without parachutes. Revolving doors and political incentives

declarations.funderStatement: Funding from the Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance, Research Grant 2022, is gratefully acknowledged. Gamalerio acknowledges support from the Baffi Research Center. This research has also received funding from the following projects: PID2021-126517NB-I00, PID2021-124353NB-I00 (Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovaci´on y Universidades).

detail.abstract: This paper investigates how connections between politics and firms influence the profiles of political candidates and their policy decisions. We focus on the effects of anti-revolving door laws, which impose a mandatory "cooling-off" period before former politicians can take significant positions in the bureaucracy or in specific firms (e.g. lobbying, state-owned etc.). We develop a political agency model where politicians can access "politically connected outside options" (PCOs), and examine how a reduction in their expected value impacts endogenous candidate selection and policymaking. Our findings suggest that a decline in the value of PCOs disproportionately affects individuals with lower human capital, thereby increasing the proportion of high human capital candidates. Simultaneously, this shift heightens the likelihood that low human capital politicians will pander toward the voters, choosing popular but possibly suboptimal policies. We test those predictions using data from Italian municipalities. Leveraging a population threshold that triggers the implementation of antirevolving door policies, we employ a difference-in-discontinuity approach. Our results show that the cooling-off period raises the average education levels of candidates and elected mayors. Additionally, we find that the reform increases the probability that low human capital mayors reduce local taxes, thereby avoiding electorally costly policies.

title: Two Fundamental Constants of the Physical World — The Speed of Light c and the Space–Mass Coupling Constant μg
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Two Fundamental Constants of the Physical World — The Speed of Light c and the Space–Mass Coupling Constant μg

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or personal conflicts of interest related to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects. All experiments were conducted in accordance with local regulations on animal welfare and agricultural research practices.
declarations.funderStatement: This study did not receive external funding. All experimental work was self funded by the author.

detail.abstract:
Natural constants are numerous, yet their mutual logical connections have long lacked a unified explanation.

This paper proposes that all constants can be determined from two fundamental constants — the speed of light (c) and the space–mass coupling constant (μg).

Within the geometric framework of a right-handed helical spatial flow, three mother equations are established, which respectively define the geometric origins of spatial divergence strength, space–mass coupling, and the gravitational constant. From these relations, the no-rescaling lemma is derived, proving that μg is an absolute geometric constant independent of units or scale.

Starting from the helical angular motion, the reduced Planck constant naturally follows, revealing that h is a “per-radian action” jointly defined by the space–mass coupling and the speed of light. 

An electromagnetic bridging layer is further introduced through the mass–charge transduction constant kmq, linking μg with the vacuum constants.

This result achieves, for the first time, a four-level closed loop among the geometric, gravitational, quantum, and electromagnetic constants, originating from c, μg thereby providing a self-consistent and experimentally testable two-constant foundation for Unified Field Theory.

title: Employment Horizons and Job Productivity: A Randomized Shock to Mexican Judges' Tenure. *
affiliations: Banco de Mexico and Banco de México

detail.title: Employment Horizons and Job Productivity: A Randomized Shock to Mexican Judges' Tenure. *
detail.abstract: Employment security shapes how public officials exert effort, yet causal evidence is limited. This paper studies how shorter employment horizons affect productivity using a large-scale randomized experiment from Mexicos 2024 judicial reform. Judges were randomly assigned ten or thirty-four-month contracts, creating exogenous variation in expected tenure. We find that shorter horizons reduce productivity by about fifteen percent relative to their peers with longer horizons. This results in an arc elasticity of 0.15. Nearly all of the decline comes from core judicial tasks, not from reduced staffing or resources, suggesting a behavioral response to weaker long-term incentives. The results provide rare experimental evidence consistent with principal-agent models linking career horizons to effort.

title: High Yield, Capped Gains: Mechanics, Trade-offs, and Practical Diagnostics for Covered-Call ETFs
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: High Yield, Capped Gains: Mechanics, Trade-offs, and Practical Diagnostics for Covered-Call ETFs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, patients, or case studies requiring ethics approval. All data used are publicly available.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently, without external funding or institutional support.

detail.abstract: Covered-call ETFs offer high yield with capped gains: they turn part of expected equity upside into option-premium income. The income is real, but it comes with structural trade-offs: upside is capped above the strike, outcomes are path-dependent, and distributions may include return of capital (ROC) that reduces principal over time. This primer explains the basic mechanics, the main risk characteristics, and the implementation choices that drive results (such as option moneyness and reset frequency). We use simple payoff intuition and stylized NAV sketches, then contrast common U.S. products with UCITS variants to show how design differences matter in practice. The core message is practical: covered-call ETFs can play a role as income complements in diversified portfolios, especially in sideways markets with reasonably firm implied volatility, but they are generally unsuitable as long-term growth anchors. Investors should judge these funds on total return and the sustainability of distributions, not headline yield alone.

title: Exploring global, economy-wide material trajectories and associated environmental pressures under shared socioeconomic pathways
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Finland - Finnish Meteorological Institute, Government of the Republic of Finland - Finnish Environment Institute, Government of the Republic of Finland - Finnish Environment Institute, University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna and University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna

detail.title: Exploring global, economy-wide material trajectories and associated environmental pressures under shared socioeconomic pathways
detail.abstract: Material production is a major contributor to many environmental challenges, but has received limited attention in the global, long-term scenarios that investigate humankind's potential responses to them. Here, we aim to fill this gap by proposing a top-down approach for quantifying pathways of economy-wide material stocks and flows, based on the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) and the material stock intensity of the global economy. In addition to the SSPs, we hypothesize a scenario of low material demand (LMD) with modest economic growth and a strongly decreasing material stock intensity. The material stocks are then translated to production and waste flows through stock lifetime dynamics based on the MISO2 material-flow accounting model; and to environmental pressures, such as energy use, CO2 emissions and human appropriation of net primary production (HANPP) with the SuCCESs integrated assessment model. Halting the growth of material production and related environmental pressures requires modest economic growth (SSP3), possibly combined with strong decoupling of GDP and material stocks (LMD). The economy-wide material stocks grow in all scenarios-from a 55% increase between 2020 and 2100 in LMD, to a nine-fold increase in SSP5. Concomitantly, production volumes of major materials, e.g. steel and concrete, grow in all scenarios except LMD. Without active mitigation, the environmental impacts from material production continue to increase in all but the SSP3 and LMD scenarios, in which the impacts remain stable or decline even without deliberate action to reduce them. Conversely, with moderately or strongly growing GDP and only slightly declining material stock intensity, material production would grow immensely, requiring significant effort to mitigate the related environmental pressures. The exception for this is waste accumulation, which will continue to grow for at least several decades due to the inherent lag in material flow dynamics.

title: Private Firm, Traded Stock: The Case of Private Secondary Markets

detail.title: Private Firm, Traded Stock: The Case of Private Secondary Markets
detail.abstract: Why do startups increasingly choose to trade on private secondary markets (PSMs)? I examine the trade-offs associated with this decision and the characteristics of startups trading on PSMs. Using a recent regulatory change that expanded investor access to PSMs and drawing on novel startup share price data, I show that PSM-listed startups face higher fundraising uncertainty and typically experience declining share prices once listed. My results reveal a risk-return trade-off, in which startups accept increased financing risk for higher returns when fundraising succeeds and broad stock markets are supportive, benefiting from price discovery without foregoing private status.

title: A Replication and Robustness Check of the Centipede Game
affiliations: and University of Southampton

detail.title: A Replication and Robustness Check of the Centipede Game
detail.abstract: We replicate the classical centipede game of McKelvey and Palfrey (1992) and examine the effects of feedback regarding aggregate behavior. Our subjects exhibit Nash behaviour significantly more frequently than subjects in the original experiment, and aggregate feedback concerning opponent behavior induces stronger convergence to Nash equilibrium. However, following a slight modification to the payoff structure of final decision node, the treatment effects of aggregate information often shift in the opposite direction.

title: Purpose Projection How Teleology Shapes Decisions, Norms, and Power
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Purpose Projection How Teleology Shapes Decisions, Norms, and Power
detail.abstract: Humans are "teleology machines". From early childhood we default to reading purpose into the world, "for what is this?", and we carry that bias into morality, politics, science talk, and institutional life. This essay develops a unified theory: teleological perception is not a peripheral error but a primary cognitive stance that organizes self-narratives, social coordination, and the stabilization of large-scale institutions. We show how the intention heuristic-the felt transparency of our own will-encourages a systematic inversion of time's arrow: outcomes are treated as if they were prior purposes. I argue that "intention", in the sense often pursued in interpersonal and public interpretation, functions less as a cause and more as a teleological appearance, an after-the-fact story that a system tells about its own results. Building on evidence from developmental psychology, cognitive anthropology, and institutional theory, I propose a corrective method-Causal-First Reconstruction (CFR)-anchored by four criteria: continuity, counterfactuals, prediction, and correction. CFR reframes explanations from "what for" to "what from", without erasing lived meaning. The payoff is practical: cleaner diagnostics in interpersonal discourse, fewer institutional confusions (treating amplifiers as generators), and a research program that yields testable predictions about how causal language, when deliberately substituted for teleological framing, changes judgment, trust, and policy uptake.

title: Anti-Harassment Policy and the Startup Labor Market
affiliations: Southern Methodist University (SMU) - Finance Department,  and University of Illinois at Chicago

detail.title: Anti-Harassment Policy and the Startup Labor Market
detail.abstract: This paper examines how anti-harassment legal reforms that weaken non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) in cases of workplace sexual harassment affect startups' hiring and organizational decisions. Using a staggered difference-indifferences design and LinkedIn data on over 80,000 U.S. venture-capital-backed startups from 2014-2022, we find that NDA reforms, although intended for employee protection, reduce female hiring by about 7%, with effects concentrated among junior women, who are statistically more prone to sexual harassment, and in small or male-dominated startups. The results apply to both the intensive and extensive margins of hiring female workers. Treated entrepreneurial firms also witness more departures of male managers, promote more women, and receive less VC funding. These results suggest that while NDA-weakening laws increase firms' perceived legal risk and reduce female hiring, they also trigger internal restructuring that promotes women's advancement into leadership and may, over time, foster more accountable and inclusive organizational cultures.

title: Giving Eyes to Automated Valuation Models: Computer Vision Assessment of Interior Home Condition
affiliations: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) - NTNU Business School, NTNU Business School and Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) - NTNU Business School

detail.title: Giving Eyes to Automated Valuation Models: Computer Vision Assessment of Interior Home Condition
detail.abstract: Housing condition is a key determinant of property value, yet it is often omitted from automated valuation models (AVMs) due to inconsistent data and subjective measurement. This study develops a computer vision framework to assess interior condition at the room level from digital sales listings and evaluates its impact on valuation accuracy. Using 8,865 condominium transactions from Oslo, Norway (2022-2023) paired with listing images, we adopt a threephase approach: (i) automatic classification of images by room type (86% accuracy), (ii) roomspecific condition assessment on a 1-5 scale using tailored convolutional neural networks (>70% accuracy, with <3% large misclassifications), and (iii) integration of these condition measures into both hedonic linear regression and XGBoost AVMs. Including visual condition variables improves predictive performance, reducing RMSE by 0.5-0.6 percentage points. Both regression coefficients and explainable AI analysis confirm that higher room condition is positively associated with transaction prices, highlighting the potential of image-based assessments to enhance mass appraisal systems.

title: The Role of Domestic vs. Global Attention in Shaping Israeli Financial Markets During the 2023-2025 Israel-Palestine Conflict
affiliations: and Hellenic Mediterranean University, Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: The Role of Domestic vs. Global Attention in Shaping Israeli Financial Markets During the 2023-2025 Israel-Palestine Conflict

keywords: Principal Component Analysis JEL codes: G12

detail.abstract: This study examines how war-related public attention, measured via Google search data, influences Israeli financial markets during the 2023-2025 Israel-Palestine conflict. By distinguishing between domestic (Israeli) and global search trends, we assess their impact on equity (TA125) and bond (TA20) markets. To address high dimensionality and multicollinearity in search-based sentiment indicators, we apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Results show that domestic searches send mixed signals-sometimes stabilizing, sometimes destabilizing depending on the topic-while global searches consistently reflect a unified, conflict-focused sentiment with negative market effects. Although topic-level models occasionally yield better in-sample fits, PCA ensures greater stability and generalizability. This research contributes to behavioral finance by demonstrating that investor reactions to geopolitical crises are shaped not only by cognitive biases but also by the geographic framing of information. These findings offer key insights for investors and policymakers managing financial uncertainty amid armed conflict.

title: Systematic Variance Risk Everywhere in Equity Option Markets
affiliations: UNSW Business School, UNSW Business School, University of Houston - C.T. Bauer College of Business and HEC Montréal

detail.title: Systematic Variance Risk Everywhere in Equity Option Markets
detail.abstract: We propose systematic variance risk as the primary factor for pricing the cross-section of equity option returns. Using a parsimonious factor model with time-varying risk premiums, we find pervasive negative variance risk premiums in index, stock, and ETF options, consistent with asset pricing theory. The magnitudes of the risk premiums are plausible and similar across markets and the cross-section of options. This highlights the central and unifying role of systematic variance risk in option markets. We emphasize aspects of model specification and empirical implementation which play a critical role in establishing this stylized fact and explain differences with existing studies.

title: Multinomial Choice with Negative Externalities: A Note
affiliations: University of Cambridge, Trinity College and University of Cambridge

detail.title: Multinomial Choice with Negative Externalities: A Note
detail.abstract: We consider econometric settings of multinomial choice where a consumer's utility from choosing an alternative declines as a larger fraction of consumers choose it, e.g. commuting in rush-hour trains, applying to enrol in a popular university course with limited capacity, owning a high-end luxury good etc. We show that in such settings, the equilibrium is generically unique. This result requires no restriction on the functional form of utilities or on the dimension and distribution of unobserved preference heterogeneity across consumers, besides a no-ties assumption.

title: Praying for Inflation”: How Market Concentration Facilitates Inflationary Pressures.
affiliations: Northeastern University (USA) - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Praying for Inflation”: How Market Concentration Facilitates Inflationary Pressures.
detail.abstract: In this article, we propose a nuanced explanation connecting concentration and inflationary pressures. Drawing on oligopoly theory, behavioral factors, and infor- mation asymmetries, we argue that firms in concentrated industries may exploit economy-wide inflation as a pretext to raise prices beyond cost-justified levels. Gen- eral inflation provides legitimacy, coordination cues, and reduced scrutiny that lower the strategic risks of price increases. We discuss how this mechanism differs from standard pass-through and transitional explanations, provide anecdotal evidence from recent episodes, and outline an empirical framework—using variation in airline market concentration—to test this “pretextual inflation” hypothesis. The results have important implications for competition policy, suggesting that inflationary periods may warrant heightened vigilance toward concentrated markets.

title: Digital Public Infrastructure, the Building Blocks for Digital Financial Inclusion and Taxation of the Digital Economy in Liberia
affiliations: Wilmington University

detail.title: Digital Public Infrastructure, the Building Blocks for Digital Financial Inclusion and Taxation of the Digital Economy in Liberia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not Applicable
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not Applicable
declarations.funderStatement: Not Applicable.

keywords: digital ID and digital financial inclusion
digital payment system and digital financial inclusion
data exchange system and digital financial inclusion
Digital ID and taxation of the digital economy

detail.abstract: The digital era presents remarkable opportunities for the digital transformation of economies and an all-inclusive financial system. However, for Liberia, these prospects seem out of reach. The harsh reality of inconsistent, duplicated, siloed, and fragmented e-government service delivery, combined with the scarcity of resources, looms significantly over the country's digital transformation ambitions. Despite the positive outcomes, such as the amendment of the National Electronic Payment Switch (NEPS), the digitalization of the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA), e-Liberia service centre, coordination and empowerment of the National Identification Registry (NIR) and talks with N-Soft for governance digital solution over the years, the broader adoption of digital financial inclusion, and mobilization of tax revenue from the digital economy, remain a challenge for the government of Liberia. Nonetheless, Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) has emerged as a ray of hope to make Liberia's digital transformation journey a reality. Based on a conceptual review and critical analysis of literature, policy documents, and briefs from international organizations, this study examines the impact of the government of Liberia's development and implementation of digital public infrastructure on digital financial inclusion and the taxation of the digital economy in Liberia. The outcome of the review reveals that a wellbuilt, well-funded, secure, scalable, and interoperable digital public infrastructure layer, including digital ID, digital payments, and consent data exchange systems, will spur wider adoption of digital financial inclusion in Liberia and enhance the mobilization of domestic tax revenue from the digital economy. With DPI, Liberians can use a secure digital ID to open a bank account, connect payment systems to identity, and exchange verified data across service providers, thus accelerating digital financial inclusion in Liberia. In addition, linking digital ID, digital payments, and consent-based data sharing across the public and private sectors will boost tax compliance and enhance LRA capacity to collect lawful domestic tax revenue from the digital economy. Thus, by implementing an inclusive DPI, the government of Liberia can overcome some of its most entrenched challenges in its digital transformation journey, hindering the broader adoption of digital financial inclusion and the taxation of the digital economy in Liberia.

title: Worried About AI Monopoly? Embrace Copyright's Limits
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers Law School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Worried About AI Monopoly? Embrace Copyright's Limits

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Big Tech is in the crosshairs. Critiques reverberate on both sides of the aisle. Antitrust lawsuits abound. Privacy problems persist. And now, a new front has opened: copyright—specifically, the claim that Big Tech’s generative artificial intelligence (AI) infringes copyrighted works. Some observers have even applauded copyright enforcement and expansion as a vehicle to weaken Big Tech’s monopoly power.

Attempts to use copyright to pursue such “antimonopoly” goals, however, need to keep in mind copyright’s competition framework. Copyright is built on not just rights that benefit authors but also limits on those rights that benefit everyone. Focusing solely on the former not only is ineffective to attain these goals (given the size of the largest copyright owners) but also fails to exploit copyright’s competition-promoting tools in fostering a robust AI marketplace.

This short piece explores these issues in the context of AI training, shadow libraries, and news summaries.

title: Circular Organization of Economic Processes: Symmetric Model of Economic Equilibrium
affiliations: University of Georgia (Tbilisi)

detail.title: Circular Organization of Economic Processes: Symmetric Model of Economic Equilibrium
detail.abstract: On the basis of dialectical analysis of basic economic categories a new understanding of economic value, price formation and general equilibrium has been proposed. Market economy appears as the form of a complex, non-linear, functionally closed and causally open system of economic actions. Such systems have a number of unique properties that are well studied by second-order cybernetics. The self-organization of a market economy is carried out through the recursive processes. Recursive processes in the economic system, as well as in other complex nonlinear dynamical systems, generate "eigenvalues" ("fixed points"). These "eigenvalues" are the equilibrium prices and quantities of goods to which through the recursive processes tend the actual prices and quantities, thus providing a tendency to the general equilibrium. However, due to constant influence on the system of random external factors, the general equilibrium is never achieved. On the base of created model the hidden relationships among the gross profit, gross saving, gross investment and gross consumption in debt, as well as the relationships among the other economic parameters are revealed.

title: The Cost of US Reserve Currency Status: Term Structure of Convenience Premia via Model-Free Triangulation
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: The Cost of US Reserve Currency Status: Term Structure of Convenience Premia via Model-Free Triangulation
detail.abstract: We develop a model-free methodology to extract convenience premia, defined as differentials in expected term premiums across currencies, using triangular no-arbitrage relationships in cross-currency swap markets. Without parametric assumptions, we find USD systematically requires 16-42 basis points higher expected returns than EUR, JPY, and GBP at long maturities, indicating negative expected convenience despite reserve currency status. Extracted premia demonstrate strong predictive power of subsequent realized returns with R-squared values reaching 77% for ten-year horizons. These findings provide new empirical moments for international term structure models to match regarding expected term premiums. The model-free nature ensures these are robust stylized facts for understanding multi-currency portfolio allocation and risk management.

title: Neutralizing Market Risk with Backward and Forward Looking Betas
affiliations: University of New South Wales, University of Auckland Business School, University of Auckland Business School,  and UNSW Business School, University of New South Wales

detail.title: Neutralizing Market Risk with Backward and Forward Looking Betas

declarations.funderStatement: We gratefully acknowledge financial support from the University of Auckland’s Research Development Fund.

contentType.other: UNSW Business School working paper series

detail.abstract: In this paper we provide advances in the methodology of market neutral portfolio management through utilizing both backward and forward looking betas. Backward looking betas are computed from realized beta estimators with high frequency stock returns and forward looking betas are computed from option prices. Forecast combinations of both backward and forward looking betas are utilized in the portfolio management and we find improvements in the accuracy and robustness of targeting zero beta portfolios through this methodology, relative to standard approaches in practice. Economically significant improvements are demonstrated particularly during the volatility of the global financial crisis of 2008 and 2009.

title: Asset pricing anomalies: Comparative performance of CAPM, FF3FM, and FF5FM in the Indian equity market

detail.title: Asset pricing anomalies: Comparative performance of CAPM, FF3FM, and FF5FM in the Indian equity market
detail.abstract: This study evaluates asset pricing models in India, highlighting the superiority of the Fama-French Three-Factor Model over CAPM while questioning the added value of the Fama-French Five-Factor Model. The findings offer insights for investors and policymakers in portfolio management and asset allocation. The study evaluates and compares the performance of asset pricing models-Single-Factor Model of Sharpe and Linter, Three-Factor Model of Fama and French, and Five-Factor Model of Fama and French-on the Indian stock market. It employs the Fama-French methodology to analyze asset pricing. This paper uses four characteristics of a firm to test the market capitalization model for the size effect, the book-to-price ratio for the value effect, the net income to book equity ratio as a variable of profitability effect, and annual growth of total assets for the investment effect. Spanning nine years from July 1, 2012 to June 30, 2021, this study examines 64 companies from the NSE 100 index to analyze stock return dynamics. This study provides a comprehensive comparison of the three models using 18 (6 x 3) portfolios constructed based on size, value, profitability, and investment. The study found that the Fama-French Three-Factor Model, with an R² of 95.6%, outperformed the Capital Asset Pricing Model, which had an R² of 89.9%. Although the Fama-French Five-Factor Model achieved the highest R² of 95.8%, its improvement over FF3FM was minimal. This indicates that the inclusion of profitability and investment factors does not significantly enhance the model's ability to explain stock returns.

title: Beyond the Ballot Box: How Ranked Choice Voting Influences Campaigns and Voter Engagement The SPRING Group
affiliations: The SPRING Institute, The SPRING Institute, The SPRING Institute, The SPRING Institute, Frontlines Foundation, The SPRING Institute, The Perrin Research Institution, The SPRING Institute and The SPRING Institute

detail.title: Beyond the Ballot Box: How Ranked Choice Voting Influences Campaigns and Voter Engagement The SPRING Group
detail.abstract: Ranked Choice Voting, also known as RCV, is a voting system designed to allow voters to rank candidates in an election in order of preference. Overall, RCV increases electoral fairness and reduces the negative effects of strategic voting. This report examines the impact of RCV on election outcomes, campaign strategies, voter behavior, and policies. Today, RCV is used across 14 states, such as Alaska, Maine, and Hawaii. RCV minimizes wasted votes and the spoiler effect, allowing voters to show a ranking of preferences. Such a method often results in candidates with the broadest support winning elections and increases representation for more underrepresented candidates. Although RCV’s majority-wins strategy may seem an appreciable approach to voting, it still receives concerns from the public. To successfully implement RCV, a great deal of voter education and administration transparency is required. Policymakers must balance the fine line between RCV’s benefits of representation and its complexity. As political polarization continues to create discrepancies in our electoral systems, RCV offers a potential solution to leverage voting fairness and representation.

title: Beyond Democratic Assumptions: Altruism, Political Citizenship and State-Society Relations in Contemporary China
affiliations: University of Alberta - Department of Political Science, London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Social Policy and Administration and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Beyond Democratic Assumptions: Altruism, Political Citizenship and State-Society Relations in Contemporary China
detail.abstract: This study challenges democratic citizenship theory by examining altruistic behaviour in authoritarian China. We find that financial resources influence prosocial engagement primarily through psychological mediators such as long-term planning and self-discovery, rather than directly providing material means for participation. Communist Party membership shapes specific domestic ideological orientations, but not attitudes toward market regulation or income equality, while cultural tradition emerges as a stronger predictor of certain political attitudes than party affiliation. Cluster analysis identifies three distinct citizen profiles: (1) future-oriented altruists; (2) status-driven contributors; and, (3) short-term pragmatists, revealing motivational heterogeneity within authoritarian publics. These findings suggest that authoritarian citizenship operates through psychological mediation and plural motivational pathways fundamentally different from democratic societies, with potential applicability to other single-party regimes where states actively structure prosocial behaviour. The study contributes to comparative authoritarianism literature by theorizing how regime type moderates the relationship between socio-economic resources, political identity, and civic engagement.

title: FROM INFORMATION TO COLLAPSE: THE DYNAMICS OF SUBSECTORS
affiliations: Purdue University

detail.title: FROM INFORMATION TO COLLAPSE: THE DYNAMICS OF SUBSECTORS
detail.abstract: This paper develops a general theory of equilibrium formation under imperfect information within a discrete choice framework. Firms choose product characteristics that shape both the mean and variance of perceived utility, and informational frictions cause the economy to partition into subsectors-clusters of firms whose beliefs and market shares evolve together. These cluster equilibria capture how limited precision generates persistence, asymmetry, and collective adjustment in differentiated markets. Financial conditions influence this structure through their effect on equity and adjustment capacity: shifts in interest rates or funding costs alter how clusters reorganize, amplifying instability when firms within a subsector respond collectively to financial stress. The framework thus links informational and financial imperfections to the emergence and fragility of real market structures. Finally, the analysis shows that coordinated policy instruments-particularly interest rate adjustments and targeted taxes-can modulate these adjustment dynamics, indirectly stabilizing cluster behavior and reducing the risk of systemic collapse without constraining competitive efficiency.

title: Causal Recreation Demand Estimation with Cellphone Mobility Data: Evidence from the 2021 Huntington Beach Oil Spill
affiliations: China University of Petroleum-Beijing and

detail.title: Causal Recreation Demand Estimation with Cellphone Mobility Data: Evidence from the 2021 Huntington Beach Oil Spill

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Illinois-Indiana Sea Grant, Award Number NA22OAR4170654-T1-01.

detail.abstract: Accurately estimating the welfare impacts of environmental changes in recreation demand modeling requires robust causal inference methods. However, a persistent challenge remains as the zero market share issue restricts the causal inference application to broader regions and longer periods. To address this, we integrate empirical Bayes posterior mean estimation into a two-step random coefficient logit model, ensuring that sites with low or zero visitation are properly incorporated without distorting demand estimates. We apply this framework to the 2021 Huntington Beach oil spill, using high-frequency cellphone data to track changes in beach visits. By combining the Synthetic Difference-in-Differences (SDID) approach with empirical Bayes-adjusted market shares, we examine the causal effects of temporary beach closures on visitor welfare. Our findings reveal that Huntington Beach experienced the largest and most prolonged welfare loss, with an estimated aggregate loss of $1.0 million and weekly losses of $83 thousand persisting beyond the initial closure. In contrast, Newport Beach and Laguna Beach exhibited faster recoveries. This study advances recreation demand modeling by refining demand estimation for low-visit sites and strengthening causal inference techniques for environmental disruptions, ultimately providing a more reliable framework for assessing the economic costs of beach closures and other environmental policy interventions.

title: DELAYS IN PUBLIC PAYMENTS AND MARKET FAILURES IN COLOMBIA
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: DELAYS IN PUBLIC PAYMENTS AND MARKET FAILURES IN COLOMBIA
detail.abstract: This article analyzes, from an economic and development perspective, the effects of delayed payments from the public sector to contractors when completed works are not paid for within the corresponding fiscal year. Using a mixed-methods approach, with hypothetical simulations based on real-world precedents, it examines how these delays, recorded as accounts payable in subsequent budgets, affect business liquidity, labor stability, and market equilibrium. It demonstrates that payment delays generate a multiplier effect of nonpayments, reduce consumption, disrupt production planning, and foster inflationary pressures due to the pentup demand in the money supply. This study aims to provide a pedagogical perspective for understanding how inefficiencies in public payments can lead to structural market failures that undermine productivity and social welfare.

title: Regulating Plastic Bags: Evidence from China's Supermarket Industry
affiliations: National University of Singapore - NUS Business School, Renmin University of China, Institute of Real Estate and Urban Studies, National University of Singapore and Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU)

detail.title: Regulating Plastic Bags: Evidence from China's Supermarket Industry
detail.abstract: Using monthly panel data tracking individuals' carbon footprints, this study examines the causal impact of a plastic restriction policy in China that bans non-degradable plastic bags and mandates their replacement with biodegradable alternatives that cost 67% to 167% more. Following implementation, residents in treated cities are on average 2.21 percentage points (52.5%) more likely to forgo purchasing plastic bags relative to comparable controls. The effect emerges gradually but persists, stabilizing at 5.1 percentage points (121%) one year after the policy takes effect. The effect cannot be explained by other concurrent events, and the policy does not significantly affect consumption expenditure. Consistent with an environmental consciousness mechanism, consumers with higher pre-policy environmental awareness exhibit larger and faster reductions in plastic bag usage. Extrapolated nationally, the policy could reduce annual plastic bag consumption by approximately 204,000 tons-equivalent to about 30 billion medium-sized bags.

title: Open-Economy Dimensions of Monetary Policy in the WAMZ: Evidence from a Bayesian Dynamic Multivariate Panel Model
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria, Bank of Sierra Leone, Bank of Sierra Leone and Bank of Sierra Leone

detail.title: Open-Economy Dimensions of Monetary Policy in the WAMZ: Evidence from a Bayesian Dynamic Multivariate Panel Model
detail.abstract: This study examines the monetary policy behaviour of West African Monetary Zone (WAMZ) central banks using annual data from 1995 to 2024, estimated through a Bayesian Dynamic Multivariate Panel Model. Within the frameworks of the Traditional and Augmented Taylor rules, the analysis evaluates how policy rates respond to inflation, output, and open-economy factors. The results show strong interest rate smoothing, modest reactions to inflation, and limited responsiveness to output across member states. External variables, crude oil price and exchange rates, exert only marginal and uneven influences. Robustness checks using non-informative priors confirm that these patterns are driven by the data rather than prior specification. The findings indicate partial but incomplete convergence in monetary reaction functions across the WAMZ. To strengthen readiness for monetary integration, the study recommends deeper policy coordination, gradual adoption of forward-looking inflation-targeting frameworks, and improved management of external buffers. Future work should incorporate time-varying Bayesian models to capture evolving policy dynamics.

title: Municipal-level Gender Norms: Measurement and Effects on Women in Politics
affiliations: and

detail.title: Municipal-level Gender Norms: Measurement and Effects on Women in Politics
detail.abstract: We study the implications of traditional gender norms for legislators' engagement with women's issues. We leverage rich data from Facebook on the popularity of gender-related interests (processed using machine learning algorithms) to develop a granular Gender Norms Index (GNI) at the municipal level within Italy, a geographical resolution that would otherwise be unavailable. After validating our index, we leverage this local variation in norms to isolate their impact on legislators' policy activity in the Italian Parliament. We show that while female legislators generally sponsor more gender-related bills than their male counterparts, their engagement is substantially smaller if they were born in a gender-conservative town. This result persists even when comparing legislators within the same party, constituency or with similar characteristics. The absence of such a systematic impact on non-gender legislation further reinforces the causal interpretation of our estimates. Supplementary evidence on voting behavior suggests that traditional gender norms also negatively affect the passage of pro-equality legislation. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of social norms and sexist culture in lawmaking, thereby slowing down reform for the expansion of women's rights.

reference: This paper was accepted to Operations Research.
title: You Are the Best Reviewer of Your Own Papers: The Isotonic Mechanism

detail.title: You Are the Best Reviewer of Your Own Papers: The Isotonic Mechanism

publicationDetails.detailsText: This paper was accepted to Operations Research.

detail.abstract:
Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) conferences including NeurIPS and ICML have experienced a significant decline in peer review quality in recent years. To address this growing challenge, we introduce the Isotonic Mechanism, a computationally efficient approach to enhancing the accuracy of noisy review scores by incorporating authors' private assessments of their submissions. Under this mechanism, authors with multiple submissions are required to rank their papers in descending order of perceived quality. Subsequently, the raw review scores are calibrated based on this ranking to produce adjusted scores. We prove that authors are incentivized to truthfully report their rankings because doing so maximizes their expected utility, modeled as an additive convex function over the adjusted scores. Moreover, the adjusted scores are shown to be more accurate than the raw scores, with improvements being particularly significant when the noise level is high and the author has many submissions---a scenario increasingly prevalent at large-scale ML/AI conferences.

We further investigate whether submission quality information beyond a simple ranking can be truthfully elicited from authors. We establish that a necessary condition for truthful elicitation is that the mechanism be based on pairwise comparisons of the author's submissions. This result underscores the optimality of the Isotonic Mechanism, as it elicits the most fine-grained truthful information among all mechanisms we consider. We then present several extensions, including a demonstration that the mechanism maintains truthfulness even when authors have only partial rather than complete information about their submission quality. Finally, we discuss future research directions, focusing on the practical implementation of the mechanism and the further development of a theoretical framework inspired by our mechanism.

title: Public Communication in Regime Change games *
affiliations: and London Business School

detail.title: Public Communication in Regime Change games *
detail.abstract: We study a regime change game in which the state and an opposition leader both observe the regime's true strength and may engage in costly communication by manipulating the mean of citizens' private signals. Each citizen then decides whether to attack the regime; the citizens take their private signals at face value and do not discount or attempt to undo propaganda or counter-propaganda. From the perspective of both the state and the opposition, the size of the attack is uncertain, as the number of committed partisans-those who always attack regardless of their signal-is not observed in advance. We show that a regime on the brink of collapse optimally refrains from propaganda, while the opposition engages in counter-propaganda. The equilibrium level of counter-propaganda increases with the opposition's benefit-cost ratio and with the precision of citizens' private signals, and decreases with the cost of attacking.

title: Forecast of Compute Platform Development
affiliations: goldennanox

detail.title: Forecast of Compute Platform Development
detail.abstract: Based on learning-curve economics and architectural performance models, this paper systematically reviews and forecasts the coupling trends of form factor, cost, energy efficiency, and performance for future artificial intelligence (AI) compute platforms. The discussion centers on the following four faithful innovation points: (1) the desktop-integrated end state: a single desktop device completes mainstream training/fine-tuning/inference; (2) the key engineering constraint that system power does not exceed 1 kW ; (3) in an extremely aggressive scenario, unit cost decreases by two orders of magnitude per year and unit-time performance increases by two orders of magnitude per year; (4) HBM-integrated matrix processors (near-memory compute + high-bandwidth memory collaboration) become the main route to break through the bandwidth wall and energy wall. We model cost evolution with the Wright learning curve and analyze the compute-bandwidth upper bound with the Roofline model, proposing a four-in-one co-design principle-"Compute-Memory-Thermal-Compiler"-and a time roadmap.

title: The Dao of the DAO: Eastern Philosophies in Decentralized Worlds
affiliations: New York University Shanghai and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: The Dao of the DAO: Eastern Philosophies in Decentralized Worlds
detail.abstract: In chapter 62 of Daodejing, Laozi describes the Dao as "the hearth and home of the ten thousand things. Good souls treasure it, lost souls find shelter in it." Contemporary DAOs are often framed within Western discourses of decentralization, autonomy, and Web 3.0 innovation. However, emerging practices-especially in Chinese-speaking communities-reveal a distinctive layer of cultural imagination deeply rooted in Eastern thought. This research proposes to understand DAOs from Eastern philosophies by examining how Daoist principles inform the values and practices of DAO communities in Asia to articulate alternative visions of autonomy, community, and social organization. Concepts such as wú-wéi (non-action) and xiāo-yáo (carefree wandering) are increasingly referenced in the context of blockchain governance in the East. Using SeeDAO, a prominent DAO in the Chinese-speaking Web3 space, as a focal point, this study will explore how concepts such as non-action governance, the "Dao follows nature", and "emergence" are operationalized in digital governance practices. The research seeks to make three key contributions: first, to elucidate the lived experiences and ethical visions of DAO participants in China; second, to provide a culturally grounded theory of decentralized governance rooted in Eastern philosophical paradigms; and third, to explore how ancient philosophical ideas find renewed life in emergent socio-technical forms.

title: Commitment Fields: Risk, Meaning, and Constraint Why LLM Weights Encode Absence
affiliations: My Digital Truth

detail.title: Commitment Fields: Risk, Meaning, and Constraint Why LLM Weights Encode Absence
detail.abstract: This paper argues that large language models (LLMs) do not generate output through probabilistic prediction in the conventional sense. Instead, they operate as constraint resolution systems in a highdimensional, curved representational space. Tokens function as anchors that partition semantic possibility, while model weights encode the boundary conditions that govern which continuations remain coherent. Each output token is therefore not the result of temporal inference, but the collapse of a coherence field reconstructed at every step. This framework clarifies why LLMs can produce structured, contextually appropriate language without possessing goals, memory, or self-reference. It also provides a general computational analogy to biological cognition, where stable identity emerges from dynamic realignment rather than stored propositions. I further reframe risk management as the relational asymmetry between commitments operating under shared constraints, rather than as probabilistic forecasting or exogenous uncertainty. Finally, the paper shows how this constraint geometry relates to institutional and legal systems that maintain coherence under commitments, and explains why misunderstanding LLMs as agents leads to conceptual and regulatory errors.

title: INCREASING IMPORTATION OF RICE IN GHANA: CAN THE COUNTRY TRANSFORM ITS FORTUNES IN THE RICE SECTOR? Institute for Fiscal Studies
affiliations: Institute for Fiscal Studies, Ghana

detail.title: INCREASING IMPORTATION OF RICE IN GHANA: CAN THE COUNTRY TRANSFORM ITS FORTUNES IN THE RICE SECTOR? Institute for Fiscal Studies
detail.abstract: Importation of rice has been a serious issue of concern for the government of Ghana since the 1960s, due to its balance of payments, exchange rate, and food security implications. Therefore, over the years, the government has pursued a number of strategies to stem it. Yet, not only do data reveal that the strategies have failed to curtail it, but they also reveal that rice importation has accelerated in recent years, making it assume alarming proportions. This is because, even though the government is generally aware of the challenges facing the country’s rice sector, we find in this paper that the government’s strategies are not appropriate enough to address the fundamentals of the problem. Simply put, we find that there has been a policy failure in the country’s rice sector because the policies the government of Ghana has pursued in the sector are ill-suited. Methodologically, we have compared, in this paper, Ghana with Thailand and Vietnam, two major successful players in the global rice industry, in terms of the dynamics of rice import, production, and consumption. We have also examined the fundamental factors that have affected these dynamics. Additionally, we have analyzed the policies that have been pursued by the respective governments of these countries to address the fundamental factors affecting the performance of the rice sectors in these countries. These have provided us with a strong empirical understanding of the performance of Ghana’s rice sector and its underlying factors in comparative terms. They have also enabled us to identify the weaknesses in the government of Ghana’s policies towards the sector. Armed with these insights, we have provided recommendations, which, if adopted by the government, will not only successfully address the issue of increasing rice importation, but they will also lead to a positive transformation of the country’s rice sector, making Ghana become a major net exporter of rice.

title: Identity versus Economics?
affiliations: Ahmedabad University

detail.title: Identity versus Economics?
detail.abstract:
When does identity politics become more important than economic issues in democracies?
How does identity politics spread? What incentivises identity politics? In this paper we try to
model the society’s dilemma of ‘politics over identity’ versus ‘politics over economics’.
In a static model with bi-party democracy, two Downsian parties who are purely office seekers,
compete over two dimensions- economy and identity. There are two types of behavioral voters
in the economy, viz. the economic and the swing voters. Economic voters’ support is based on
the parties’ economic performances and their own exogenous ideological preferences for the
parties. Swing voters support on the basis of both economic performance and identity
propaganda, depending on the campaigns. The economic voter’s political decision is modeled
as per the standard probabilistic voting framework. They make their voting decisions based on
the parties’ economic performances and relative popularity. The parties campaign on identity
dimension by optimally allocating their electoral resources, thereby creating a polarization of
identities. Swing voters observe a noisy signal about the polarization, modeled by Global
Games. They infer the true state of polarization from their observed signal, and take their voting
decisions by comparing the economic and identity-based pay-offs. Lastly, elections take place
and the utilities are realized.
We find that when costs are the same, both parties engage in the same level of identity politics,
irrespective of their economic performance. It implies an economically well performed party may
engage in high identity politics too. An increase in the size of swing voters lowers the spending
on identity politics. An increase in the ideological spectrum of economic voters also discourages
identity politics. But competition among the political parties on the economic dimension is
increasing identity politics.
In a summary, this paper attempts to explain how and when identity politics can supersede
economic issues and potentially solves the puzzle why sometimes economically well performing
parties engage in high identity politics too.

title: Geopolitics, Geoeconomics and Risk: A Machine Learning  Approach
affiliations: BBVA Research and BBVA Research

detail.title: Geopolitics, Geoeconomics and Risk: A Machine Learning  Approach
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel high-frequency daily panel dataset of both markets and news-based indicatorsincluding Geopolitical Risk, Economic Policy Uncertainty, Trade Policy Uncertainty and Political Sentiment-for 42 countries across both emerging and developed markets. Using this dataset, we study how sentiment dynamics shape sovereign risk, measured by Credit Default Swap (CDS) spreads, and evaluate their forecasting value relative to traditional drivers such as global monetary policy and market volatility. Our horse-race analysis of forecasting models demonstrates that incorporating news-based indicators significantly enhances predictive accuracy and enrich the analysis, with nonlinear machine learning methods-particularly Random Forests-delivering the largest gains. Our analysis reveals that while global financial variables remain the dominant drivers of sovereign risk, geopolitical risk and economic policy uncertainty also play a meaningful role. Crucially, their effects are amplified through non-linear interactions with global financial conditions. Finally, we document pronounced regional heterogeneity, as certain asset classes and emerging markets exhibit heightened sensitivity to shocks in policy rates, global financial volatility, and geopolitical risk.

title: Instrumentalizing Industrial Policy for GDP Manipulation
affiliations: ,  Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) and

detail.title: Instrumentalizing Industrial Policy for GDP Manipulation
detail.abstract: China’s performance-based cadre evaluation system creates incentives for local officials to manipulate economic statistics. We demonstrate that officials instrumentalize industrial policy as a novel, indirect channel for this purpose. Using LLM analysis of 4.29 million policy documents (2013–2024) across 328 cities, we identify 403,240 industrial policies and show that officials leverage them to inflate GDP statistics far more than real economic activity. Such manipulation is more prevalent among older, longer-tenured, and performance-stressed officials, and in state-owned sectors and less-developed cities. While boosting short-run statistics, it undermines long-run economic dynamism by reducing firm entry and increasing exit.

title: Policy of the European Union in the Field of Healthcare
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Interregional Academy of Personnel Management, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shupyk National Healthcare University of Ukraine and Shupyk National Healthcare University of Ukraine

detail.title: Policy of the European Union in the Field of Healthcare

publicationDetails.detailsText: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development, 18 (12), 303-414, 2025.
publicationDetails.journalName: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development

detail.abstract: In this study were analyzed healthcare provision, health needs meeting 'state-of-the-art', as well as healthcare policies and frameworks throughout the EU space. In particular, some implications of COVID-19 crisis were examined. Based on the method of thematic analysis, authors conducted a review of both scholarly publications and EU policy documents and reports. This allowed to trace patterns of health policies formation and their effects in healthcare field, including addressing health inequalities, staff shortage, and other acute current issues. The factor of trust and quality of institutions was also taken into account, demonstrating that non-data-related issues might be overlooked aspects of health inequality monitoring. As the result of conducted analysis, authors suggested the capability maturity model, describing the levels of nation-state' healthcare system overall capability in face of the current challenges.

title:
Transition Risk as Investment Risk Signal
Quantifying Transition Shortfalls in European Equities: An Emissions Gap and Carbon-Price Exposure Approach
affiliations: IE Business School, International University of Monaco (IUM), EDHEC Business School, Panthera Solutions and

detail.title:
Transition Risk as Investment Risk Signal
Quantifying Transition Shortfalls in European Equities: An Emissions Gap and Carbon-Price Exposure Approach
detail.abstract:
