Climate transition risk is an increasing part of financial analysis. This white paper prescribes an open and reproducible methodology that projects company emissions, simulates forward-looking scenarios against a company-agnostic 2050 net-zero benchmark, and values resulting exposures under EU carbon price assumptions.

Used for European equities, the system generates a ranking of firms by modeled exposure per euro of sales, which is an unambiguous and comparable metric of relative transition pressure. The analysis does not forecast regulatory penalties, nor does it forecast investment returns. Instead, it models realistic costs exposures under carbon-price trajectories, conditioned on historical emission trajectories.

Positioned within the broader study of Panthera Solutions (PS) on investment decision intelligence, the PS model depicts how scenario tools can help investors compare firms' relative degree of exposure to transition risks and where additional qualitative analysis — such as sectoral dynamics, commitment credibility, or investment plans — would be best applied.

title: Farm to Fridge: Digital Traceability and Quality Upgrading in the Kenyan Dairy Value Chain
affiliations: University of California, Santa Cruz

detail.title: Farm to Fridge: Digital Traceability and Quality Upgrading in the Kenyan Dairy Value Chain
detail.abstract: Disorganized agricultural value chains often prevent the transmission of quality incentives to upstream farmers, especially when quality is costly to observe at the farm gate. This study develops digital traceability systems for Kenyan dairy cooperatives and introduces an innovative quality monitoring method, using Bayesian statistical models to infer individual milk quality from pooled samples and reduce testing costs. I reveal randomly selected farmers' milk quality either by the model or by random tests to both cooperatives and farmers. I find that the farmers in the model group reduce the added water by a significant 21.9% compared to the control group, while the farmers in the random test group show an insignificant 12.6% reduction. In addition, treated farmers who consistently provide high-quality milk receive higher credit limits from the cooperative and use more credit for animal feed. A back-of-the-envelope calculation suggests that the model offers cost-effective quality improvement, making it a promising tool for continuous quality monitoring and scalable implementation.

title: THE EVOLUTION OF PAIRS TRADING by Michael V. Blumeyer
affiliations: Blumeyer Investment Partners

detail.title: THE EVOLUTION OF PAIRS TRADING by Michael V. Blumeyer
detail.abstract:
Pairs trading is an equity market-neutral strategy that employs a comparative framework, wherein the product of one security’s beta, market price, and position size is algebraically equated to that of its counterpart to determine the optimal offsetting quantity. In contemporary hedge fund practice, the statistical arbitrage opportunities inherent in pairs trading have become a foundational tool for portfolio diversification and relative value exploitation. Some practitioners extend this framework intersectorally, juxtaposing securities across disparate industries—to uncover robust correlations or stable pairs ratios that may yield above-average profit potential, even when the underlying economic drivers are only partially understood.

This paper investigates the differential outcomes between dollar-neutral and beta-neutral portfolio constructions, tracing the intellectual lineage and institutional adoption of these methodologies among major U.S. asset management firms. Subsequently, we illustrate an applied case using current market data, providing a quantitative walkthrough for determining position weights under a beta-neutral mandate. Finally, we identify salient internal and external risk factors—ranging from firm-level operational exposures to competitive market dynamics—and conclude with recommendations for risk mitigation and alpha preservation within contemporary pairs trading frameworks.

title: Al-Maqrizi: The Most Prominent Historian and Economist in Egypt's History
affiliations: Cairo University

detail.title: Al-Maqrizi: The Most Prominent Historian and Economist in Egypt's History
detail.abstract: There are scholars who created civilizations or contributed to human civilization. Among them is Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, who authored a vast encyclopedia interpreting the noble Hadith over twenty years, Al-Maqrizi, the sheikh of historians who is credited with much of what we know about Islamic Egypt, and Ibn Khaldun, the founder of sociology, among others. Most scholars, politicians, rulers, and even soldiers in the Islamic era were not Egyptian by birth from both parents; many acquired Egyptian nationality, similar to how it happens today in the United States, Canada, or Europe through naturalization. Back then, everyone lived within one vast state, whether Egypt was part of the Abbasid Caliphate, the Fatimid Caliphate, or the Mamluk Sultanate. Today, some countries compete to claim the legacy of medieval scholars-for example, the tomb of Ibn Sina (Avicenna), the most prominent physician, lies in Iran, and his image was featured on the Tajik Samani 20-currency note. Al-Maqrizi (764-845 AH / 1364-1442 CE) He was an Egyptian, born and died in Cairo. His full name was Taqi al-Din Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Abdul-Qadir al-Maqrizi. His family origins traced back to Syria, specifically Lebanon, while his mother was Egyptian. He was born in Harat Barjawan in the Darb al-Sa'ada district, where he grew up, was educated, and always took pride in belonging to his neighborhood. Al-Maqrizi held political opinions that cost him dearly. He criticized the corruption of the Mamluks, their deviation from the righteous path, and their shortsighted greed, which led to enrichment at the expense of Egypt's agricultural and trade stability. He was the most prominent student of Ibn Khaldun, the founder of the science of civilization (sociology). Al-Maqrizi became the chief of Arab and Egyptian historians. His legacy was like a media and scientific institution, documenting a very important period of Islamic Egypt's history. Although modern media did not exist at that time, Al-Maqrizi functioned as a one-man institution that chronicled events comprehensively. He discussed economic theories centuries before modern scholars-ideas for which others later won Nobel Prizes. In his famous work Al-Khitat al-Maqriziya he described Egypt as: "Egypt is my birthplace, the playground of my companions, the gathering of my people, the abode of my clan and family, and the home that nurtured me. Since my youth, when God granted me intelligence and understanding, I desired to know its news and loved to observe its wells of knowledge."-Key Scientific and Practical Contributions of Al-Maqrizi-The Father of Monetary Economics: He was among the first to analyze economic crises, inflation, and prices, linking them to monetary policy. He was the first to connect monetary policies and economic fluctuations (crises and recessions), particularly during the Black Death that devastated Egypt and claimed his son's life.-His Works: * Al-Mawa'iz wa al-I'tibar bi Dhikr al-Khitat wa al-Athar (known as Al-Khitat al-Maqriziya), the most important historical reference on Islamic Egypt, detailing Cairo's neighborhoods, population, economy, politics, rulers, and more. * Ighathat al-Ummah bi-Kashf al-Ghummah (Relief of the Nation in Exposing the Crisis), diagnosing Egypt's crises and their causes. * Al-Kayl wa al-Mizan al-Shar'iya (Weights and Measures in Shari'a). * Shudhūr al-'Uqūd fi Dhikr al-Nuqud (Fragments on Currency), a treatise on Islamic coins.-Public Service: In 801 AH (1398 CE), he was appointed Muhtasib (market inspector) of Cairo and Lower Egypt, a highly significant role through which he closely observed Egypt's economic, social, and political conditions, later recording them in his writings.-Economic Analysis: He studied monetary phenomena, crises, and their causessome political (corruption of governance), others economic (rising production costs, excessive money supply). He argued crises were primarily due to corruption in government and mismanagement, which increased food prices and poverty.-Policy Proposals: He proposed minting coins only from precious metals (gold or silver) to limit monetary supply and maintain value, excluding copper as it destabilized circulation. He stressed silver had intrinsic commodity value beyond its nominal monetary role, leading many to melt it for alternative uses.

title: The Effect of Managers’ Mix of Real and Accrual-Based Earnings Management on Future Performance
affiliations: Virginia Commonwealth University, Vanderbilt University and University of North Carolina at Greensboro

detail.title: The Effect of Managers’ Mix of Real and Accrual-Based Earnings Management on Future Performance

contentType.other: Forthcoming, Journal of Business Finance and Accounting

detail.abstract: Prior research finds that firms use both accrual-based earnings management (AEM) and real earnings management (REM) to manage financial reporting outcomes and that each practice influences firm performance. We extend this research by examining how managers' choices regarding the mix of AEM and REM relates to future performance. We argue that the sequential nature of the two earnings management strategies, as suggested by Zang (2012), constrains managers' ability to obtain a mix of AEM and REM that minimizes the total cost of earnings management, leading to weaker future performance. Consistent with this argument, we find evidence of deviations from the mix of AEM that would be expected based only on their costs: (1) resulting in future earnings and cash flows that are lower than the firm's historical performance, and (2) being significantly negatively associated with future buy-and-hold abnormal returns. We find similar results using commonly used measures of earnings management and recently refined measures designed to capture opportunistic earnings manipulation. Our evidence indicates that deviations from the mix of AEM and REM expected based on their relative costs are costly to firms regardless of whether managers' intent is to inform or to mislead financial statement users.

title: Stock Market Index Dynamics and Rough Volatility
affiliations: University of Technology, Sydney (UTS) - Finance Discipline Group and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Stock Market Index Dynamics and Rough Volatility
detail.abstract: The paper proposes a realistic, parsimonious, highly tractable model for the dynamics of a stock market index. The normalized index evolves in market time as a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process of dimension four. The derivative of the market time is modeled as a linear function of the squared derivative of an exponential moving average of a proxy of the Brownian motion driving the stock index. The index volatility evolves in market time as a solution of a system of stochastic differential equations. When observing the index volatility in calendar time, significant moves of the driving Brownian motion generate accelerated market time and volatility spikes, and the volatility appears to be rough. The model explains well the S&P500 dynamics and allows the extraction of the trajectories of the model volatility and the driving Brownian motion.

title: Digitalisation, Social Media and Bank Deposit Dynamics: Evidence from the Recent Euro Area Monetary Tightening
affiliations: Central Bank of Ireland, European Systemic Risk Board and Central Bank of Malta

detail.title: Digitalisation, Social Media and Bank Deposit Dynamics: Evidence from the Recent Euro Area Monetary Tightening
detail.abstract: This study sheds light on the impact of digitalisation and social media on deposit flows and rates of euro area banks during the recent period of monetary tightening. Drawing on difference-indifferences analysis of confidential monthly data of deposit flows and rates as well as measures of bank digitalisation and social media exposure through Twitter sentiment, the study offers two novel sets of findings. First, banks with a higher degree of digitalisation exhibit larger fluctuations in deposits, with higher inflows from mid-2020 to early 2022 but greater outflows in response to the tightening. Digitalisation is also correlated with higher sensitivity of banks' NFC deposit rates to policy rates. Second, a negative Twitter sentiment reduces deposit inflows, even after * Disclaimer: The views presented in this paper are those of the authors' only, and do not represent those of the ESRB, ECB, Central Bank of Malta or their member institutions. We would like to thank Magnus Andersson, Vasso Ioannidou, Kristine Petrovska, Jonathan Rice, and Antonio Sanchez Serrano for useful comments, and Arthur Campos for outstanding research assistance. We also thank the participants of the Research Workshop of the MPAG-AWG (ECB and ESRB) including Jan Klacso for his discussion. Any error is our own responsibility. † Contacts: Raffaele Giuliana, Central Bank of Ireland and European Systemic Risk Board, raf

title: Carbon Accounting for Contracting
affiliations: Peking University - Guanghua School of Management,  and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Carbon Accounting for Contracting
detail.abstract: We propose an innovative, accrual-based carbon accounting system designed to facilitate efficient contracting. In addition to accurately measuring firms' total carbon emissions, our system emphasizes the generation of performance indicators that facilitate incentive alignment, monitoring, and governance. We argue that such indicators enable stakeholders to promote systematic carbon reduction through contractual mechanisms. Compared to existing frameworks, our system expands the scope of measurement, allocates supply chain emissions more equitably, reduces susceptibility to manipulation, and improves accuracy by accounting for carbon removals and the time value of carbon emissions. The resulting statements can be applied in internal performance evaluation, debt contracts, and supply chain agreements, thereby incentivizing firms to reduce emissions both within the organizations and across their value chains. We demonstrate the feasibility and informativeness of our system through a case study with Foxconn Industrial Internet Co., Ltd., in which we generate and analyze the firm's carbon statements.

title: Corporate Emissions Target Announcements: Credibility and Market Reaction
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Department of Accounting, University of California, Berkeley - Haas School of Business and Harvard University - Business School (HBS)

detail.title: Corporate Emissions Target Announcements: Credibility and Market Reaction
detail.abstract: We study stock market reactions to corporate announcements of emissions reduction targets. Using generative AI to screen news headlines, we identify 2,417 emissions target announcements from 2006 to 2023 and document three main findings. First, target announcements are associated with negative stock price reactions on average but with significant variations. Second, firms with more credible disclosures—those with higher environmental scores, reasonable assurance of emissions data, and a longer history of emissions reporting—receive more negative reactions. Third, firms with more negative market reactions subsequently reduce their emissions intensity more, consistent with the market correctly anticipating firms that will engage in costly decarbonization efforts. We identify two reasons why firms set targets and follow through despite negative market reactions: (i) benefits are realized later, as seen in less negative market reactions when climate regulation materializes; and (ii) ESG-linked pay incentivizes target announcement and subsequent decarbonization. Our findings shed light on how market values voluntary climate commitments.

title: Tenure, Accountability and Electoral Selection: Evidence from Italy

detail.title: Tenure, Accountability and Electoral Selection: Evidence from Italy
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of a 2014 reform that extended term limits for mayors of Italian towns with population under 3,000 residents, transitioning from two to three consecutive terms. Exploiting the fact that the reform was not anticipated by incumbent second-term mayors, I estimate separately three main channels through which this policy shift may have impacted local government performance: mayors' tenure, electoral accountability, and electoral selection. My results indicate that the overall effect of the reform on voters' welfare was negative. In particular, I uncover a negative tenure effects in the speed of payments in investment spending and in the supply of general administrative service. Specifically, third-term mayors exhibit a decline in performance compared to their second-term. A possible explanation for this performance drop is a decrease in motivation that arise during the concluding stretch of extended tenures as mayor of a small municipality. In such contexts, the mayor's job tend to become repetitive and less engaging over time. My findings can be of relevance for policymakers contemplating similar reforms for small subnational local governments.

title: Financing the Green Transition of "Brown" Sectors
affiliations: Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business, National Taipei University, Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business, Central University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai Dianji University and Singapore Management University

detail.title: Financing the Green Transition of "Brown" Sectors
detail.abstract: We examine whether cheaper financing conditions facilitate firms' transition away from carbon-intensive activities and toward sustainable ones, measured by the share of revenue from green activities ("green revenue"). Using a novel revenue-decomposition dataset for Chinese listed firms, we find that lower costs of debt are associated with a higher green-revenue share, with effects concentrated in high-emission (brown) sectors. The association is stronger for smaller firms and for firms with richer ex-ante green technologies. Exploiting policy-induced reductions in borrowing costs, we document a plausibly causal effect of cheaper debt on increases in green revenue. We corroborate these patterns in a global sample. Taken together, the results indicate that financing the transition of brown sectors—by lowering the marginal cost of capital for credible investments—can materially accelerate corporate decarbonization. We discuss implications for emerging transition-finance frame works.

title: On Application of the Cramer-Von Mises Distance for Equivalence Testing
affiliations: ERGO Group AG

detail.title: On Application of the Cramer-Von Mises Distance for Equivalence Testing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: no funder

detail.abstract: We consider an equivalence test for a fully specified continuous distribution on the real line. The equivalence test is a powerful tool to show that observed data are sufficiently close to a given distribution. The test under consideration is based on the time-proven Cramér-von Mises distance. We show that the test is locally asymptotically most powerful. A consistent estimator for the asymptotic variance of the test statistic is provided. The bootstrap percentile-t method is applied to improve the finite sample performance of the equivalence test. A detailed algorithm for the asymptotic and percentile-t tests is given. An extensive simulation study of the finite sample properties is performed. A practical approach to find efficient values of the tolerance parameter is provided.

title: How Do Fintech and Bank Credit Flows Affect Environmental Sustainability? Global evidence from Greenhouse Gas Exposure
affiliations: and University of Melbourne

detail.title: How Do Fintech and Bank Credit Flows Affect Environmental Sustainability? Global evidence from Greenhouse Gas Exposure
detail.abstract: The study examines the effects of fintech and bank credit flows on greenhouse gas (GHG) exposure to 134 countries over the past decades. The study documents the transition to environmentally friendly credit flows, with a predicted decrease in GHG exposure. The impacts of credit flows on environmental sustainability are heterogeneous with variable advanced panel data estimators. The study documents a relatively strong moderation effect of government effectiveness on the long-term relationships between credit flows and environmental sustainability. Unequal contributions of financial innovation to sustainability are presented across income groups and regional economies. With the significant treatment effects of world governance and the Paris Agreement as our international climate action commitment, along with banking systems, Fintech credit flows are critical to mitigate GHG exposure of the global economy as an important factor for growth.

title: Information Asymmetry, Liquidity, and Dark Pool Trading
affiliations: VU University Amsterdam

detail.title: Information Asymmetry, Liquidity, and Dark Pool Trading
detail.abstract: Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) announcements provide a public, high-information setting to study dark market trading under drastic liquidity improvement and a reduction in information asymmetry. On announcement day, quoted and effective spreads drop by 50% or more, depth increases at least fivefold, and volatility falls for target firms in lit markets. Theoretical models do not uniformly predict the relationship between such an information shock and dark market trading. I find that dark market proportion jumps by at least 15% on and after the announcement and mean dark trade size increases. Further, the results are more pronounced in completed and all-cash deals, those types of deals which reduce information asymmetry the most. This paper highlights the connection between information asymmetry and market fragmentation around a major corporate announcement, suggesting that dark market proportion can rise despite deeply liquid lit markets.

title: The Impact of Public Registries on Governance  Structure in Agriculture
affiliations: and Institute of Agricultural Economics, Sofia

detail.title: The Impact of Public Registries on Governance  Structure in Agriculture

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no financial relationships with other persons and organizations, except those described below. The authors declare that they have equal input on the research questions addressed in the study. There is no conflict of interest in the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study does not address questions of a medical nature.
declarations.funderStatement: This study has been funded by the Bulgarian Science Fund, the project “The Mechanisms and the Modes of Agrarian Governance in Bulgaria”, Contract No КП-06-Н56/5 from 11.11.2021. This research was financially supported by the Fruit Growing Institute - Plovdiv, Agricultural Academy, Sofia, Bulgaria.

detail.abstract: New Institutional Economics (NIE) posits that economic system improvement can be achieved through incentives for hybrid contractual organizations. In Bulgaria's agricultural sector, the increasing use of public registries (PRs) and their digital formats reduces information asymmetry, facilitates access to property rights, and lowers social costs. Enhanced governance structures are realized through hybrid contractual forms and property rights protection, enabled by the synergy between electronic and physical transactions. These conditions lead to low asset specificity, reduced uncertainty, and high transaction repeatability, characteristic of contractual alternatives with low transaction costs (TrC). However, the redirection of incentives for property rights acquisition by certain actors, who retain ownership rights, absorb cash flows, and reduce TrC, prevents the hybrid contract from achieving its goal of low social costs. This article aims to compare alternatives and test the hypothesis that hybrid technological contracts, exemplified by PRsin agriculture, result in lower social costs. The methods employed include comparative institutional analysis, discrete structural analysis, and effect analysis. The expected results and conclusions are that the studies are expected to confirm the positive impact of digitalized public registers on the agricultural sector. A concept for improving the institutional environment is proposed.

title: Frontloading Wealth: How Parental Transfers Shape Housing and Savings
affiliations: Maastricht University

detail.title: Frontloading Wealth: How Parental Transfers Shape Housing and Savings
detail.abstract: Parents transfer substantial wealth to their children during their lifetime, yet the timing and consequences of these inter vivos transfers remain poorly understood. I show that most parental transfers occur around first-time home purchases, while transfers are largely unrelated to other life events. Because they are predominantly received by already wealthier children, these transfers increase absolute wealth inequality in the short run. Next, I identify the causal effect of parental home purchase transfers on housing outcomes and subsequent wealth accumulation, exploiting exogenous variation from a Dutch tax-exemption policy. While transfers promote wealth accumulation by enabling homeownership, recipients use them primarily to reduce mortgage debt. As a result, the initial wealth gains dissipate over time, as recipients consume the savings from lower debt service rather than reinvesting them.

title: Talking their Own Book: Brokerage Proprietary Trading and Analyst Bias
affiliations: , Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) - School of Finance and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE)

detail.title: Talking their Own Book: Brokerage Proprietary Trading and Analyst Bias
detail.abstract: We identify a novel conflict of interest for financial analysts arising from brokerage proprietary trading. Using a unique Chinese dataset, we find that analysts issue significantly more optimistic recommendations for stocks held indirectly by their brokerage firms through proprietary investments in mutual funds. Evidence from regulatory sanctions, analyst relocations, and reactions to negative news implies that this bias is driven by strategic incentives to support the firm's proprietary investments. Cross-sectionally, the bias is weaker in the presence of high peer coverage and for analysts with greater reputational capital, but stronger when proprietary trading income is more important. While investors who follow these conflicted recommendations suffer from subsequent stock underperformance, the brokerage itself profits from increased returns on its fund investments. Our findings reveal a subtle but important channel where proprietary interests compromise analyst independence, creating value for the brokerage at the expense of investors.

title: DFAS-AM: The DFAS Analysis Map Manual: A Meta-Scientific Architecture for Ethical-Temporal Interpretation of Global Systems
affiliations: Institute of Certified Public Accountant ( ICPAP)

detail.title: DFAS-AM: The DFAS Analysis Map Manual: A Meta-Scientific Architecture for Ethical-Temporal Interpretation of Global Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research. The DFAS Analysis Map (DFAS-AM) was independently developed as part of the Dynamic Financial Applied Meta-Science (DFAS) doctrine, founded and authored by Hasan Mohamed Husain Alaali. The research represents the author’s original intellectual work, conducted without institutional or corporate influence, and adheres fully to the DFAS-FEP (Future Engine Prototype) Protocol and DFAS-EIR (Editorial Integrity Reporting) standards of ethical authorship and research transparency.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human participants or patient data were involved in this research. The study is conceptual and methodological in nature, involving theoretical model development and applied analytical design. Accordingly, ethical approval was not required, but all procedures and reporting comply with the ethical and integrity standards outlined in DFAS-FEP.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was self-funded and self-conducted under the author’s independent research initiative within the Alaali Financial Models Meta-Framework (AFMF) and the Dynamic Financial Applied Meta-Science (DFAS) discipline.

detail.abstract:
The DFAS Analysis Map (DFAS-AM) establishes a new scientific discipline that interprets global systems through the convergence of ethics, time, and financial behavior.
Unlike traditional analytical schools — Behavioral Economics (Kahneman, 2011), Narrative Economics (Shiller, 2019), or Financial Instability Theory (Minsky, 1992) — (DFAS-AM) does not predict or simulate; it audits the ethical–temporal geometry of civilization itself, mapping how moral liquidity flows through decisions, institutions, and markets.

DFAS-AM is the first applied doctrine that converts ethics and time into quantifiable analytical coordinates, transforming moral and temporal dimensions into measurable scientific variables. It introduces four primary indicators — the Ethical Liquidity Ratio (ELR), Temporal Decision Lag Index (TDLI), Moral Equilibrium Index (MEI), and Cognitive Liquidity Index (CLI) — which collectively bridge moral philosophy, temporal accountability, and financial analytics. The framework employs a reproducible six-step analytical methodology designed for integration with AI-driven systems, public policy evaluation, and institutional governance diagnostics, allowing ethical and temporal assessments to be mapped, replicated, and validated empirically.

This manual codifies DFAS-AM as a living cartography, transforming ethics and time into measurable coordinates that reveal how behavioral energy travels through history, policy, and financial structures.
It constitutes the analytical foundation for DFAS Signals, Ethical Liquidity Analysis, and Behavioral-Financial Integration within the Alaali Financial Models Meta-Framework (AFMF).

title: Intelligent Machines and Incomplete Information
affiliations: Dibrugarh University, Indian Statistical Institute, North East Center and Dibrugarh University

detail.title: Intelligent Machines and Incomplete Information
detail.abstract: We consider a firm that wants to hire two individuals who potentially differ in their efficiency levels and may put in distinct levels of efforts. The firm is not informed about the levels of efficiency of the potential employees a priori. The classical principalagent models assume that employees know their efficiency levels. Hence, these models design incentive-compatible mechanisms. We do not assume that employees know how efficient they are. Instead, we assume that the production technology of the firm is intelligent, and the machine-output reveals the efficiency levels of the employees. We call such a production technology to be an intelligent machine. The machine is modeled as a game in characteristic form, and thus the payoffs of the employees are determined by the Shapley shares and the costs of effort. Thus, we embed a cooperative game in a non-cooperative game of incomplete information and contribute to the literature on cooperative games under uncertainty. A characterization of ex-ante Nash equilibrium is established. We discuss our notion of an intelligent machine in the context of explainable artificial intelligence in Remark 2.

title: Art as Data in Political History
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

detail.title: Art as Data in Political History
detail.abstract: Ongoing advances in machine learning are expanding opportunities to analyze large-scale visual data. In historical political economy, paintings from museums and private collections represent an untapped source of information. Before computational methods can be applied, however, it is essential to establish a framework for assessing what information paintings encode and under what assumptions it can be interpreted. This article develops such a framework, drawing on the enduring concerns of the traditional humanities. I describe three applications using a database of 25,000 European paintings from 1000CE to the First World War. Each application targets a distinct type of information conveyed in paintings (depicted content, communicative intent, and incidental information) and a cultural transformation of the early-modern period. The first revisits the notion of a European “civilizing process”---the internalization of stricter norms of behavior that occurred in tandem with the growth of state power---by examining whether paintings of meals show increasingly complex etiquette. The second analyzes portraits to study how political elites shaped their public image, highlighting a long-term shift from chivalric to more rational-bureaucratic representations of men. The third documents a long-term process of secularization, measured by the share of religious paintings, which began prior to the Reformation and accelerated afterward.

title: Failures of Humanitarian Actors in Mitigating the Human Rights Abuses in Myanmar

detail.title: Failures of Humanitarian Actors in Mitigating the Human Rights Abuses in Myanmar
detail.abstract: The humanitarian crisis in Myanmar has emerged as one of the most complex and persistent tragedies of the twenty-first century, shaped by a long history of ethnic persecution, authoritarian governance, and aggravated by the 2021 military coup. Central to this crisis is the plight of the Rohingya, a stateless minority who have endured decades of systemic discrimination, culminating in the 2017 "clearance operations" that forced more than 700,000 people into Bangladesh and were described by the United Nations as a "textbook example of ethnic cleansing." Beyond the Rohingya, the coup reignited conflict across ethnic states, displacing millions and collapsing healthcare, education, and livelihoods, leaving nearly 17 million in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. Despite the scale of suffering, the response of the international community and humanitarian organisations has been widely criticised as inadequate, fragmented, and politically constrained. Geopolitical rivalries have paralysed the United Nations, ASEAN remains bound by its principle of non-interference, and international NGOs face operational barriers ranging from limited access to donor fatigue and coordination failures. As a result, humanitarian engagement has often produced symbolic gestures rather than sustainable solutions, fostering cycles of dependency rather than resilience. This paper therefore explores the magnitude and nature of the crisis, interrogates the failures of humanitarian actors and the international community, and analyses the structural, political, and operational challenges that undermine effective responses. Ultimately, it argues for a rethinking of humanitarian mandates towards rights-based, locally grounded, and justice-oriented approaches that can restore dignity, agency, and long-term resilience for Myanmar's affected populations.

title: A New Measure for Investors' Private Information
affiliations: Aston University, Aston Business School and University of York - The York Management School

detail.title: A New Measure for Investors' Private Information
detail.abstract: We develop a new measure for investors' private information (SDPIN) embedded in a stock price. Unlike existing measures such as PIN and DPIN, it considers both trade order size and trade frequency; we argue that private information can also be revealed through trade order size, thereby applying to a broader range of stock trading scenarios. We test the accuracy of our new private information measure against PIN and DPIN and find it to be more precise. Consequenlty, it reduces information asymmetries among investors and helps managers better assess the private information reflected in their firms' stock prices, enabling them to make more informed (optimal) decisions.

title: GREAT EX-SPAC-TATIONS: The role of the Regulation A+ in SPAC Activity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, and The University of Sydney - Discipline of Finance

detail.title: GREAT EX-SPAC-TATIONS: The role of the Regulation A+ in SPAC Activity
detail.abstract: In 2020, SPAC IPOs comprised 54% of all IPOs, up from under 5% before 2015. We test whether Regulation A+ (Reg A+) helps explain this surge despite SPACs' historical underperformance. Using a quasi-experimental difference-indifferences design centered on the June 19, 2015 Reg A+ implementation as an exogenous shock, we find that Reg A+ spurred an average increase of 43 SPAC IPOs per quarter and $9.6 billion in quarterly proceeds. Sponsor compensation is tied to deal completion rather than deal performance, and post-Reg A+ SPAC quality declines: first-day returns fall by 6.6%, and average Tobin's Q drops by 1.29. These results indicate that Reg A+ amplified activity while worsening incentive misalignment between sponsors and long-horizon shareholders. Our findings provide a sponsor-based explanation for the rise in SPAC issuance and show that, on average, the ensuing acquisitions are value-destroying, consistent with pressures to complete deals within fixed timelines.

title: Administrative Obstruction in European Union Medical Education: Systematic Discrimination and Administrative Failures in the EU Medical Program -A Legal Case Study from Semmelweis University VI
affiliations: Semmelweis University

detail.title: Administrative Obstruction in European Union Medical Education: Systematic Discrimination and Administrative Failures in the EU Medical Program -A Legal Case Study from Semmelweis University VI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal, financial, or organizational conflicts of interest related to the preparation, authorship, or publication of this manuscript. The research, analysis, and documentation presented in this work were conducted independently, without external sponsorship, institutional influence, or third-party involvement. All interpretations, conclusions, and assessments reflect my own academic judgment and are not shaped by any funding source, private organization, or individual.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was conducted independently without any financial support or external sponsorship. No institution or organization provided funding, resources, or incentives for this research.

detail.abstract: This legal case study offers the most comprehensive analysis to date of systemic discrimination and administrative obstruction in Hungary's English-language medical education system. Focusing on Semmelweis University and referencing documentary evidence from Ombudsman Case EBF-AJBH-309-2025, Administrative Court Case 7. Kpk.. 750.239/2025/2, NAIH Data-Protection Case J-427-3/2025, and extensive institutional correspondence, the study shows that international FM/CV-registered students were denied compulsory anatomy practical based on unwritten, external requirements that directly contradict Semmelweis University's Study and Examination Regulations (Articles 5, 10, 11, 13, 29, 45). Evidence from works such as Administrative Obstruction in EU Medical Education, Denied Access to the Scalpel for Dissecting the Specimen, Ghost Students: The Legal Fiction of FM and CV Status, and the Cross-Border Acknowledgment series confirms that inconsistent enforcement, signature-revocation demands, and discriminatory access restrictions form a recurring administrative pattern rather than isolated errors.

title: Decision Flexibility, Not Information Feedback, Explains Myopic Loss Aversion
affiliations: University of Innsbruck - Department of Banking and Finance,  and Radboud University, Institute for Management Research

detail.title: Decision Flexibility, Not Information Feedback, Explains Myopic Loss Aversion

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval given by University of Zurich

detail.abstract: Myopic loss aversion (MLA)-the tendency to avoid risk when investment outcomes are evaluated frequently-has long been cited as a key behavioral explanation for overly conservative portfolios. However, importantly it has remained unclear whether MLA is primarily driven by the frequency of performance feedback or by the flexibility to revise investment decisions (i.e., the decision frequency). Previous studies have yielded mixed evidence. To address this, we conducted two studies; each independently manipulating feedback and decision frequency, featuring substantially higher statistical power than previous research. Our results indicate that MLA is driven by decision rather than feedback frequency. These results refine the theoretical foundations of MLA, with implications for the design of investment interfaces, behavioral finance, and policy interventions aimed at improving long-term investment outcomes.

title: Political Polarization and Stock Market Expectations
affiliations: , , University of Arizona, Eller College of Management, Department of Finance, Students and Colorado State University, Fort Collins - Department of Finance & Real Estate

detail.title: Political Polarization and Stock Market Expectations
detail.abstract: Political polarization explains much of the heterogeneity in how individuals' perceptions of the distribution of stock returns evolve over time. Individuals are more optimistic when "their" party occupies the White House and are more pessimistic when the "other" party takes office. Polarization influences perceptions of near-term returns, long-term returns, and tail returns. Polarization has explanatory power beyond party, vote choice, or political ideology alone. The effect is particularly pronounced for Republicans and has grown over time-by 2025, a one-standard deviation shift in polarization has a greater effect size than a five-standard deviation shift in income.

title: Digital Financial Inclusion and Financial Performance of Selected Money Deposit Banks in Nigeria
affiliations: Lead City University - Department of Management and Accounting, Lead City University and Lead City University, Ibadan. Nigeria

detail.title: Digital Financial Inclusion and Financial Performance of Selected Money Deposit Banks in Nigeria
detail.abstract: The relaunch of Digital Financial inclusion in 2012 by the central bank of Nigeria has made Nigerian banks to embrace several innovative ideas towards providing better quality services to their customers. These innovations are expected to impact on the performance of the banks as suggested by theoretical literature. This study is therefore conducted to provide some empirical explanation on the impact of Digital Financial inclusion instruments on performance of Nigerian banks. Data were collected from World Bank database, Central Bank of Nigeria Statistical Bulletin, and annual reports of deposit money banks. The data were analysed with Fixed Effect Regression Model. The Regression analysis was conducted after conducting the Breusch-Pagan Lagragian Multiplier (BP-LM) test to determine the suitability of either the fixed effect or random effect model. The findings revealed positive and significant impact of Automated Teller Machines, Bank embranchment, and point of sale terminals on bank performance at both 1% and 5% levels of significance. However, the result on the number of bank account is not significant. The study concludes that improvement in the quality of financial services will attract more customers to the bank and boost their performance. It is thus recommended that more ATMs, POS and Branches be put in place for better inclusive finance.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility Reporting Reforms around the World: Evidence on Firm Value and Externalities
affiliations: The University of Western Australia - Department of Accounting and Finance, Students, Australian National University - Research School of Accounting, Xiamen University - Accounting Department and Zhejiang University - School of Management

detail.title: Corporate Social Responsibility Reporting Reforms around the World: Evidence on Firm Value and Externalities
detail.abstract: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) reporting reforms are increasingly adopted worldwide, yet their implications for firm value and externalities remain unclear. Using a novel handcollected dataset of global CSR reporting reforms and a stacked difference-indifferences design, we find that treated firms experience a 9.25% decline in firm value but a 16.4% reduction in CO₂ and CO₂ equivalents emissions and a 10.27% increase in CSR ratings. Effects are stronger under reforms requiring greenhouse gas disclosures, lacking safe harbor provisions, not recommending a specific reporting framework, or not mandating external assurance. Stronger changes also emerge in jurisdictions with weaker stakeholder orientation and more developed market institutions, and among firms without CSR-contingent executive compensation and those with weaker CSR transparency and performance. At the country-level, reform jurisdictions reduce emissions by 40.75 million metric tons, yielding societal savings of $7.5 billion. Overall, CSR reporting reforms reduce firm value, but generate significant societal and environmental benefits.

title: Special Economic Zones: the Chinese Ladder to Get into Neoliberal Globalization
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Colombia

detail.title: Special Economic Zones: the Chinese Ladder to Get into Neoliberal Globalization
detail.abstract: This paper explored how the neoliberalism influenced the formulation, adoption, and implementation of the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in China. In grappling with this question, a significant link was found: globalization. This process was driven by openness and liberalization, premises that neoliberalism revived in the global political sphere in the last decades of the 20th century. Then, to get into the world economy, China abandoned the protectionist ladder to take an additional one: formulate and adopt SEZs. These zones allowed China to have free trade policies without internal market liberalization. Furthermore, the implementation of SEZs as cities generated direct access to the neoliberal model of globalization.

title: Regulatory responses to the financial stability implications of stablecoins
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Regulatory responses to the financial stability implications of stablecoins
detail.abstract: In essence, stablecoins are electronic money issued by a narrow balance sheet vehicle into a distributed ledger (or a "programmable platform"). Many believe that they will have significant success as new form of money. Members of the current US administration expect that US stablecoins would circulate globally and support demand for treasuries and the international role of the USD. Related to the latter, recent industry initiatives plan to rely on US stablecoins as settlement asset for cross border payments ("stablecoin sandwich"). We review the implications of large global stablecoins on the financial system and discuss financial stability risks and remedies. We compare regulatory approaches across some jurisdictions and note that different directions have been taken, although all authorities seem to agree that stablecoins must not be remunerated. We discuss additional ideas how to address the risks associated with successful stablecoins, propose some basic regulatory principles and note that prohibiting the remuneration of stablecoins is not necessarily fostering financial stability. We suggest three regulatory options fulfilling the proposed regulatory principles.

title: Between Nothing and Everything: The Cosmic Equilibrium and Its Interdisciplinary Insights
affiliations: National Stock Exchange of India

detail.title: Between Nothing and Everything: The Cosmic Equilibrium and Its Interdisciplinary Insights
detail.abstract: This article presents the Unified Continuous Self-Balance Universe Hypothesis, a novel cosmological model that posits the universe as a dynamic, self-regulating system. Unlike classical finite-start or infinite-steady frameworks, incorporating multiscale feedback integration, this hypothesis maintains that the universe preserves equilibrium through sophisticated feedback mechanisms. Here, the Big Bang is reinterpreted as a critical phase within an ongoing self-balancing process, supported by empirical observations like the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The existence of universe is defined as a result of automatic equilibrium between "absolute nothingness"—a state absent of space, time, matter, or energy—and "unbounded infinity"—a limitless expanse of chaotic potential. Mathematically, the state of the universe, denoted by 𝐔, satisfies 𝟎 < 𝐔 < ∞, indicating it is always positive and finite. More specifically, within this framework, the time-dependent state U(t) satisfies 0a < U(t) < ∞u for all time t , where 0a represents absolute nothingness (denoted with subscript 'a' for absolute, a state devoid of space, time, matter, or energy) and ∞u represents unbounded infinity (denoted with subscript 'u' for unbounded, a limitless expanse of chaotic potential), emphasizing the universe's continuous evolution within these conceptual bounds. The universe evolves continuously between absolute nothingness (0a) and unbounded infinity (∞u), always remaining strictly within these bounds (0a < U(t) < ∞u for all t), ensuring the universe will not collapse into nothingness nor reach unbounded infinity; even in scenarios of eternal expansion leading to dilution toward emptiness, feedback mechanisms ensure no violation by regulating dynamics to prevent such dilution, converging to equilibrium Ueq. As time progresses, the universe's state converges to a unique equilibrium Ueq , expressed mathematically as limt→∞U(t) = Ueq, with 0a < Ueq < ∞u. This convergence signifies that all emergent possibilities (the bounds between absolute nothingness, 0a, and unbounded infinity, ∞u), are resolved by the automatic equilibrium, leaving only the universe itself as the final, self-contained reality. The model links to observable phenomena, including the CMB and dark energy, while extending its principles to interdisciplinary applications in fields such as ecology (e.g., ecological balance), economics (e.g., economic stability), artificial intelligence (AI), and artificial superintelligence (ASI) (e.g., optimization algorithms). Human talent optimization and exploration (e.g., feedback-driven skill development), and multiverse theories proposing cosmic equilibrium across multiple realities. Though partly speculative, this framework offers a testable and transformative perspective on cosmic evolution.

title: Do Global Board Reforms Encourage Voluntary Delistings?
affiliations: Lehigh University - College of Business, , Alfaisal University and University of South Carolina - Moore School of Business

detail.title: Do Global Board Reforms Encourage Voluntary Delistings?
detail.abstract: We examine how global board reforms affect corporate decisions to voluntarily delist from public stock exchanges. Combining Azevedo et al.'s (2024) delisting model with Fauver et al.'s (2017) quasi-natural experiment setting, we analyze the impact of regulatory costs and expropriation penalties on delisting decisions. Contrary to prior evidence of positive reform outcomes, we find a significant increase in voluntary delistings. Further analyses show this increase results from an increase in the expropriation penalty. Our study suggests that global board reforms increase the expropriation penalty sufficiently that poorly managed, weakly governed firms choose to withdraw from public scrutiny.

title: The New Dark Age: Modern Academic Publishing as the Most Autocratic Censorship Era in Scientific History
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The New Dark Age: Modern Academic Publishing as the Most Autocratic Censorship Era in Scientific History
detail.abstract: This article argues that contemporary academic publishing represents the most autocratic censorship regime in the history of science, paralleling and potentially exceeding the intellectual repression of the medieval period. While medieval despotism suppressed human freedom through political and religious authority, modern academic institutions suppress scientific truth through sophisticated gatekeeping mechanisms that systematically protect erroneous mainstream theories while excluding corrective research. We document five critical dimensions of this new dark age: (1) unprecedented proliferation of garbage and erroneous articles in mainstream journals; (2) complete absence of error-correction mechanisms despite 90-95% error rates; (3) multi-layered institutional protection systems for academic authorities and erroneous paradigms; (4) systematic suppression of correct theories through coordinated rejection across journals, preprint platforms, and even AI training datasets; and (5) elimination of historical vindication opportunities that previously allowed minority correct viewpoints to eventually triumph. The analysis reveals that modern academic censorship has achieved what medieval authorities could only dream of: creating self-perpetuating systems where errors multiply exponentially, corrections face insurmountable barriers, and even artificial intelligence inherits and amplifies institutional biases. Unlike Newton's era when correct theories could achieve posthumous recognition, contemporary minority correct viewpoints face permanent burial under mountains of mainstream garbage, creating a dark age from which escape may prove impossible without fundamental systemic revolution.

title: Colonial state and Muslim institutions: history of regulatory endowment) in British India
affiliations: University of Oxford - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Colonial state and Muslim institutions: history of regulatory endowment) in British India
detail.abstract:
From the perspective of English law, a typical waqf appeared to be a curious mixture of paradoxical features—combining elements of both the religious and the secular, and the public and the private. Lawyers and judges often struggled to determine whether a waqf should be classified as a religious or a secular institution, or as a public or a private trust. This question lay at the heart of debates over how such endowments should be regulated by the state.

Because vast tracts of land were dedicated as waqf, the East India Company could not overlook their significance. After the Company assumed full charge as diwan (tax collector) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, it initiated a series of resumption proceedings—that is, efforts to recover lands that had been granted as rent-free holdings. These included a large number of waqf properties that the colonial authorities sought to bring under fiscal control.

title: Independent Director-Affiliated Donations and Stock Price Crash Risk
affiliations: Xiamen University, Hunan University of Technology and Business, Xiamen University and Providence College - School of Business

detail.title: Independent Director-Affiliated Donations and Stock Price Crash Risk
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether and how independent director-affiliated corporate donations affect stock price crash risk in China. We find a significant positive relationship between affiliated donations and future crash risk. The relationship is more significant for firms with weak internal governance and limited external monitoring, when affiliated directors serve on the audit committee, and in non-state-owned enterprises. Overall, our findings suggest that the social ties built through affiliated donations undermine rather than enhance director monitoring, and that agency theory has more explanatory power than resource dependence theory for understanding the impact of affiliated donations on stock price crash risk.

title: W.H. Hutt's Analysis of Nazi Economics: "The Economic Strength of Dictatorships" (1939) and "Economic Lessons from the German Offensive" (1940)

detail.title: W.H. Hutt's Analysis of Nazi Economics: "The Economic Strength of Dictatorships" (1939) and "Economic Lessons from the German Offensive" (1940)
detail.abstract: This paper reproduces and contextualizes two unpublished lectures by the South African economist W.H. Hutt from 1939 and 1940 in which Hutt analyzes the economic policy of Nazi Germany. Hutt argued that the Nazis' early success in the war was attributable to their policy of eliminating anti-competitive restrictions on production by labor unions and capitalists. He believed that this provided a model for the Allies to emulate. This analysis of Nazi economic policy was far too generous to the Nazis in its depiction of Hitler as an advocate for ordinary workers and an enemy of monopoly capital. It also broke from the assessments of Hutt's fellow neoliberal economists-the German Ordoliberals and Austrian economists, such as Friedrich Hayek and Ludwig von Mises-who classified the Nazis as socialists and collectivists. Hutt's analysis of Nazi economic policy in 1939 and 1940 contributes to and complicates our understanding of neoliberal economists' recurring fascination with the possibility of a 'liberal dictator.'

title: Broken IPOs
affiliations: Miami University

detail.title: Broken IPOs
detail.abstract: This study examines the prevalence, determinants, and consequences of "broken" initial public offerings-IPOs that trade below their offer price in the secondary market. Broken IPOs are common, between 1990 and 2022, nearly one-third of U.S. IPOs trade below their offer price after one month, and nearly one-half do so after one year, with average price declines of 15.0% and 43.7%, respectively. The likelihood and timing of broken IPOs are related to firm, issue, and market characteristics, many of which reflect elevated uncertainty and information asymmetry. The implications are significant, as firms with broken IPOs suffer from limited post-IPO attention, encounter tighter external financing constraints, and face a greater risk of delisting from the stock market due to bankruptcy or liquidation than do other IPO firms.

title: Bootstrapping under Imperfect Knowledge of Data: An Integrated Approach for Performance Assessment Using Composite Indicators
affiliations: Instituto Superior Técnico (IST), University of Lisbon, University of Catania - Department of Economics and Business and Instituto Superior Técnico (IST)

detail.title: Bootstrapping under Imperfect Knowledge of Data: An Integrated Approach for Performance Assessment Using Composite Indicators
detail.abstract: This study proposes a novel integrated methodology for performance assessment through composite indicators, capable of addressing multiple sources of imperfect knowledge of data and incorporating expert input. Performance and efficiency assessment techniques, particularly nonparametric methods such as Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), are highly sensitive to data quality. Although the proposed framework is applicable to DEA in general, for clarity and without loss of generality, this study focuses on the Benefit-of-the-Doubt (BoD) formulation. Building on the BoD approach, a DEA-based optimization method used for constructing composite indicators through entity-specific weights, we introduce for the first time a Bootstrap BoD framework. This approach brings statistical inference and bias correction into the BoD methodology, which until now lacked robustness tools. To overcome Bootstrap's known limitations, particularly its sensitivity to the original sample and its tendency to generate unrealistic resamples, we integrate it with the Hit-and-Run (H&R) procedure. H&R serves as a preprocessing step, capturing structural uncertainty by modelling and populating the feasible space for each entity. Bootstrap is then applied as a postprocessing tool, introducing stochastic perturbations to the frontier and correcting for bias. Results show that this dual-layered methodology significantly enhances the robustness and reliability of performance and efficiency assessments by combining the complementary strengths of both methods, performing better than classical BoD. This approach is capable of replacing current composite indicators methodologies as it is more complete, or at the very least capable of replicating them.

title: Can International Income Transfers Reduce the Use of Child Labor?
affiliations: Central Michigan University

detail.title: Can International Income Transfers Reduce the Use of Child Labor?

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper shows how a policy of income transfer, such as remittance payments from a developed country, can reduce child labor, a target for the UN Sustainable Development Goals, by turning the terms of trade in favor of the transfer-receiving country. This is a novel policy measure because it utilizes an existing international economic event, known as income transfer, without imposing a significant financial burden on national governments. This reduces inequities in the global labor market without creating economic and non-economic turmoil resulting from policies involving bans or other alternatives to bans.

title: AI4Policy: AI-Enabled Scenario Planning for Policy-Making in the Age of AI
affiliations: Equiano Institute and Unaffiliated Author

detail.title: AI4Policy: AI-Enabled Scenario Planning for Policy-Making in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: AI-enabled scenario planning (AIESP) promises to compress policy-analysis cycles from months to days, yet the same generative systems also introduce novel epistemic vulnerabilities: synthetic evidence floods, adversarial prompt injection, model-drift lobbying, and runaway feedback loops between generated narratives and data-collection priorities. We integrate recent advances in generative modelling, multi-agent wargaming and metascience retrieval into a single governance pipeline that is self-diagnostic-i.e., it continuously audits its own epistemic reliability. Our three contributions are: (1) Planning-a Bayesian scenario generator that treats LLM outputs as noisy priors and corrects for semantic data poisoning; (2) Synthesis-a metascience retrieval engine that surfaces "counter-evidence" embeddings to mitigate confirmation bias; (3) Generation-a constitutionalpolicy drafter with rollback tokens that can retract clauses when downstream audits detect inconsistency. We validate the system on a live case-UK policies retrofitting for generative foundation models-and show a reduction in epistemic error rate versus human-only panels, while flagging six intervention points that were invisible to legacy impact-assessment workflows.

title: Bullish Minting: An Adaptive Control Framework for Token Issuance
affiliations: Kosmos Ventures and Kosmos Ventures

detail.title: Bullish Minting: An Adaptive Control Framework for Token Issuance
detail.abstract: We propose Bullish Minting, a dynamic framework for adaptive, goal-oriented token issuance. Inspired by modern monetary policy, the mechanism endogenizes the token emission rate through measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and adjusts supply according to network performance. The model formalizes the token economy as a bounded feedback-control system: the emission rate responds to KPI deviations via a weighted distance metric and decays through a timedependent sigmoid representing adoption and maturation. Targets themselves evolve according to an Additive-Increase/Multiplicative-Decrease (AIMD) rule, endogenizing the trajectory of network goals. We provide stability results under mild regularity conditions, a welfare interpretation as discounted loss minimization subject to a dynamic supply constraint, and comparative statics of policy elasticities. We outline empirical calibration and implementation considerations and propose a simulation protocol for quantitative evaluation.

title: Blockchain and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Bibliometric Analysis and Research Agenda
affiliations: Blockchain Research Lab, Blockchain Research Lab and Blockchain Research Lab

detail.title: Blockchain and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Bibliometric Analysis and Research Agenda

declarations.funderStatement: The study was conducted as part of the research project AVIK (acronym; engl.: automated ground-air intercommunication in mobility for enhancing interaction and collaboration) which focuses on automating and enhancing the interconnectedness of different vehicles and mobility actors (e.g. UAVs and cars) in the context of data transmission, harmonization, aggregation and monetization. The project is funded by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) under the conditions of the mFUND program (FKZ: 19F2227A). Consortium partners of AVIK comprise ASINCO GmbH (Consortium leader), Technische Hochschule Wildau, Werner Turck GmbH & Co. KG, and Blockchain Research Lab gGmbH.

detail.abstract: The convergence of blockchain technology and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has garnered significant attention due to its potential to enhance security, automation, and data management in UAV ecosystems. However, the ongoing growth of research in this domain necessitates a systematic analysis to delineate its intellectual structure and development trajectories. This study employs bibliometric techniques, specifically co-citation analysis and exploratory factor analysis (EFA), to identify and analyze key research streams at the intersection of blockchain and UAV technologies. Based on a dataset of 340 peer-reviewed publications retrieved from Web of Science, the analysis reveals six distinct research streams: (I) privacy and security in the Internet of Drones (IoD), (II) implications of combining emerging technologies, (III) federated learning, (IV) resource and data management in IoT, (V) optimization, security, and applications in UAV-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) systems, and (VI) blockchain-enabled data sharing and automation in the IoD. These findings highlight blockchain's role in securing UAV communication, optimizing resource management, and enabling decentralized automation. Despite these advancements, challenges related to scalability, computational efficiency, and interoperability persist, with limited empirical validation of proposed frameworks. This study provides a structured overview of the evolving research landscape, offering insights for future investigations and interdisciplinary collaborations aimed at addressing these challenges. Building on the identified research streams, this study proposes a research agenda that highlights unresolved challenges and critical gaps-such as lightweight consensus protocols, privacypreserving federated learning, efficient resource allocation, and integration with emerging technologies-thereby advancing the secure and efficient integration of blockchain and UAV technologies across diverse applications.

title: The Developmental State and the Constitutional Economy
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: The Developmental State and the Constitutional Economy
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the institutional and constitutional foundations of the developmental state in Colombia, using Joseph Stiglitz's analytical framework on market failures and the role of the state in creating equitable and sustainable development. The study focuses on Title V of the 1991 Political Constitution, "On the Organization of the State," to examine whether its articles establish the necessary normative and institutional conditions to correct market failures, balance economic efficiency and social justice, and build a hard (physical) and soft (educational, cognitive, and financial) infrastructure that enables sustained and equitable growth. Preliminary results indicate that the 1991 Constitution conceives of the state as an active agent that not only regulates markets but also guides and creates them, fostering social mobility, competitiveness, and redistribution. The article concludes that the Colombian constitutional order contains the foundations of a developmental state, although its effective implementation requires a more coherent, deliberative, and distributive institutional architecture.

title: Implementation Of Social and Economic Intervention Policies to Promote Financial Inclusion and Alleviate Poverty in the Coastal Zone of Ghana
affiliations: University of Buckingham

detail.title: Implementation Of Social and Economic Intervention Policies to Promote Financial Inclusion and Alleviate Poverty in the Coastal Zone of Ghana
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the design and impact of social and economic intervention policies aimed at expanding financial inclusion and reducing poverty in Ghana's coastal zones, highlighting policy mechanisms, implementation challenges, and potential outcomes for households and small enterprises. This study thus contributes to the policy discourse by examining how targeted interventions such as microcredit support, savings mobilization, credit facilities for small and medium enterprises, and social safety nets can be designed to maximize uptake, ensure financial literacy, and promote sustainable livelihoods in coastal communities. This study thus contributes to the policy discourse by examining how targeted interventions such as microcredit support, savings mobilization, credit facilities for small and medium enterprises, and social safety nets can be designed to maximize uptake, ensure financial literacy, and promote sustainable livelihoods in coastal communities. Building on this framework, the analysis synthesizes empirical evidence from coastal Ghana to identify the mechanisms through which financial access translates into poverty reduction, resilience against climate and economic shocks, and inclusive growth in the region. By examining credit access, savings behavior, and the role of microfinance, the study underscores how expanded financial services can foster entrepreneurial activity, diversify income, and enhance household resilience to climaterelated disruptions in coastal communities.

title: On Significant Misunderstandings in Macroeconomics
affiliations: Doshisha University - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: On Significant Misunderstandings in Macroeconomics
detail.abstract:
I present arguments on significant misunderstandings in macroeconomics about relationship between investment and savings. I will show that investment and savings are undertaken by the same economic agent. 
To summarize the meaning of Investment = Savings most simply, (setting aside the government and overseas factors) since savings are defined as income minus consumption, spending money on consumption increases the recipient's income without changing savings. Spending money on investment also increases the recipient's income, but since it's not consumption, the “minus consumption” component doesn't occur, so savings increase. Therefore, investment equals savings. The intermediary function of banks has nothing to do with it.
 Excluding the government and overseas sectors, total financial assets amount to zero. Therefore, savings in the equation investment = savings do not represent the accumulation of financial assets. Instead, investment represents the accumulation of fixed assets. Consequently, this savings also constitutes an increase in fixed assets. 
 Both investment and savings involve spending money to purchase goods. Defining savings as income minus consumption minus investment yields
savings = fiscal deficit plus current account surplus.
This correctly represents changes in financial assets.

title: Narrative, Flows, and Concentration: Why the Contemporary AI Equity Surge Warrants Bubble Concern
affiliations: Bronx Small Business Development Center (SBDC)

detail.title: Narrative, Flows, and Concentration: Why the Contemporary AI Equity Surge Warrants Bubble Concern
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the surge in artificial intelligence (AI)-themed equities and investment vehicles exhibits classic bubble signatures, including pervasive narrative contagion, flow-driven price dynamics, elevated valuation multiples, and extreme performance concentration. Drawing on frameworks from narrative economics (Shiller, 2019) and a comparative analysis with the 2020–21 Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) boom (Klausner et al., 2020, Saul 2022), this study integrates quantitative data on valuation ratios, Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) flows, and asset concentration. Empirical evidence indicates a market susceptible to correction unless realized earnings growth aligns with heightened investor expectations. This analysis provides a structured, evidence-based assessment of the AI equity market, concluding that its structural trends justify significant bubble concern.

title: The Amateur's Curse of Positive Income Shocks *
affiliations: University of Mannheim - Center for Doctoral Studies in Economics and Management (CDSEM)

detail.title: The Amateur's Curse of Positive Income Shocks *
detail.abstract: How do soccer clubs react to positive income shocks? Exploiting quasi-random variation induced by penalty shootouts in Verbandspokal finals, a German amateur tournament, we find that clubs receiving a positive income shock are unable to improve their final league position in the following years. Even more surprising, these teams start to significantly underperform three years and onwards after the income shock. We observe an associated increase in insolvency proceedings, indicating financial struggles after the Verbandspokal final. We identify a causal link to longer managerial tenure, which suggests the emergence of a bias in the decision-making process regarding whether or not to appoint a new team manager. The long-run decline in club performance also carries political externalities, as the majority party in the municipal council of the club's municipality significantly underperforms in subsequent elections.

title: Human Capital Assessment via Large Language Models alignment
affiliations: Amundi Institute, Amundi Institute, Amundi Asset Management, Amundi Institute, University of Paris-Saclay and Amundi Asset Management

detail.title: Human Capital Assessment via Large Language Models alignment
detail.abstract: This study presents a new methodological framework that combines clustering techniques with large language models (LLMs) to analyze intangible assets in various fields of research. By applying this approach to human capital, we reveal that its definition and perception vary considerably from one region to another and evolve over time, reflecting differences in socioeconomic development, institutional frameworks, and geopolitical contexts. Our financial analysis confirms that these regional variations in the perception of human capital have important implications for investment performance. Specifically, strategies that incorporate human capital development scores generate significantly different returns in emerging markets compared to developed markets, highlighting the importance of tailored portfolio approaches. Furthermore, our asset valuation results highlight the central role of human capital development in explaining emerging market dynamics, particularly during periods of geopolitical turmoil, when companies with stronger human capital demonstrate greater resilience and stability.

title: What is the Interest Rate Pass-Through under Surplus Liquidity in the Banking Sector?
affiliations: and University American College Skopje (UACS)

detail.title: What is the Interest Rate Pass-Through under Surplus Liquidity in the Banking Sector?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors declare that no funds, grants, or other support were received during the preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the interest rate pass-through in an economy with structurally high banking sector liquidity, using North Macedonia as a case study. Persistent surplus liquidity limits commercial banks' reliance on central bank and interbank funding, potentially weakening the transmission of monetary policy. Employing a dynamic autoregressive distributed lag and error-correction (ARDL/ECM) framework augmented with a liquidity variable, we estimate the two stages of the transmission process-from the policy rate to the interbank rate, and from the interbank to lending rates. The results show that high liquidity dampens both the strength and speed of pass-through by reducing interbank rate responsiveness and moderating lending rate adjustments. These findings suggest that in banking systems with structural liquidity surpluses, conventional interest rate policy may be insufficient, underscoring the need for complementary instruments to enhance monetary transmission effectiveness.

title: Inferential Theory for Pricing Errors with Latent Factors and Firm Characteristics
affiliations: and Columbia University

detail.title: Inferential Theory for Pricing Errors with Latent Factors and Firm Characteristics

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by NSF Grant DMS-2052955.

detail.abstract: We study factor models that combine latent factors with firm characteristics and propose a new framework for modeling, estimating, and inferring pricing errors. Following Zhang (2024), our approach decomposes mispricing into two distinct components: inside alpha, explained by firm characteristics but orthogonal to factor exposures, and outside alpha, orthogonal to both factors and characteristics. Our model generalizes those developed recently such as Kelly et al. (2019) and Zhang (2024), resolving issues of orthogonality, basis dependence, and unit sensitivity. Methodologically, we develop estimators grounded in low-rank methods with explicit debiasing, providing closed-form solutions and a rigorous inferential theory that accommodates a growing number of characteristics and relaxes standard assumptions on sample dimensions. Empirically, using U.S. stock returns from 2000-2019, we document strong evidence of both inside and outside alphas, with the former showing industry-level comovements and the latter reflecting idiosyncratic shocks beyond firm fundamentals. Our framework thus unifies statistical and characteristic-based approaches to factor modeling, offering both theoretical advances and new insights into the structure of pricing errors.

title: A Cold Stop: Temperature, Unemployment and Joblessness Dynamics
affiliations: School of Global Policy and Strategy, Universite du Luxembourg - Department of Economics, Columbia University and Lund University

detail.title: A Cold Stop: Temperature, Unemployment and Joblessness Dynamics

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We provide new evidence that short-run temperature shocks affect unemployment dynamics. Linking daily weather data with three decades of Current Population Survey microdata, we show that cold, but not hot, temperatures significantly increase unemployment risk.
